532772|2026-09.headline: DCB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 29% YoY to INR 236 crore, a record, with ROA 1.03% and ROE 14.6%, while NIM slipped on surplus liquidity.
532772|2026-09.overview: Advances grew 21% YoY and deposits 19%, with net interest income up 17% and revenue up 21%. Cost to income fell to 59.64%, an 18-quarter low, and cost to average assets was 2.47%. Asset quality improved: GNPA 2.29%, NNPA 0.73% (both 23-quarter lows), PCR 81.38%, and credit cost 0.28%. NIM declined QoQ because the bank carried surplus liquidity from a $194 million FCNR(B) raise, which management expects to reverse from Q3 as repo-linked loans reprice.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY; highest ever quarterly, fifth consecutive record

financial_highlights.value: 19% YoY (18.6% per management on Q2 basis)

financial_highlights.change: Core fee income described as strong
+7.23 pp YoY; ex technical write-off 68.75%, +9.6 pp

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: About 23% of total assets, with ~INR 14,000 crore book and NPA of INR 26 crore; management is comfortable taking share to 25% but not beyond. Roughly 30% organic and 70% inorganic (co-lending and DA).

segments.name: Mortgages / LAP
segments.commentary: Incremental mix about 70:30 home loan to LAP (71:29 per management). Balance transfers from NBFCs are a target segment, priced without rate cuts; mortgage growth was described as muted so far and expected to pick up.

segments.name: Corporate / NBFC lending
segments.commentary: Corporate is about 8% of the asset book, mostly NBFC exposure via co-lending and DA; management sees it rising toward 10%. Management says the book delivers good ROE with low historical NPAs.

segments.name: Agri and PSL
segments.commentary: Tractor book about 4%, KCC about 4%, individual MFI about 1% of the book; management says these are behaving well with low bounce rates. No state exceeds 20% of asset exposure.

segments.name: Bancassurance / cross-sell
segments.commentary: Management expects a bancassurance commission drop under draft norms and sees cross-sell as slow to ramp, with results possibly over 12 to 18 months. Analysts estimated a 10-12 bps ROA hit.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY27 even without further rate hikes, as surplus liquidity runs off and repo-linked asset repricing begins in November.
Opex trend and cost to average assets expected to continue at similar levels; headcount expected around 12,800-12,900 by year-end, not 13,000.
About 20 new branches in the year, mostly in existing locations.
Credit cost to remain well below the 0.28%-plus guidance level; growth guided at 18-20%.
FY27 ROE guidance of 13.5% expected to be exceeded; capital raise could change the ROE guidance, and management declined to issue a new FY28 target.
Gold loan share capped at 25% of assets.
ECL model with a Big 4 advisor expected to be up and running by March; SMA-1 and SMA-2 reduction is the next credit-cost lever.
capex_capacity: Employee count at 12,002, up sequentially by about 450; growth is directed to existing branches for both assets and liabilities.
Branch network up about 3 in the quarter; about 20 branches planned for the year.
Floating provisions of about INR 218 crore held, with a stated 5.93x cover of operating profit by provisions.

Capital raise: management said it is near closure on three components, with a firm commitment expected within weeks to about a month, before the next investor call; the bank has not raised equity since 2017. Management said it will not raise below book value.
demand_pricing: NIM fell QoQ as surplus liquidity from the $194 million FCNR(B) window (August) was carried for most of the quarter; the NIM is around 3.3% against a guided 3.5-3.6% range, per an analyst.
Deposit cost reduction attributed to a conscious non-highest-rate strategy and repricing of long-tenure term deposits; top-20 deposit cost is under 7%.
Management says LAP demand is strong with a stable rejection rate; about one-third of LAP borrowers are arbitrage cases, a third seek better products and the rest need more exposure.
Gold prices are fairly stable at around INR 14,560 per gram (999 gold). Management names gold price decline as the main risk.
Management cites a bancassurance fee drop as the main earnings headwind, and said other levers will be needed to offset it.

qa_highlights.question: Is opex growth elevated, and will headcount reach 13,000 with 20 branches added this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was driven by people costs and normal cyber-security tech spend, with no one-offs. Headcount is 12,002 and is expected to reach about 12,800-12,900 by year-end; about 20 branches are planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM decline QoQ, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus liquidity from the FCNR(B) raise was carried for most of the quarter; lending yield fell 2 bps QoQ. Management expects NIM to improve in Q3 and Q4 as repo-linked loans reprice in November, and as credit costs stay low.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gold loan book growing faster than disbursements, and are gold slippages rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth includes inorganic DA and co-lending, while disbursement figures are organic only. Non-gold slippage rose to 1.55% from 1.52%. Management said some co-lending and DA partners collect before NPA, so the 1 DPD rule does not apply to many of them.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-FCNR(B), what was the lending yield and margin, and will the expansion continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an ex-FCNR NIM figure. It said lending yield fell 2 bps and that yield should rise with repo hikes, with a fairly decent NIM expansion expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL readiness and impact on PCR and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: A Big 4 firm has been appointed; the ECL model is expected to be live by March. Management said lead indicators are positive except SMA-1 and SMA-2, and sees credit-cost gains from SMA reduction after ECL.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA/ROE guidance be revised, and how will bancassurance fee loss be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to set a new ROE target until capital comes in; it expects ROE above 13.5%. On bancassurance, it cited the prior loss of about INR 100 crore of treasury gains and said it will wait for final norms and build offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Is gold loan CIBIL screening relaxed, and what is the risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Low CIBIL is not a bar for gold loans; management uses it to profile customers. The main risk is a fall in gold prices, and auction recovery was under 10% during the MFI stress, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How are the drought and agri books, and what is the mortgage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor and KCC books are about 4% each and collections remain robust, with no state above 20% of exposure. Management expects mortgage share to rise as gold is capped at 25% and overall growth is 18-20%.

risks_watch: Non-gold slippage edged up to 1.55%, and SMA-1 and SMA-2 are elevated; ECL transition and the related model risk are to be tested by March.
Gold loan book, co-lending and DA partner collection practices and gold price exposure.
Bancassurance commission drop under draft norms; management has not quantified the offset, and analysts estimated a 10-12 bps ROA hit.
Capital raise: terms and price are not yet disclosed; management said it will not raise below book value.
NIM recovery depends on repo pass-through and on deposit repricing lagging asset repricing.
532772|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and firm on asset quality, cost and profitability. Management was evasive on NIM ex-FCNR(B), product-wise repricing mix, and the size and price of the capital raise, citing ongoing negotiations.
key_quotes: So we got more than what we deserve in terms of foreclose -- what you call, prepayment penalty, etcetera, and lesser interest rate.
Below the book value, we will not raise capital. That much I can tell you.
So it's about -- it's from that perspective that you'd be looking at the CIBIL.
So, we are stockpiling liquidity post February '26 Israel-Iran war.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM slipped to about 3.3% vs guided 3.5-3.6% as FCNR(B) surplus liquidity ($194 million) was carried for most of the quarter; management expects it to reverse as repo-linked loans reprice from November, with lending yield already down only 2 bps QoQ while cost of funds fell 8 bps.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 20 new branches planned for the year, branch count up about 3 in Q2, and headcount guided to rise from 12,002 to 12,800-12,900 by year-end, but these are mostly existing-location adds with no plant-style capacity numbers.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 21% YoY and deposits 19%, with management guiding 18-20% growth for FY27 backed by LAP demand, NBFC/co-lending expansion and mortgage pickup as gold share is capped at 25% of assets.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 ROE will definitely be above the 13.5% guidance (quarterly ROE rose to 14.6% from 12.73% over four quarters) and credit cost is expected to stay well below 0.28%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bancassurance commission drop under draft norms could cost about 10-12 bps of ROA (analyst estimate), management has not quantified the offset, and non-gold slippage edged up to 1.55% from 1.52%.

rows.label: Equity capital raise near closure
rows.when: within weeks to about a month of the call
rows.why: Management said it is near closure on three components with a firm commitment expected before the next investor call, the bank has not raised equity since 2017, and it will not raise below book value; size and price undisclosed.

rows.label: ECL model go-live with Big 4 advisor
rows.why: Model expected live by March, and management sees credit-cost gains from SMA-1 and SMA-2 reduction after ECL, against GNPA of 2.29% and PCR of 81.38%.

rows.label: Bancassurance fee drop offset levers
rows.why: Management cited a prior loss of about INR 100 crore of treasury gains and says cross-sell results may take 12-18 months, with offsets not yet quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 2.29%, credit cost 0.28%), cost and ROE above 13.5%, but evasive on NIM ex-FCNR(B), the product repricing mix, and capital raise size and price; analysts pressed on NIM shortfall versus the 3.5-3.6% guide and the bancassurance hit.

532777|2026-03.headline: Info Edge Q4 FY26 standalone billings rose 7% to Rs.1,057 crore and revenue 17% to Rs.805 crore, with 99acres billings flat at 2%.
532777|2026-03.overview: Standalone operating profit rose 39% YoY to Rs.323 crore at a 40% margin, helped by a one-time Rs.20.5 crore 99acres warranty provision write-back that lifted revenue. Recruitment billings grew 10% standalone (9% including Zwayam and DoSelect) amid a subdued hiring market, with GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4. 99acres billings grew only 2% after a sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls, while traffic share rose to 49% web and 52% in April. Management guided to double-digit Naukri topline growth as the threshold for holding margins, and said 99acres should turn cash-generative in FY27 if execution holds.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone cash from operations before tax (Q4 FY26)
Recruitment billings incl. Zwayam and DoSelect (Q4 FY26)
Cash and equivalents incl. wholly owned subsidiaries (Mar 2026)

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri, standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.811 crore (+10%), revenue Rs.581 crore (+14%), operating margin 58% on Rs.340 crore profit (+22%). FY26 billings Rs.2,374 crore (+10%), margin 57%; growth stayed in the 9-11% band all year.

segments.name: Naukri JobSeeker Services
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.53 crore (+33%) at 60% margin; FY26 billings Rs.176 crore (+19%) with Rs.98 crore operating profit. Online revenue mix rose from 27% to 53% in 15 months.

segments.name: NaukriGulf
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.41 crore (+9%), down from about 20% growth before Middle East disruption; FY26 billings Rs.126 crore (+16%) at 35% operating margin.

segments.name: 99acres (real estate)
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.163 crore (+2%), revenue Rs.144 crore (+36%) including the Rs.20.5 crore one-time write-back; operating profit Rs.3 crore. FY26 billings Rs.497 crore (+10%), revenue Rs.488 crore (+19%), operating loss Rs.59 crore.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi and Aisle)
segments.commentary: Jeevansathi Q4 billings Rs.39 crore (+21%) with a Rs.3 crore operating loss; Jeevansathi plus Aisle FY26 billings Rs.182 crore (+29%) and combined operating loss halved to Rs.15 crore.

segments.name: Education (Shiksha)
segments.commentary: Q4 billings Rs.45 crore (-13%), revenue Rs.44 crore (+11%), operating profit Rs.6 crore. FY26 billings Rs.164 crore (+1%), revenue Rs.170 crore (+13%); AI-led search changes cut Google referral traffic.

guidance_outlook: Naukri margins: if topline grows 10% or more, margins should hold; faster growth could expand them; growth of 7-8% could cost some margin in the short term.
Continued investment in JobHai and AI; JobHai targeted to grow about 100% YoY for the next few years, with plans to be more aggressive in Mumbai and Bangalore this year.
99acres: expects billings growth to recover in Q1 FY27; medium-term goal to double billings over 3 years and reach 25-30% EBITDA margin, with cash generation in FY27 if all goes well.
Shiksha: AI-led search headwind expected to persist near term; counselling and voicebots expected to progressively offset it.
Deferred revenue: billings slowdown in H2 FY26 will flow through to lower revenue growth in FY27, per management.
Long-term aspiration: AI-Rex, Talent Pulse, PremiumX and related offerings could add a few hundred crore rupees of incremental revenue over three years.
capex_capacity: 99acres: traffic share rose to 49% web in Q4 FY26 from 46%, 54% app traffic share, and 51% overall in March and 52% in April 2026.
99acres new projects market estimated at Rs.5,000-5,500 crore; new-home responses grew 33% YoY in Q4 versus 20-22% last year; 99Shorts rolled out in NCR with other cities planned for FY27.
AI-Rex agentic recruiting platform: over 1,000 clients onboarded and about 30,000 job mandates processed; made free to many recruiters to drive adoption.
Naukri resumes database about 115 million; about 21,000 resumes added per day in Q4 FY26.
Info Edge Ventures: over 130 non-strategic investments since 2007, about 50 deep-tech or AI-first; two new funds (growth stage and deep tech) launched.
demand_pricing: Hiring sentiment described as lukewarm; JobSpeak Index grew 7-8% YoY in FY26 and has been stable in a 4-6% range per management.
Q4 recruitment billings by segment: Tech, IT and BPM +6%; GCCs -1%; recruitment consultants +8%; other sectors +14%. FY26: Tech/IT/BPM +8%, GCCs +10%, consultants +6%, other sectors +8%.
IT services are 19% of billings (grew 10% in FY26); other sectors are 29% of billings (grew 8% in FY26 vs 14% in FY25).
Premium hiring (above Rs.25-30 lakh) growing faster than mid-level; LinkedIn seen as stronger for senior and passive candidates.
B2C jobseeker revenue growing about 30% after self-serve shift, versus 18-20% historically; paid users rose from 1.2% to 2.2% of MAU in 15 months.
99acres competitors: MagicBricks, Housing (burn about Rs.250 crore per year), NoBroker; Meta and Google compete in new homes; management said leadership changes at Housing and MagicBricks.
Q4 99acres billings hit by a one-time transitional impact from sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls on advance collections.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hiring sentiment across GCCs, IT and non-IT, and what is driving 99acres margins and share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitesh Oberoi called the market lukewarm; larger GCCs have shrunk headcount while smaller ones hire. Share gains credited to execution, with 13-14 points added to traffic share in recent months; new-home responses up 33% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.20 crore 99acres revenue write-back sustainable, and how did it affect billings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-time reversal of over-provisioned warranty on cost-per-lead products, which did not affect billings. Provision will move from 20% to 5% of leads going forward; the write-back was not expected to recur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did jobseeker services revenue grow so fast, and is there guidance for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from AI tools, a self-serve shift away from telecalling and a counter-cyclical lift as hiring slowed. Management was surprised by 30% growth after one quarter and said it was unsure whether it would sustain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for JobHai and its monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is similar to Apna and WorkIndia but more freemium. It is monetising in Delhi NCR and will expand to Mumbai and Bangalore; management targets about 100% YoY growth for several years.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins and 99acres growth be framed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Naukri margins hold at 10%+ topline growth; 99acres aim is 60% share, doubling billings in 3 years and reaching 25-30% EBITDA margin. Management said Q1 should recover but near-term markets may slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the adoption and willingness to pay for AI-Rex, and how does 99acres gain share in new homes?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex was made free to many recruiters after B2B sales friction; it has 30,000 mandates, with 1% take rate targeted. New-home share gains come from secondary-market traffic plus 99Shorts video content.

risks_watch: 99acres Q1 FY27 billings recovery after the 2% Q4 growth and the sales reorganisation; the one-time write-back will not repeat.
Recruitment growth held at 9-11% all year; watch whether Naukri can hold double-digit topline growth to protect the 57-58% margin.
GCC and IT hiring softness, with larger GCCs shrinking headcount and GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4.
Shiksha billings down 13% in Q4 on AI-driven search traffic loss; study-abroad softness in the US and Canada.
Sustainability of B2C jobseeker growth (about 30%), which management said is still unproven after one quarter.
Matchmaking pricing pressure from competitors' discounting; Jeevansathi operating loss of Rs.4 crore in FY26.
532777|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on 99acres share gains and AI product pipeline, but cautious on the hiring market, which management called lukewarm and stable, and explicit that Q4 billings were a reset. Management was evasive on specific forward numbers, saying near-term outcomes are hard to predict and that the B2C growth may not sustain.
key_quotes: Q4 was a reset. The underlying business trajectory remains intact and we expect growth to recover going forward.

If the Indian economy picks up, we expect the non-IT sectors to start hiring once again, and to start hiring a lot more people than earlier, and attrition rates will pick up, but that'll depend on how the economy plays out over the next few quarters.
If we are able to do that, then we should be able to generate at least a 25 -30% EBITDA margin as well.
This business used to grow at 18-20% per year, but after making these changes, it's now started growing at 30%, but it's only been one quarter.
Now, of course, the team is very bullish, but let's see if this sustains.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone billings grew 7% in Q4 and 10% in FY26, 99acres billings only 2% in Q4 after a sales reorganisation, and management expects 99acres to recover in Q1 FY27 with no firm order numbers; deferred revenue from the H2 FY26 billings slowdown will weigh on FY27 revenue growth.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Recruitment billings grew only 9-11% all year, 99acres grew 2% in Q4, Shiksha billings fell 13%, and H2 FY26 billings slowdown flows into lower FY27 revenue growth, with the Rs.20.5 crore one-time write-back not repeating.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI-Rex has 1,000+ clients and 30,000 mandates; 99Shorts rolled out in NCR with other cities planned for FY27; JobHai is being pushed more aggressively in Mumbai and Bangalore this year.

rows.label: JobHai expansion to Mumbai and Bangalore
rows.why: JobHai is monetising in Delhi NCR, with about 100% YoY growth targeted for several years and more aggressive plans in Mumbai and Bangalore.

rows.label: 99acres double billings in 3 years, 25-30% EBITDA margin
rows.when: over next 3 years, cash generation FY27 if execution holds
rows.why: 99acres FY26 billings were Rs.497 crore (+10%) with an operating loss of Rs.59 crore, and Q4 billings grew only 2%, so the doubling target depends on a Q1 FY27 recovery that management has not yet shown.

rows.label: 99acres cash generation in FY27

532777|2026-06.headline: Info Edge Q1 FY27: standalone billings up over 14% and recruitment billings up 17%, with underlying recruitment billings growth at about 15%.
532777|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.824 crores and operating profit rose 33% to Rs.334 crores, with cash from operations up 25% to Rs.225 crores. Naukri recruitment billings grew 17%, which management says is about 15% after adjusting for renewal timing, with revenue up 13% and a 58% operating PBT margin. 99acres billings grew 17% and its operating PBT loss narrowed to about Rs.2 crores, near break-even. Shiksha billings fell 23% on AI-driven search traffic loss, and matchmaking grew billings 20% and was near break-even.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash balance at end of Q1

segments.name: Naukri recruitment
segments.commentary: Billings up over 17% (about 15% normalised), revenue up 13%, operating PBT margin 58%. Tech/IT/BPM billings +15%, GCCs +31%, other sectors +12%, recruitment consultants +1%.

segments.name: Naukri Jobseeker (Naukri 360)
segments.commentary: Billings up over 35%, PBT margin 63%. Paid subscribers rose from 1.3% to 2.6% of MAU over six quarters.

segments.name: NaukriGulf
segments.commentary: Grew 12%, below the roughly 20% pre-geopolitical trajectory; operating margin above 35%.

segments.name: 99acres
segments.commentary: Billings and revenue both up about 17%; operating PBT loss of about Rs.2 crores versus Rs.17 crores underlying loss in Q4 FY26. Web timeshare 49%, app 55%, iOS 69%.

segments.name: Shiksha
segments.commentary: Billings down 23% and revenue down 12% as reduced Google referral traffic hit client delivery; US and Canada study-abroad softer.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Portfolio billings up 20%; Aisle +44%, Jeevansathi +14%; near break-even operating PBT; more than 45% profile share in Hindi-speaking markets.

segments.name: Job Hai
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly doubled on a small base; about Rs.15 crores revenue last year, burn near Rs.50 crores a year.

guidance_outlook: Management said it is not guiding on billing growth; it is unsure whether volume growth can sustain 10% or 15%, but is more confident on new products than six months ago.
Margin expansion depends on topline growth in the teens; if topline grows 8-10%, margins will be hard to improve.
Heavy AI investment will continue, so margins are not expected to expand from AI monetisation alone.
99acres aims to become cash-generative during FY27 and to grow revenue 18-20% a year with cost control; ultimate goal of 30% margin.
Job Hai aims to more than double revenue this year, reach 18 cities in coming months, and could reach Rs.100 crores in two to three years.
Headcount is down YoY; management expects to resume hiring once the business grows in the teens.
capex_capacity: AI-Rex live across more than 4,000 enterprise customers and recruitment firms by end-June, with over 10% converted to paid; free trial rolled out to 10,000 customers in Q2.
Talent Pulse has more than 600 paid customers; AI-Rex and Talent Pulse to be scaled to several thousand more customers over the next few quarters.
Coding Ninjas acquisition completed; short-form upskilling courses priced at Rs.5,000-7,000 being tested.
Over 150 people in GenAI and machine learning; AI efficiencies of 15-20% in some functions.
99Shorts (new project listings) launched in NCR, with plans to expand to more cities; new project segment estimated at over Rs.5,000 crores.
Naukri database of about 118 million resumes, with over 25,000 new profiles added daily.
demand_pricing: Growth split per management: about one-third from volume and renewals, about one-third from price increases, and about one-third from new offerings (AI-Rex, Talent Pulse, employer branding); customer-count growth is a small subset.
AI-Rex priced per mandate at Rs.3,500 for companies and Rs.2,500 for consultants (launch prices); sold to over 400 clients in Q1 and about 300 more in July.
Recruitment consultants, about a quarter of revenue, grew only 1%; management attributes this to clients insourcing in a slow market.
99acres: primary about 45-47% of revenue, secondary about equal, owners 7-10%; NCR is the largest market and has been affected by sales-team restructuring.
Management says the JobSpeak index measures volume only, which does not capture premiumisation, pricing and new products.
Competitive pressure easing after Housing.com was acquired by Aurum, which management expects to reduce competitor marketing spend.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 13% revenue growth is from realisation versus customer count, and how much from AI products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about one-third of revenue growth came from renewals and volume, and about one-third from newer offerings such as AI-Rex and Talent Pulse. Premium CV views are growing over 25% from a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the normalised 15% recruitment billings growth adjusted for the favourable Q1 FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said normalisation nets out early and deferred renewals each quarter, which captures the prior-year base effect. GCC billings grew 31% reported, with about 2.5% of one-off timing shift from Q4 FY26 deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients paying separately for AI-Rex, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex is charged per mandate and sold separately in many cases, by the same sales team plus specialists. Of 4,000 free trials, 400 converted; management says cannibalisation is possible, mainly among consultants who downgraded.

qa_highlights.question: Will 99acres reach 30% margin faster after the Housing acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so: competitive intensity should fall as Aurum may cut marketing spend. Sales restructuring is mostly behind, and NCR may take one to two more months to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-Rex renewal cycle and how is value measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs one renewal cycle to confirm success. Customers buy mandate bundles (10, 20 or 30 mandates), and internal dashboards track shortlisting, screening and delivery time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 99acres billing reconciled against JobSpeak index trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JobSpeak index tracks volume only, while billings also include premiumisation, pricing and new products. Sanjeev Bikhchandani attributed faster billings to sales teams making more and better calls.

risks_watch: Volume growth depends on net hiring; management says mid-tier volume is weak and consultant (about a quarter of revenue) growth is flat.
Shiksha billings down 23% with no near-term recovery expected; AI-driven search changes and weakness in US and Canada study-abroad.
NaukriGulf growth slowed to 12% due to Middle East disruption.
AI-Rex and Talent Pulse have only one renewal cycle of evidence; possible cannibalisation of existing products.
Consultant and mid-market volume trends; watch whether July's AI-Rex sales convert to paid usage.
Job Hai burn of about Rs.50 crores a year, and 99acres NCR sales recovery.
532777|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the Naukri product pipeline and 99acres traction, but cautious on volume: management repeatedly said it does not know whether growth will sustain at 10% or 15%. It was candid that Shiksha faces continued pressure and that 99acres monetisation lagged its traffic lead.
key_quotes: This was a better quarter than the ones we saw through FY26.
If you're able to grow topline in the teens, margins should improve. But if for some reason, top line growth comes at 8, 9, 10%, then it'll be hard to improve margins.
AI is also changing how we operate, driving efficiencies of 15-20% across some functions.
We're confident of being able to deliver revenue growth without adding too many people.

rows.why: Management says margins improve only if topline grows in the teens; recruitment revenue grew 13% with 58% PBT margin, and 8-10% growth would make margin gains hard, while heavy AI investment continues.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

532777|2026-09.headline: Info Edge Q2 FY27: standalone billings up 13% YoY, revenue up 13% to Rs.842 crore, operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore; CEO Hitesh Oberoi steps down Dec 2.
532777|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone billings grew 13% and revenue 13% to Rs.842 crore, with operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore and operating PBT margin of 41% (up 541 bps). Management said renewal timing shifted billings between Q1 and Q2, so H1 (billings +14%, revenue +12%) is the better read, with underlying growth guided at about 14-15%. Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi announced he will step down as MD and CEO at close of business on December 2, with Sanjeev Bikhchandani becoming Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from December 3; Oberoi stays on the board subject to shareholder approval. Management said AI-first products now run at a Rs.240 crore annualised rate, and 99acres reached near-breakeven operating losses with positive cash generation.

segments.name: Real Estate (99acres)
segments.commentary: Billings +21% YoY in Q2 (up from 17% in Q1), revenue +17%. Operating loss cut 93% from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore; operating cash flow Rs.22 crore vs Rs.2 crore a year ago. Marketing spend down about 13% YoY while enquiries grew 33%.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Billings +23% in Q2 (Jeevansathi +18%, Aisle +40%). Segment near breakeven at operating PBT; Jeevansathi operating profit Rs.2 crore, Aisle operating loss Rs.3 crore. Segment cash generation Rs.3 crore vs cash loss Rs.2 crore a year ago.

532782|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose over 115% YoY to INR37 crores at a 5.3% margin; FY26 EBITDA up 25% to INR85 crores on 3% lower income.
532782|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the best quarter of the year, with standalone total income of INR699 crores (up 4% YoY) and gross margin of 45% (up 329 bps YoY). For FY26, standalone income fell 3% to INR2,585 crores while EBITDA rose 25% to INR85 crores at a 3.3% margin, and management said the year was cash positive. Home textiles turned EBITDA-positive at INR8.4 crores (from negative INR3.5 crores), and the company is guiding FY27 as a year of margin expansion, profitability and deleveraging, without giving numeric targets. Management also flagged losses at the US subsidiary American Silk Mills, which is being closed or muted; India operations reported no inventory losses.

segments.commentary: Recycled polyester and sustainable fiber business operating at over 100% utilisation in FY26, described as a breakout year and a strategic ESG-aligned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What margins are expected from technical textiles, and which sectors are targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Protective textile margins of 12-15%, depending on inherent or treated FR. Target sectors include oil and gas and steel, with the application base much wider.

qa_highlights.question: Home textile EBITDA trajectory and whether INR18-20 crores in two years is realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it is confident of at least doubling home textile EBITDA next year on the order book and strategic customer commitments.

532783|2026-03.headline: LT Foods FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR11,023 crore, but reported EBITDA margin was 11.8% after U.S. tariff pass-through and brand spend.
532783|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue including other income grew 26% YoY to INR11,023 crore, with normalized revenue growth of 19% excluding U.S. tariff effects. Reported gross profit was INR3,692 crore (normalized gross margin about 35.3%) and EBITDA INR1,236 crore, with PAT of INR625 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR2,938 crore, EBITDA INR300 crore and PAT about INR136 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to U.S. tariff pass-through, a doubling of marketing spend in India, UK investment phase and remodelling of the organic segment, and guided to a gradual margin recovery toward 12% EBITDA.

financial_highlights.change: excl. U.S. tariff and shipment-terms change

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to EBITDA / net debt to equity

financial_highlights.value: INR9,742 crore; 88% of revenue; EBITDA margin 12.3%

segments.name: Basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR9,742 crore (88% of total) with 29% reported and 21% normalized growth; EBITDA margin 12.3%. Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19% in FY26.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue crossed INR1,016 crore, up 9% in FY26, but segment is under stress from currency and commodity pressure and is being remodelled; holds 12% share of India's organic food exports.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat (RTH) and ready-to-cook (RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR187 crore in FY26 (2.5x over five years); growth constrained by RTH plant capacity, with new capacity expected from Q2 FY27 (production start around July). Segment gross margin ~32-33% reported, ~35% per management, and 40%+ before sampling and promotion spend.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Value growth 10% and volume growth 12%; quick commerce and e-commerce grew over 45%; premium segment grew 2x the portfolio; market share 23.7% (Nielsen); household reach 64.4 lakh (Kantar).

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Contributed 48% of FY26 revenue with 53% reported growth (about 9% normalized); Royal holds over 60% share; Golden Star is about 10% of segment revenue and was fully consolidated after buying the remaining 49% stake.

segments.name: Europe / UK
segments.commentary: Europe revenue grew 34% in FY26; UK revenue about GBP 45 million with a target of GBP 100 million by 2030; UK is in an investment phase.

segments.name: Middle East and Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Saudi Arabia is a new market launched with about INR50 crore revenue; Southeast Asia contributed INR53 crore; management is not investing heavily in the Middle East.

guidance_outlook: Management expects continued double-digit growth; long-term growth target 10-12% organic.
Gross margin for FY27 expected broadly in line with FY26, around 33-33.5%, as tariff has normalized from 50% to 10%.

EBITDA margin expected to recover toward the ~12% level as brand investments normalize and scale benefits come through; management says it is confident of the 12% range but flagged a disruptive environment.
RTH, RTC and organic segments expected to grow faster than the overall business.
Capex guidance: about INR330 crore in FY26 and similar in FY27; long-term run-rate about INR250 crore a year. Rice capacity cost is about INR3 crore per ton.

RTH revenue target of INR300 crore in about two years; RTC target INR100-120 crore by 2030; RTH/RTC breakeven at about INR400 crore segment revenue, now pushed out about one year due to capacity constraints.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR330-360 crore, mainly U.S. (Houston land purchase and RTH facility and warehouse), UK packaging facility, and India land and warehouses.
RTH capacity in the U.S. was 15 million (INR150 crore) this year; a new plant is delayed and is expected to start production around July/Q2 FY27, targeting INR300 crore in two years.
Raichur (Karnataka) facility investment to deepen regional rice play.
India milling capacity is 8 lakh tons of paddy-to-rice; packing capacity is about 8-9 lakh tons. The company adds 50,000-60,000 tons of rice capacity a year.
Europe packaging asset build-out and India warehousing are planned for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says the U.S. consumer demand has not been impacted by war and inflation, as food spending is the last to be cut.
Basmati industry paddy prices rose about 20-25% in the domestic season; international deals are 85% closed for the season, with the remaining 10-15% priced 15-20% higher.
Raw material prices are up roughly 25-30% from opening levels; management expects prices will not fall much.
Freight to the Middle East rose 10-15x (Dubai about $200 to $2,200; Jeddah $700-800 to $2,600); Europe freight is the most disrupted; U.S. freight is not materially disrupted.
Premium SKUs grew 2x the overall portfolio in India, and the mix shift is supporting gross margin; value and volume growth in India were roughly equal.
Distribution in India is flat at about 172,000 outlets versus the 170,000 cited earlier, but market share improved year on year.
Regional rice revenue is about INR170 crore, growing at a high double-digit rate.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 U.S. and basmati volume growth, and how much did U.S. tariffs affect them?
qa_highlights.answer: Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19%; U.S. volume rose about 30-38% including Golden Star, or 7-8% excluding it. Management said the tariff disruption helped win customers through better service levels, at some margin cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment revenue growth numbers not reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the India and U.S. figures are normalized for tariffs and Golden Star, while the basmati segment figure includes tariffs. Golden Star moved from a JV to a 100% subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 gross and EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected to stay within the FY26 range, about 33-33.5% (FY25 was about 24.6% on the old basis). EBITDA should return toward 12%, which was the prior-year level.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payable days about 100?
qa_highlights.answer: 60-70% of purchases are made in season and 30-40% outside it, with deferred payment terms. Management expects roughly 100 payable days to persist. Inventory is about 190-200 days on average, with 250 days cited as of March 31.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RTH/RTC targets and breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: RTH revenue is INR15 crore this year, with a target of INR300 crore in two years. RTC targets INR100-120 crore by 2030. Breakeven is at about INR400 crore of segment revenue, now about one year later due to capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex breakup and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about INR350 crore, mainly U.S. (Houston land, RTH plant) with UK and India warehousing. FY27 capex is expected to be similar, with a long-term run-rate of about INR250 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bhopal insurance claim status?
qa_highlights.answer: INR136 crore is outstanding from the insurer and INR50 crore has been received against a bank guarantee backed by an FD. No accounting gain has been booked until the final verdict, expected in June.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin recovery depends on tariff normalization holding at 10% and on higher paddy and freight costs (Middle East freight up 10-15x) not persisting.
RTH supply is constrained until the new capacity starts around July/Q2 FY27, which could hold back the segment's growth and breakeven timing.
Organic segment remodelling and currency/commodity pressure are weighing on profitability; capacity will take time to utilize.
Inventory of about 250 days and payable days of about 100 need watching for working capital and cash flow.
Bhopal insurance claim: INR136 crore outstanding with a court verdict expected in June; no accounting gain booked until then.
El Nino and the 1.5-month outlook for the next basmati crop are key open risks for procurement costs.
532783|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share and growth targets, but cautious on margins, citing a dynamic environment and several items management could not yet quantify, such as aged-inventory volumes and the El Nino outlook. Some answers were deferred to investor relations, and the call ran through a mix of questions from the analyst and individual investors.
key_quotes: So we are eying at 10% to 12% of growth on a long -term basis that we are and we remain to that growth levels.
Whatever the disruption has come, we have accounted for till time said, we are confident that we will be in the range of 12%.
So this year, we have spent INR330-odd crores. And the next year also will be in the same range.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA margin back toward ~12% from 11.8% in FY26 as brand spend normalises, while gross margin is held at 33-33.5% with tariff at 10% vs 50% earlier; partly offset by paddy prices up 20-25% and Middle East freight up 10-15x.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: U.S. RTH/RTC plant is under construction with capacity coming online from Q2 FY27, targeting INR300 crore segment revenue in about two years from INR15 crore this year; India adds 50,000-60,000 t/yr of rice capacity on top of 8 lakh t milling.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19% in FY26, India volume grew 12%, and management expects continued double-digit growth; RTH/RTC/organic expected to outgrow the group, though RTH is capped by capacity until Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex ran about INR330-360 crore in FY26 and is guided to a similar INR330-odd crore in FY27 with a long-term run-rate of about INR250 crore a year, plus Raichur, Europe packaging and India warehousing projects planned; an incremental announcement is likely but not a step-change.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on margins, citing a dynamic environment, raw material up 25-30%, El Nino risk and an unquantified aged-inventory issue, so an upgrade looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA recovery to 12% depends on tariffs holding at 10%, paddy costs and Middle East freight (10-15x) not persisting, and RTH breakeven already pushed out about one year to around INR400 crore segment revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RTH capacity start in Q2 FY27 unlocks the RTH/RTC range growth toward INR300 crore in two years and RTC INR100-120 crore by 2030; Saudi Arabia is a new market at about INR50 crore revenue.

rows.label: International basmati deals 85% closed for season
rows.why: 85% of international deals are closed at prices for the season, with the remaining 10-15% priced 15-20% higher, supporting realisations, while raw material is up 25-30%.

rows.label: Bhopal insurance claim verdict
rows.why: INR136 crore is outstanding from the insurer and INR50 crore already received; no accounting gain booked until the final verdict expected in June, so a one-time gain is possible in the window.

rows.label: Working capital days down to 176 from 196
rows.why: Working capital days fell 20 days YoY to 176, but inventory of about 190-200 days (250 cited at March 31) and roughly 100 payable days leave cash flow exposed.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, market share, RTH growth and the 12% EBITDA target, but cautious on margins, El Nino and unquantified aged inventory; analysts and investors probed on segment growth reconciliation, payable days and inventory.

532783|2026-06.headline: LT Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore, with EBITDA up 20% to INR363 crore but margin down to 11.5% from 12.1%.
532783|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore (19% normalised), with gross profit up 19% to INR1,029 crore and PAT up 9% to INR183 crore. Core basmati and specialty rice revenue rose 34% to INR2,845 crore on 11% volume growth at a stable 13% EBITDA margin. Organic foods revenue fell to INR254 crore at a 4% EBITDA margin during restructuring to a direct-to-retailer CPG model. Management said results are in line with annual estimates and reiterated full-year guidance, with the organic recovery expected over 1.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 12.1% in the prior-year period (stated as 11%)

segments.name: Core basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,845 crore, up 34% YoY on 11% volume growth, with EBITDA margin stable at 13%. India revenue grew 23% YoY; market share 23.1% and household penetration 64.4 lakh households.

segments.name: International (incl. North America)
segments.commentary: Contributed 71% of consolidated revenue. North America grew 49% (29% normalised); Middle East and rest of world grew 44%. Europe/UK are in an investment phase with margin pressure from logistics costs.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue INR254 crore after a temporary decline during the shift from wholesale to direct retailer (CPG) sales. EBITDA margin 4%; management guides to 7-8% by year-end and double digits later.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook (RTH/RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 13% YoY, with biryani kits up 42%. The US RTH facility is expected to become operational this quarter; breakeven is targeted at INR400 crore revenue within 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 results are in line with annual estimates and the company is on track across all financial parameters for the full year.
Organic EBITDA is expected to reach INR70-80 crore by year-end, with margin rising to 7-8% and returning to double digits; full recovery in growth and margin targeted for FY27-FY28.
Medium-term segment growth guidance: basmati 10-12%, RTH 15-20% (small base), organic 10-12%.
FY30 ambition is more than doubling India revenue with expanding margins; RTH revenue to double in about 3 years.
Basmati EBITDA margin historically 13-14%, with a plus or minus 1% variance possible if crop inflation occurs.
Middle East growth expected around 15% from a small base.
capex_capacity: Capacity doubled for ready-to-heat products; US RTH facility expected to become operational in Q1 FY27.
Organic capacity expanded in Europe, with a plant set up and a full sales organisation built there.
No capex planned yet for the newly opened Australia entity, which has received a very small equity infusion.
Rice inventory 346,000 tonnes at an average of INR56/kg and paddy inventory 164,000 tonnes at INR38/kg as of 26 June, described as sufficient for the next year's branded demand.
Quarterly volumes: India 109,000 tonnes; international 117,000 tonnes.
demand_pricing: US tariff on rice fell from about 50% to 10%, which management says reduced the margin distortion from tariffs; pricing volatility from tariffs is now normalising.
Rice revenue growth (32-34%) was above volume growth (11%), driven by commodity inflation pass-through and US duty.
Management said it is charging a premium in basmati and Sona Masoori in organic versus competitors.
Freight rates to the Middle East rose from $200 to $4,000 per container; the competitive landscape limited pass-through there.
Logistics cost was 4.7% of revenue in Q1 FY27 after one-offs (damage retention) in Q4 FY26 phased out.
Nielsen methodology change cited for the India market share decline from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%; management claims share gains in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino on the crop, and whether margins are at risk from inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-85% of basmati area relies on canal or groundwater irrigation and 14-15% on rain. About 20% of area faces issues; a clearer crop picture is expected by mid-to-end August. Costs would be passed on to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary gross and EBITDA margins fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to the shift from CIF to C&I shipment terms with a related US subsidiary and a drop in organic gross margin from 35% to 33%. Management said consolidated gross margin improved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR419 crore to INR486 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the increase reflects Golden Star, now 100% owned, being consolidated from this quarter. Previously it was not consolidated, so both revenue and expenses rose.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US growth net of discounts, with discounts still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are recorded net of promotions and discounts under accounting rules, so the reported growth is already net.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior quarter included a one-off gain from revaluation of investments, which has not recurred; other income is now normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did organic margin fall and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model moved from wholesalers to direct retail, with a new Europe plant and sales organisation. Margin is 4% now, targeted at 7-8% by year-end, and expected back in double digits in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much more working capital can be released from supplier financing?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is near optimum supplier financing, with perhaps 4-5 days of further room but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India's market share falling and will the top two players lose share to the third?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to a Nielsen methodology change. It claims share gains this quarter, with about 40%+ share on e-commerce platforms and a 20 lakh household increase last year.

risks_watch: El Nino and irrigation: crop size clarity expected by mid-to-end August; management says about 20% of basmati area faces issues and a lower crop would bring inflation, which it expects to pass on to consumers.

Organic recovery execution: margin is 4% now, targeted at INR70-80 crore EBITDA and 7-8% margin by year-end, with a return to double digits over about 1.5 years (FY27-FY28); organic gross margin fell from 35% to 33%.
US RTH facility start-up this quarter; RTH breakeven at INR400 crore revenue targeted in 2-3 years, and management acknowledged the US RTH ramp has weighed on segment margin.
Logistics and geopolitical costs: Middle East freight rose from $200 to $4,000 per container, and Europe/UK margins are under pressure; pass-through is uncertain in the Middle East.
Market share: India share fell from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%, which management attributes to a Nielsen methodology change; it claims share gains this quarter, which is not yet independently verified.
Working capital headroom: management sees only about 4-5 days of further supplier-financing room; US tariff refund eligibility is partly received but not yet booked.
key_quotes: So the previous rate, 10%, has continued for after that expiry as well.
So in terms of changing our route to market earlier, we were selling to the wholesaler. Now we are directly selling to the retailer, which we call CPG.
So it is the breakeven that will be coming at a revenue size of INR400 crores.
So there is no impact of demand and on the margin side also.

rows.why: Working capital days fell from 195 to 170 and inventory days from 221 to 187, but the CFO sees only about 4-5 days more supplier-financing room.

532783|2026-09.headline: LT Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR3,253 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.0% on freight and brand spend.
532783|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 17% YoY to INR3,253 crore, with PAT up 10% to INR180 crore. Gross margin fell to 32.5% from 34.2%, driven by a shift to FOB shipment terms with a related party (EBITDA-neutral) and higher shipping costs, which rose about 40 bps of revenue. Advertising rose to 2.5% of revenue from 1.8% in Q1, and EBITDA margin was 11.0%. Management reiterated a 13-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin target without a timeline, while Middle East was hit by supply and freight disruption.

vs 11.4% in Q2 FY26 and 11.5% in Q1 FY27

qa_highlights.question: What are current basmati inventory levels and average cost, and what is the procurement strategy for higher-priced crops?

qa_highlights.question: Why did RTC/RTH gross and EBITDA margins decline sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to planned promotions and sampling netted in gross profit, which per management was about INR2 crore for H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any revision to FY27 EBITDA guidance from 11.5%-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not revise guidance. It said freight added about 40 bps and brand investment about 20 bps. CFO reiterated 13%-13.5% consolidated margin, with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital release in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is seasonal, as Q2 is a non-peak procurement period. Cash will be used as procurement resumes in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are tariff refunds being accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said partial refunds have been received and discussions with customers are ongoing. Clarity is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Do you benefit from the falling rupee, and how much is forex in the top line?

532784|2026-03.headline: Sobha FY26 real estate sales hit a record INR8,136 crore (+~30%), with Q4 EBITDA of INR194 crore and FY27 sales growth guided at a similar ~30%.
532784|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: real estate sales of INR8,136 crore at an average realisation of INR14,675 per sq ft (up 9.4% from INR13,412), and 3,188 homes (5.4 million sq ft) delivered, up about 19%. Q4 revenue recognition improved after occupancy certificates delayed in Q3 were received, with Q4 total income of INR2,030 crore, EBITDA of INR194 crore and PAT of INR92 crore. Net operating cash flow was INR1,637 crore for FY26 (up 39.4%) and the company moved to a net cash position of about INR800 crore. Management expects margins to improve through FY27, with projects nearing completion guided at 24-26% margins against a 30%+ EBITDA margin on the overall unrecognised revenue of INR18,647 crore. Some FY26 launches slipped, and the Rivana (Greater Noida) launch and the Crescent (Gurgaon) launch in April were the main new-launch data points.

A ₹12 crore FX loss was attributed to mark-to-market on a liability balance-sheet item (payables) and was called out separately; management is reworking its hedging policy and plans to settle the balance. Management said Bandhan Bank went live as the third ATP bank in the quarter, and that the UAE (ValueFirst international) closure, delayed for about three years, should close this quarter. Management gave no quantitative guidance, declining to share FY27/FY28 growth targets or Digital Platform mix, and said the platform revenue lag is a timing issue.

FY28 absolute EBITDA target of about INR 1,000 crore reaffirmed.

North Star: 20% revenue CAGR FY25-FY31, with EBITDA margin moving toward 20% over 5-7 years; FY31 revenue aspiration about INR 11,000 crore. Organic CAGR of about 20% now seen as achievable if industry momentum holds.
Margin ambition of a further 100-200 bps over the next few years, toward 17-18%.

capex_capacity: Capex capitalised in H1 FY27 was INR 60 crore; full-year capex guided at about INR 300 crore.

Board approved (24 Oct 2026) a new Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, with capex of about INR 150 crore funded by debt and internal accruals; commissioning in two phases from Q3 FY28, peak turnover about INR 500 crore.

Greenfuel Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 (ferrule-less tubes, fittings, receptacles) for M&M; Maruti Suzuki firm orders also won. Capacity expected to be significantly utilised by M&M and Maruti over about 2 years.

Inflation: input costs (crude-linked polymers, electronic parts, freight, rupee) are rising. Most cost increases are passed to OEMs with about a one-quarter lag; management says pass-through is complete, with a 30-40 bps EBITDA margin dilution in Q2.
Order book of INR 1,879 crore: about 14% to execute in FY27, 59% in FY28, 27% in FY29; about 85% is new business. EV and CNG together are 29% (CNG 20%, pure EV about 9%); future technologies 22%.

Content per vehicle: about INR 70,000-75,000 per PV and INR 20,000-22,000 per 2W; about 50% of PV content is in IAC; Greenfuel about INR 5,000-8,000 per vehicle. Mechatronics is about 20% of PV content; expected to rise about 10% in 2-3 years.
Aftermarket growth target of 15-20% over a 3-5 year horizon, despite weak H1.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through lags about one quarter, so margins dilute by a few bps. It remains confident of the FY28 INR 1,000 crore EBITDA target and of sustaining current margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% North Star revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31) still realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is now more confident of about 20% organic CAGR if industry growth holds. Inorganic growth could push it higher. The base year is FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Who develops the Body Control Module (BCM), and is it reported in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: BCM is a build-to-print standalone revenue stream since SOP in July 2026, with a INR 250 crore order book. Technology comes from a large Japanese electronics component maker, not a JV; it is reported under Mechatronics across standalone and subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV component strategy and the Aftermarket outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV focus is narrowed to 3-5 products, with active SOPs targeted for 2028-2030 and possible inorganic routes. Aftermarket grew 11% in Q2 and 9% in H1; the 15-20% target is over 3-5 years.

532799|2026-03.headline: Hubtown guides FY27 pre-sales of ~6,000 crore and collections of ~3,000 crore; 25 South/Downtown debt expected to fall at least 35% by end-FY27.
532799|2026-03.overview: Management hosted its Q4 and FY26 analyst meet, focusing on the promoter-entity mergers, project launches and debt reduction. In FY26 the company sold about 1 million sq ft, mainly in Mumbai, for roughly 4,400 crore of pre-sales and collected about 1,900 crore. About 11,300 crore of unrecognised revenue from booked sales sits in existing projects, with substantial recognition expected in FY27 on project completions. Two of the three promoter-entity mergers are NCLT-approved and the third awaits exchange approval. Refinancing of the roughly 15% legacy debt has slowed due to Middle East market conditions, and the proposed equity placement at 341 was cancelled in favour of a possible QIP.

financial_highlights.change: Management said both pre-sales and collections improved vs previous years; no exact percentage given

financial_highlights.value: approx. 1 million sq ft, primarily Mumbai

financial_highlights.metric: Unrecognised revenue from booked sales (existing projects)

financial_highlights.change: Construction finance for 25 West from ICICI at 12%

segments.name: 25 South / 25 Downtown (merging entities)
segments.commentary: 25 South is about 95% sold and expected to complete in FY27; 25 Downtown has sold almost 1.1 million sq ft of carpet area. Combined debt of these two is about 4,000 crore and management expects at least 35% reduction by end of this year.

segments.name: 25 West (Bandra)
segments.commentary: Fifth tower launched, selling about 1,40,000 sq ft; first tower completion expected next year. Construction finance from ICICI at about 12%.

segments.name: Rising City (Ghatkopar)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 (about 6.5 lakh sq ft): 5 of 6 towers have received OC; 6th tower OC expected in calendar 2026. Phase 2 (commercial offices) to be partly launched this year.

segments.name: Hubtown Seasons (Chembur)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 launch of about 500,000 sq ft expected this year, including a strata commercial building, one luxury and two mid-luxury buildings; phase 1 revenue expected in FY27.

segments.commentary: About 150 acres on seafront at Thane and Mulund, about 2.5 crore sq ft, not yet launched; environmental clearances being obtained and expected within months.

Management says returns to shareholders and stakeholders will start coming from FY27 onwards.
Mergers: 25 West and Ghatkopar holding entity merger expected this year; 25 South/Downtown awaiting exchange approval. Effective date of all mergers is 1 April 2025.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 350 acres and over 35 million sq ft; delivered 47+ projects, mainly in MMR.
Total ongoing and unlaunched pipeline stated as in excess of 1 lakh crore GDV; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore.

Rising City Phase 2 commercial offices expected to do well given strong office market.
Management said price growth cannot be expected to be sharp, but prime-location product should avoid a cycle hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pro forma financing cost look high relative to combined debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest payable to DLF on Downtown's balance sheet was unprovided for 3-4 years due to disputes; it is now provisionally booked after settlement. Some further outflow until full repayment; Shapurji's share was small.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 15% cost of borrowing be refinanced lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing efforts continue but have slowed due to the last six months' market conditions and the Iran-US/Middle East situation; not expected in the immediate future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end FY27 debt level for 25 South?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is combined across 25 South and 25 Downtown, not only 25 South; at least 35% of the total should go down by end of this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total GDV of the launch and pipeline projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Total including unlaunched and ongoing projects is over 1 lakh crore; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore; other launch projects about 50,000 to 60,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the equity placement at 341 per share?
qa_highlights.answer: It was cancelled because the market did not support the preference share issue; management is now looking at a QIP instead.

qa_highlights.question: Has the 6,000 crore asset-debt raise authorised last year been done?

532799|2026-06.headline: Hubtown Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 17% YoY to INR156 crore and PAT dropped 68% to INR27 crore under project completion accounting.
532799|2026-06.overview: Revenue and profit fell year on year because revenue is recognised only on occupation certificate and handover, and Q1 FY26 was a high base. Management stressed contracted pipeline (INR11,583 crore yet to flow through P&L), collections of INR320 crore and pre-sales of INR535 crore in the quarter. Merger of 25 Downtown, 25 West and 25 South entities remains subject to NCLT sanction, with the first two schemes approved by key authorities. Management guided pre-sales of about INR6,000 crore for FY27, weighted to Q3 and Q4, and collections of INR3,000 crore.

532804|2026-03.headline: Technocraft Q4 FY26 margins lifted by a one-time INR20 crore steel quantity discount; management guides June quarter in line with Q4 but declines full-year outlook.
532804|2026-03.overview: Management described a strong Q4 FY26, with scaffolding US demand recovering from the September quarter slowdown and sustained momentum into June. Scaffolding margin was boosted by a one-time INR20 crore steel quantity discount relating to prior quarters; the company cited the adjusted margin at about 16%. Forex gains of INR20 crore in Q4 (INR46 crore for FY26) also supported profitability. Aluminium formwork (Mach One) volumes were soft due to real estate project delays, though order book rose to over 4.5 lakh sq m. Management declined to give FY27 guidance beyond the June quarter, citing volatility.

segments.name: Scaffolding (US-led)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat QoQ but margin up sharply on INR20 crore one-time steel discount and higher volumes in US; FY26 scaffolding volumes down ~6.5% YoY per analyst, ~8% growth in division revenue cited. Middle East ~15% of FY26 scaffolding revenue; Europe ~1.5% after Poland B certificate.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork (Mach One)
segments.commentary: Volumes soft (down ~17% in Q4 per analyst); capacity utilisation ~60-70% due to slow site mobilisation; order book up QoQ to over 4.5 lakh sq m (>6 months of production). Extrusion plant at 100% utilisation. South America ~3% of formwork volume in FY26.

segments.name: Drum closures
segments.commentary: Stable demand and pricing; single-digit revenue growth; China growing strongly, rest of world ~4-5% growth in quantity and price. March quarter volumes down ~10 lakh sets YoY, which management attributed to a volatile prior-year base.

segments.name: Engineering services
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR80 crore per quarter, growing ~8-10% QoQ; investing heavily in AI-led services, which may cause bottom-line growth to lag top-line. Billing mainly headcount/hourly basis.

segments.commentary: Yarn EBIT near breakeven, EBITDA ~10%; overall textile division still loss-making though losses narrowed in Q4. Fabric division under restructuring review; options include outsourcing processing and possible exit, not decided.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: No revenue update; samples under evaluation with DRDO and defence department; management declined to reaffirm earlier 5% to 10% of sales targets.

qa_highlights.answer: No; current run-rate is INR80 crore per quarter, growing 8-10% every quarter, so a jump to INR120 crore in one quarter is not expected.

532804|2026-06.headline: Technocraft Q1 FY27: Drum Closure EBIT margin near 43% on record volumes and rupee depreciation; management targets sustainable 30% for drums, 15% for scaffolding and engineering services.
532804|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, with Drum Closure posting its highest-ever revenue and EBIT margin (about 43%) on higher export volumes and a weaker rupee. Scaffolding volumes rose year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand, with realisations broadly stable. Mach One (aluminium formwork) volumes fell year-on-year but edged up sequentially, which management attributed to site and project readiness rather than competition. Management repeatedly declined to treat the current margins as the new normal and kept its sustainable-margin guidance unchanged. No significant new capex is planned for FY27.

segments.name: Drum Closure
segments.commentary: Almost 100% export. Volumes and rupee depreciation drove record revenue and EBIT. Management targets a sustainable margin of 30% or more. Non-seasonal, not order-book based.

segments.name: Scaffolding (Steel)
segments.commentary: Volumes up year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand (data centres, semicon, AI chip plants, energy). Operating at about 95% utilisation. Sustainable margin guidance of 15%. Middle East is 2-3% of sales and declining.

segments.name: Mach One (Aluminium Formwork)
segments.commentary: Volumes down year-on-year, up marginally quarter-on-quarter. Utilisation about 75-80%. Order book of 3-5 months. Aluminium extrusion plant at over 95%-100% utilisation and helped EBIT amid higher aluminium prices.

segments.name: Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Growing fast on US outsourcing demand, including AI-based vision, embedded systems and automation. Sustainable margin target about 14-15%, which includes ongoing tech investment.

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Fabric business shut down and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn business profitable. Garment business loss-making, with breakeven targeted within two quarters. Working capital released about Rs 15-20 crore (figure varied during the call).

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: JT Cooler approved by DRDO and an Israeli sensor maker, with export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at roughly 15% margin. Missile canister repeat orders. Confirmed order book about Rs 20-21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Drum Closure: sustainable margin of 30% or more; similar volumes expected in the immediate quarter.
Scaffolding: volumes expected to be maintained or improved for the next two quarters; beyond that not guided due to volatility. Sustainable margin 15%.

Capex: no significant new capacity capex in FY27, only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN plant and Aurangabad Mach One Phase 2 expected next year.
US tariff refund of close to $3 million expected in the Scaffolding segment, not yet received; timing not stated.
Middle East scaffolding sales expected to stay volatile for one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: No significant new capacity capex planned for FY27; only maintenance capex across divisions. The last major capex (CSN plant, FY25) is fully operational.
Aluminium extrusion plant running at over 95% (management said 100%) utilisation since the March quarter; 100% backward integrated for Mach One.
Mach One utilisation about 75-80%, after a recent Aurangabad capacity expansion. Phase 2 expected sometime next year.
Scaffolding utilisation about 95%. Management says it can add capacity within about 3 months using space in Mumbai and China plants, and is studying options.
Next year: CSN Phase 2 and extra extrusion capacity plus forward integration.
demand_pricing: US scaffolding demand strong since January 2026, driven by AI chip, semicon and energy construction; realisations stable as steel prices did not rise sharply.

US tariff on Chinese scaffolding is 75% (50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301) vs 50% for India and others. Management says Chinese steel costs are 20%+ lower, but Technocraft is only about 5% higher on cost.
Management says it does not compete on price; it competes on inventory availability, distribution and a 150+ component mix.
Indian project launches strong across 7 major cities; demand also from commercial, GCCs and data centres.
Drum Closure: no price cuts planned; competitive position as the world's second-largest producer. Rupee depreciation lifted realisations.
Europe scaffolding sales started in the last two quarters (CE certification), still small due to weak construction in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mach One volumes decline year-on-year, and how is competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to site and project readiness, not competition or demand. Volumes rose slightly quarter-on-quarter. Focus is on quality customers and profitability, not rapid volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43% Drum Closure margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the sustainable margin is above 30% and 43% is not the new normal, given volatility in freight, tariffs and geopolitics. Rupee depreciation and volumes drove the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Defence JT Cooler opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at around 15% margin. Management said quantum is hard to estimate because defence procurement is slow and product-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What are the scaffolding tariff and competitive dynamics in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff is 50% for India, 75% for China. Chinese prices are sometimes lower, but Technocraft does not sell on price. Its US subsidiary and inventory-led distribution are its edge.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capacity capex this year; only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN and Mach One expansion next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Textile plan after the fabric exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric shut and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn profitable; garment loss-making, with breakeven targeted in two quarters. No active plan to sell the rest of the business.

532805|2026-03.headline: Redington Q4 FY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 33,269 crore and adjusted PAT hit a record INR 467 crore (1.4% margin), before a INR 75.2 crore Arena impairment.
532805|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was Redington's best quarter on both revenue and profit, led by India (revenue +50%, PAT +41%) and strong TSG and PC demand. Middle East was hit by the West Asia conflict from 28 February 2026, with March weak and supply, insurance and receivable issues. FY26 revenue was INR 119,347 crore (+20%) with adjusted PAT +17% and PAT margin 1.3%. Management guided to a soft Q1 FY27 and a dividend of INR 6 per share (30% payout), while conserving cash for inorganic growth and larger large-deal working capital.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue +50% and PAT +41% in Q4; growth across all business units, with up-country expansion +45% and data-centre deals with neo-cloud operators.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue +19% YoY, about 33% of top line in Q4; driven by premium smartphones and direct-to-retail in India, while Middle East premium demand was constrained.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions Group (PCs)
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% YoY, about 30% of top line; boosted by component-shortage pull-forward, price increases and large deals of nearly INR 500 crore; 41% of India commercial AI PC revenue from >40 TOPS models.

segments.name: Technology Solutions Group (TSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue +34% YoY, about 19% of top line; record revenue as data centre, networking and server/storage all grew, with large deals above INR 1,100 crore and some deals shifted from Q3 to Q4.

segments.name: Software Solutions Group (SSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue +31% YoY, 17% of top line in Q4 (17% for FY26 vs 15% in FY25); cloud and software growing above 30%, security growing slower and needs catch-up; target gross margin 5.5-6%.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey, Lira business)
segments.commentary: Q4 loss of INR 44 crore (Redington share INR 22 crore, including exit costs on Lira business); exiting Lira phone and mix businesses by FY26 end, focus shifting to USD-based IT and cloud; Arena book value about $8 million.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa clusters
segments.commentary: Middle East is 30-35% of business; Q4 UAE +6% (FY +22%), KSA -12% (FY +5%), GCCL +51% (FY +33%), Africa +26% (FY +13%).

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be soft, with India demand strong but Middle East softness likely in Q1 and partly Q2; management said the trajectory is similar to March, neither worse nor better.
Middle East recovery expected to follow resolution of the West Asia crisis; Saudi Arabia expected to stay soft until IT priorities are clear.
Opex to stay elevated for 1-2 years as capability-building investment continues; AR provisions and war-related insurance and freight costs expected to normalise.
EBITDA outside Arena guided at about 2.2%-2.4%, subject to large-deal mix; ROCE to stay above 18% (currently near 20%).
Arena losses expected to continue into FY27 at a reduced level, with a real turnaround in the subsequent year; Turkey demand expected to soften further.
Large deals were about INR 1,600 crore+ in Q4 and about INR 2,500 crore for FY26; management expects this to keep rising in H1 FY27, with more working capital needed.
capex_capacity: No formal capex or capacity figures disclosed; management is exploring inorganic opportunities, particularly in cloud and security professional services.
AI Exchange marketplace launched mid-March with 200+ AI agents from ISVs; AI revenue expected to start during FY27.
Cloud Quarks platform 2.0 rolled out in Q4 with digital lifecycle analytics and automated subscription renewals.
India data centre market at 1.5 GW, expected to reach 7.5 GW in a few years; management is building a data-centre plan covering hardware, power, cooling and co-location.
demand_pricing: Component shortages (PCs, smartphones, GPUs) and expected price increases drove Q4 PC demand; ASP-led growth expected to be significant, with unit growth marginal.
Management does not expect COVID-style margin and working-capital gains; gross margin to be maintained, but working capital may rise on credit and stock-up needs.
Middle East war caused insurance withdrawal on 7 days' notice, higher retention, and supply-chain and logistics disruption; alternate warehousing and imports via Europe and Mumbai used.
Large deals will be lower margin than the core business; management will hold to ROCE and working-capital discipline rather than margin percentage.

Software: management sees no visible subscription softening from AI models so far, but expects AI-native security tools to be a watch item; Microsoft Copilot cited as an example of OEM tie-ups extending to other LLM providers.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 be framed, with India growth vs rest of world recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: India expected to keep growing with a soft Q1; Middle East and Africa strong in H1 once the crisis eases; management said it is not sure when the crisis will end.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable and inventory provisioning split by India and RoW?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory provision about 3 bps for FY26 vs 5-6 bps long-term average; AR provisions higher due to one-offs in Saudi and India government receivables; AR may normalise, with partial recovery possible.

qa_highlights.question: Opex, factoring and employee cost trends, and dividend rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Factoring fell sharply (Arena: INR 22 crore in Q4 FY25, INR 18 crore in Q3, INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26); employee cost up on capability investment and rupee at 94 vs 88. Dividend kept low to conserve cash for inorganic and large-deal needs.

qa_highlights.question: Large-deal guidance and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Large deals were about INR 2,500 crore for FY26, with Q4 at INR 1,600+ crore; margins much lower than core, but ROCE will not be compromised.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East inventory risk and insurance cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurers withdrew war cover on 7 days' notice; Redington added cover elsewhere and moved stock across warehouses, now said to have adequate coverage with some higher retention in the interim.

qa_highlights.question: SSG gross margin and profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: SSG gross margin tracked at about 5.5%, with an intended 5.5-6% range; professional services expected to lift margin; resell pressure to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciling INR 467 crore, INR 287 crore and INR 391 crore profit figures?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 467 crore excludes the Arena impairment exceptional item; INR 287 crore is PAT before minority; INR 391 crore is after minority, including the impairment share.

Opex and interest cost rise: elevated employee and technology spend for 1-2 years, plus higher interest costs from factoring and working capital.
Working capital and receivables: AR provisions higher; working capital may rise with large deals and stock-building.
Supply and pricing: component shortage duration (12-18 months) and when price increases end are unclear; pull-forward demand could reverse in 2-3 quarters.
AI disruption to security and SaaS subscription models is unproven but under watch; security growth lags cloud and software.
