532805|2026-06.headline: Redington Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR34,966 crores and PAT 77% to INR486 crores, helped by PC price-led stock-and-sell.
532805|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR34,966 crores (+34% YoY), EBITDA INR751 crores (+67%) and PAT INR486 crores (+77%), with profit growth outpacing revenue. Excluding Arena, revenue grew 41% to INR33,794 crores and profit was INR517 crores, which management called the best ever. India grew 63% on top line and was the strongest geography, while Middle East & Africa grew 15% despite the West Asia crisis, with UAE and Saudi softening. Management attributed a large part of ESG growth to component-shortage-driven price increases and channel stocking, and flagged that large data-center deals will dilute margin percentage. Arena continued to lose money (INR64 crores total, INR31 crores Redington share).

financial_highlights.value: INR64 crores total; INR31 crores Redington share

financial_highlights.change: vs INR31 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Middle East & Africa

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 performance was driven by pre-buying ahead of chip price hikes, and what is channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stock-and-sell effect is largely in ESG PCs; channel holds about 2-3 months of inventory, and the build is across distributors and Tier 2 partners.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on large deals and India mobility growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR700 crores of the INR1,000 crore large deals came from India data centers; funnel is multiple times that. Premium smartphone share gains helped Mobility, but management is unsure if demand holds after price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East demand in UAE and Saudi, and cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE was down about 3-4% and Saudi slightly more; some freight and warehousing cost passed on, while about $3 million of extra cost sat in opex.

qa_highlights.question: Why Arena losses persist and what is the end goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue halved, margins compressed and opex inflated by 35-40%; management says structural options are being evaluated and losses may continue this year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose industry-wide, but better payable days, especially in Middle East from additional vendor credit, offset it; spikes occurred within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise 74% QoQ, and what was the INR147 crore tax refund?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher revenue and inventory days raised interest, and market rates firmed though central bank rates were unchanged. The refund related to contested past-year demands that the company won.

532805|2026-09.headline: Redington Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR43,002 crores and PAT excluding exceptionals rose 50% to INR581 crores, with Arena still loss-making.
532805|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and PAT, with growth broad across India, GCC, Africa and the UAE, led by TSG (up 91%) on AI server and GPU migration. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue reached INR77,967 crores (up 41%) and PAT excluding exceptionals INR1,067 crores (up 61%). Arena remained the drag: revenue fell 37% YoY and Redington's share of loss was INR115 crores, including transition and impairment charges. Management flagged elevated receivable provisions, inventory above comfortable levels, rising debt, and possible softening in consumer demand after price increases.

segments.name: India distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution business grew 67% YoY in the quarter, the fastest of the regions cited.

segments.name: Rest of World ex-Arena
segments.commentary: Grew 38% YoY; GCC and Levant ex-UAE/KSA +121%, UAE +39%, Africa +35%, Middle East overall +41%.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY and was 34% of consolidated revenue; SISA geography grew 70%; Rest of World Mobility grew 34% ex-Arena.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 38% YoY to 30% of revenue, driven mainly by higher ASPs plus a sequential rise in commercial PC volumes; highest quarterly revenue to date.

segments.name: Technology Solutions Group (TSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 91% YoY to 20% of mix; large deals above INR3,800 crores (about 9% of group revenue), mostly data centres and neo-cloud. Ex-large deals TSG grew about 33-35%.

segments.name: Software Solutions Group (SSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 39% YoY to 15% of revenue, with all SBUs growing, led by cybersecurity and cloud; SSG gross margin above 6%.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 37% YoY; exited the VDF contract and high-interest Lira working capital business; new management in place; Q2 loss includes transition provisions and impairment.

guidance_outlook: Management sees H2 FY27 growth north of 25% at overall business level, with caveats on price-driven demand contraction and West Asia impact on UAE, KSA and GCC.
H2 seasonality is expected to be muted this year because price increases and shortages pulled consumption forward; H2 is normally bigger than H1.
Sustainable quarterly opex guided at INR950-1,000 crores.
TSG expected to be the strongest growth driver in H2, followed by SSG; ESG and MSG approached with more caution due to price-volume elasticity.
Neo-cloud opportunity in India estimated at INR150,000 crores over the next four years; data centre margins below the 4.5-5% run-rate, with ROCE targets maintained.
Management expects SSG and TSG gross margin to improve over 3-5 years through orchestration and services; debt-equity may rise, with equity raise possible if growth needs it.
capex_capacity: Funded capital investment for the data centre large deals is almost nil; only non-funded (bank guarantee) capacity is used, per the CFO India.
Funding strategy: additional debt is currently sufficient; dividend moderation or equity raise are options if the growth trend requires it.
Debt-equity is about 0.5-0.6x; management cited global distribution peers at 0.6-0.8x and said distribution is working-capital intensive, typically above 1:1.
Five AI learning centres rolled out in India over the last two quarters (CSR); AI COE launched in Singapore with a physical experience centre and a virtual COE in build.
demand_pricing: Smartphone and PC prices up roughly 30-50% YoY; enterprise AI PC adoption above 40% in commercial, consumer around 10%.
Consumer PC/smartphone units declining; Microsoft activation data down 20-30% for consumer, while commercial PC activation is 0-7% growth.
Enterprise is about two-thirds of Redington's PC business and consumer about one-third; Mobility is roughly equal consumer-type, so IT is about half-half.
Management views market share as flat to a slight gain, with no loss.
Channel inventory above comfortable levels as partners hold stock ahead of price increases; Middle East supply chains stressed (Strait of Hormuz closed, alternate routes adding turnaround time).
Gross margin ex-large deals about 5.13%; reported gross margin broadly similar QoQ.
AI exchange platform in early traction, engaging hundreds of partners; described as a long-term journey.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins trending down despite lower Mobility mix, and how sustainable is the TSG large-deal pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TSG jump is a CPU-to-GPU migration with roughly 4x ASPs, not just pricing, and expects it to continue. CFO said margins ex-large deals were 5.13%, similar to last year, and that Arena's higher-margin local-currency business in prior-year quarters affects comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Arena losses rise to about INR70 crores in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were three components: business loss, Lira transition provisions (rebates and discounts not aligned with vendor support), and a INR40 crore intangibles impairment. Business loss alone was much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable opex and what provisions were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex was elevated by receivable provisions, SSG investments, and Middle East war-related insurance costs. Sustainable run-rate is INR950-1,000 crores per quarter. Receivable provisions were about INR213 crores (INR67 crores SISA, INR135 crores Arena); inventory provisioning was not material.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth be funded and what are the levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is sufficient for now; levers include more debt, moderating dividends, or raising equity, which will be used if the growth trend requires it. Debt-equity of 0.5-0.6x was described as comfortable versus 0.6-0.8x for global peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth exceed 25%, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no reason to pull back from north of 25% H2 growth, with caveats on price-led demand contraction and West Asia impact. Seasonality is expected to be muted because price increases pulled demand forward.

qa_highlights.question: Would a slowdown in AI capex affect the FY29/FY30 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TSG and data-centre business would be affected by any AI capex pullback; SSG (cloud, security) and smartphones less so. PCs could see some impact, but the market is expected to rationalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the neo-cloud opportunity and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: India neo-cloud capacity is expected to go from 1.5 GW to 7 GW and then 12 GW; INR150,000 crore opportunity over four years. Margins are below the 4.5-5% run rate, but ROCE targets are maintained with less incremental opex.

qa_highlights.question: When will Arena turn around?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Arena has exited high-interest Lira working capital business and is near the end of that transition, but partner health and Turkish market issues make a turnaround timeline hard to estimate.

risks_watch: Arena (Turkey) receivables and liquidity, plus a new management team and further restructuring; Q2 loss of INR115 crores including INR40 crore impairment.
Price-led demand elasticity in consumer PCs and smartphones after 30-50% price increases; possible post-Diwali demand contraction.
Channel inventory above comfortable levels, with working-capital build and Q2 FCF of negative INR1,871 crores.
West Asia conflict impact on UAE, KSA and GCC, including logistics, collection cycles and insurance costs.
TSG large deals are lumpy in data centres; AI capex pullback risk for TSG and FY29/FY30 targets.
Rising debt and possible equity raise or dividend moderation as working capital grows.

rows.why: AI exchange platform is in early traction with hundreds of partners and the AI COE in Singapore is under construction, but no commercial product launch dates were given.

532808|2026-03.headline: Pearl Global FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11.5% to INR5,025 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% (10.3% ex tariff and new-facility losses).
532808|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,314 crore (+6.9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA (ex-ESOP) of INR135 crore at a 10.3% margin, the highest quarterly margin to date. FY26 PAT rose 17% to INR270 crore, helped by cost restructuring, while India volumes fell sharply in Q4 as US tariffs shifted orders to other countries. Management guided to a 10% group EBITDA margin for FY27 and a 12-14% revenue CAGR, with FY28 capacity of 125-130 million pieces. The company also raised its dividend to a record INR14.50 per share for FY26.

segments.name: India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 India revenue fell about 23% as the US tariff pushed orders out of India; management says Q4 India EBITDA ex-tariff was 9.6% versus 10.2% a year earlier. Target is high single-digit EBITDA for FY27 and double-digit in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Strong export growth to the US, UK, EU, Spain and Canada; capex of about 6 million pieces due H1 CY2027, with two new units (washing and stitching) ready in H2 this year.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation rose to 80%+ from 63%; management is buying land for a greenfield project and considering in-house capacity over partner factories.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Utilisation rose to 47% from 39% last year; the company will buy an extra 10% of PT Pinnacle Apparels for $1.4 million, taking its stake to 99.92%.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Losses continuing; strategy reworked and management expects breakeven in FY27. The Other segment (Indonesia, Dubai, US, Guatemala) drove the Q4 spike, not Guatemala alone.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group adjusted EBITDA margin guided at about 10%, then 10-12% in subsequent years, with the 10% considered largely operational.
Revenue CAGR of 12-14% targeted at group level; management says the INR6,000 crore FY28 target (set in 2023) is achievable even at about 9% growth.
FY28 target: 125-130 million pieces of established capacity and about 100 million pieces shipped, to reach INR6,000 crore.
FY27 capex of INR200-250 crore being outlined across geographies; INR250 crore already committed for completion by H1 FY27.
Expected realisation gain from the removal of tariff costs, though hard to quantify as costing is reset each season; current realisation about INR635-640 per garment, with a goal of INR600+.
Guatemala expected to reach breakeven in FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 101 million pieces per annum as of 31 March 2026, crossing 100 million ahead of an H1 FY27 target.
Bangladesh expansion adds about 6-7 million pieces in FY27; CWIP INR110 crore, expected to reach about INR150 crore after H1 FY27 capitalisation.
Vietnam land parcel identified; purchase consideration $2.5-3 million; greenfield plans to follow.
Management targets an additional 20-25 million pieces, combining capex and partner capacity, over the next two years; a laundry capex in Bangladesh will lift margins without adding top line.
Bihar plant is in ramp-up; the company adds capacity line by line, with partner factories used alongside in-house (target roughly 80-85% in-house).
demand_pricing: India order book is seeing good traction after the US tariff eased; EU and UK customers are interested in India under the FTAs, and some are seeking added capacity there.
US consumer demand has held up despite inflation; management says there is no sign yet of the weakness seen in 2022 at about $110 oil.
Raw material costs are typically passed through within 1-2 months of order booking, and fabric is bought once orders are placed.
Muji has crossed about $65 million in turnover and is in the top 6 clients; UNIQLO is not a current priority due to competitive overlap.
Discounts and burden-sharing to US clients during the tariff period weighed on India margins; part of the 10% US tariff is still being absorbed.
Design team grew from about 70-75 to just over 100 people.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India revenue fall about 23% in Q4 and what drove growth in the Other segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India orders shifted out under the high US tariff, with existing orders shipped by December-January. Growth in overseas business came from volume and value-added products in Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia; the Other segment includes Indonesia, Dubai, US and Guatemala, not Guatemala alone.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 10% margin be sustained in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10% is achievable for FY27, given the removal of reciprocal tariff costs and the Guatemala and Bihar ramp-up, with Q4 seasonally strongest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR6,000 crore FY28 target consistent with INR630 realisation and 100 million pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR6,000 crore target dates from 2023 and is expected to be exceeded; the company plans 12-14% group CAGR, with growth rotating across countries.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed beyond INR250 crore for 25-30 million pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: INR250 crore covers the committed program; FY27 capex could be INR200-250 crore, and the total may exceed that, combining in-house and partner capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff cost likely to be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR36 crore tariff cost will fall significantly, possibly to INR5-8 crore, with some burden share continuing at about 10%.

risks_watch: US tariff regime: the Section 122 10% tariff runs only until July; refund claims after the Supreme Court ruling may be slow.
Energy-driven input cost inflation (cotton and polyester) and freight; manpower availability is a flagged risk.
Ramp-up risk for Bihar, Indonesia and Guatemala; Guatemala breakeven in FY27 is a target only.
Higher inventory days versus last year; management partly linked this to higher Q1 FY27 shipments.
Capex scope for FY27 (INR200-250 crore) and the Vietnam land deal are still under evaluation.
Timing of the India-EU and India-UK FTA implementation dates.
532808|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY27 margins and growth, with clear numbers on tariffs and capacity. Evasive on exact figures for realisation trajectory, Muji vendor share, and new-client counts, which management said are hard to predict.
key_quotes: And we are pretty confident at this stage to really maintain 10% EBITDA for the full year as we start FY '27.

So by 2028, what we had foreseen is that we should be having established capacity of anywhere between 125 million to 130 million, and we should be shipping around 100 million pieces to get to that target of INR6,000 crores that we spoke about.
So, 12% to 14% is something like we have been talking about as a CAGR that we have planned.

rows.why: Management expects breakeven in FY27 after reworking strategy, but this is only a target, and losses (part of ~INR13 crore Bihar/Guatemala drag in FY26) are continuing.

rows.label: India-EU and India-UK FTAs
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, dependent on implementation dates
rows.why: EU and UK customers are interested in India under the FTAs and some seek added capacity there, but implementation dates are not yet confirmed and India standalone revenue fell about 23% in Q4.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 10% margin, 12-14% CAGR and the INR6,000 crore FY28 target, and tariff cost removal, but was evasive on realisation trajectory, Muji vendor share and new-client counts; analysts probed margin sustainability and FY27 capex scope beyond INR250 crore.

532808|2026-06.headline: Pearl Global Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.5% YoY to INR1,528 crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 10.7% (up 140 bps) and PAT of INR99 crore.
532808|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR1,528 crore grew 24.5% YoY, the highest ever Q1, driven by volume growth (20.8 million pieces vs 17.2 million). Adjusted EBITDA excluding ESOP was INR164 crore (up 44.1%), margin 10.7%, and PAT INR99 crore (up 51.4%). Standalone (India) EBITDA margin fell to 6.6% from 7.3% because of Haryana wage revisions. Management reiterated double-digit full-year EBITDA margin and said FY28 INR6,000 crore revenue target could be reached earlier.

financial_highlights.metric: Dividend received from Pearl Global Hong Kong

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Largest geography at about 45%+ of group volume; business growing with existing and new customers. Capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces expected operational in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: About 27% of group volume; key for high-value and outerwear products; management evaluating further capacity expansion and land acquisition completed.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: About 22% of group volume. Utilisation 65-70% on capacity basis, efficiency about 50-58%. Standalone EBITDA margin 6.6% due to Haryana wage hikes; Bihar second shed to add run-rate revenue of INR1,700-1,800 crore at full utilisation.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Healthy momentum off a lower base with focus on premium clients; described as not fully utilised; management expects both top line and bottom line growth.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Operating strategy reworked; management confident of break-even in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY28 revenue target of INR6,000 crore could be achieved earlier than planned if current trend holds; management says it may be exceeded.
Revenue CAGR range of 12-14% now seen as conservative; management indicated FY27 high-teens growth looks feasible at current run rate, subject to H2 US conditions.
Double-digit EBITDA margin expected for full FY27 and Q1 margin of about 10.7% expected to be sustained in subsequent Q1s; long-term aim 10-12% by FY28 and 11-12% as levers converge.
Installed capacity to reach about 108 million pieces after Bangladesh expansion (Sept-Oct 2026); target of 125-130 million pieces by 2028 retained, with interim capacity via partner factories.
Finance cost guided at 1.7%-1.8% of sales for FY27.
Capex of approximately INR200-250 crore planned for FY27 across geographies; detailed plan to follow in coming months.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh: capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces plus eco-friendly laundry unit starting September, operational for orders in H2 FY27.

India: Bihar two sheds of 450 machines each; first shed (woven) operational at about 120,000-130,000 pieces per month; knit shed production expected Oct-Nov 2026; full capacity 4-5 lakh pieces per month once ramped.
India second shed revenue run-rate potential INR1,700-1,800 crore at full utilisation, expected ready Sept-Oct.
Vietnam: land acquisition completed; greenfield project planned later, with partner-factory capacity also being added.
Overseas utilisation about 75-80% on quarterly available capacity; India utilisation about 65-70%.
demand_pricing: US consumer behaviour described as healthy despite inflation; similar trends in EU and UK; retailers expected to pass on IEEPA refunds, which may support order books.
Realization uplift of INR20 per piece YoY attributed mainly to product mix (outerwear shipped in Q1); management says it is not a sustainable benchmark versus full-year average of INR643 in FY26.
Last year India had double-digit discounts tied to tariffs; management expects these to fade, supporting realization in Q2-Q4.
Retailers are ordering short-term rather than long-term; no shift to early ordering seen.
Japan: China share of clothing imports fell from about 65% to about 50%; Vietnam at 17.4%, Bangladesh at 4.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in Q1 revenue and any revision to full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the growth is not one-off; the end of tariff overhang lifted customer orders. Full-year FY28 INR6,000 crore target now seen as achievable earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.7% margin free of tariff impact and is standalone margin recovery possible?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tariff impact in Q1 and the margin is operational. Standalone margin would be about 9%+ excluding the Haryana wage impact; target is high single-digit to double-digit in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 51% while gross margin rose to 51.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed this to a mix of outsourced/partner-factory production booked under other expenses and higher-value overseas products improving gross profit; management said the gross margin is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost fall and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital days stable at about 43-44; more internal cash used instead of some receivable financing. Finance cost guided to 1.7-1.8% of sales for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are India utilisation and efficiency levels?
qa_highlights.answer: India capacity utilisation about 65-70% and efficiency about 58%; Bihar ramping up line by line; India volume up about 27% YoY.

risks_watch: Standalone India EBITDA margin compression (6.6%) from Haryana minimum wage hike of 38% and Noida hike of 21%; labour availability issues in Q1.
US tariff regime: MFN plus 10% additional tariff on India, Bangladesh, Indonesia and 12.5% on Vietnam after Section 122 expired on July 24; potential 301 tariff changes.
Freight and shipping disruption (container shortages, Bab-el-Mandeb, Strait of Hormuz energy volatility); customers currently bear freight under FOB terms.
Dependence on H2 US demand, with management flagging possible Fed rate hikes and war-related uncertainty.
Guatemala break-even targeted in FY27; Bangladesh expansion ramp-up timelines; Q2-Q4 realization trend relative to Q1 seasonality.
532808|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, FTAs and capacity; more cautious on macro, US demand in H2 and the India margin drag. Some answers were loose on specifics (capacity, utilisation), with several figures deferred to later communication.
key_quotes: We registered our highes t ever consolidated revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax for the quarter.

This quarter, there is no tariff impact. This entire EBITDA is operational improvement and was driven by the volume growth and the operational efficiency which we have earlier mentioned in our commentary and answer to the questions.
So, it is not a one - off thing that has happened.
We remain confident of sustaining the double-digit EBITDA margin on a full year basis as well.

rows.label: Realization recovery as tariff discounts fade

rows.label: Finance cost held at 1.7-1.8% of sales
rows.why: Finance cost guided at 1.7-1.8% of sales with net working capital days stable at about 43-44 and more internal cash used instead of receivable financing.

rows.why: Operating strategy reworked and management confident of break-even in FY27, but no quantified loss or revenue figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, FY28 target timing, Bangladesh and Bihar capacity and double-digit margin, but cautious on US H2 demand, macro and the India margin drag from Haryana wages; analysts probed one-off nature of Q1 revenue, the 51% rise in other expenses and the 10.7% margin's tariff

532809|2026-03.headline: Firstsource Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.6% YoY in constant currency to INR25.8bn; FY27 guidance is 10-13% CC growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.
532809|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR25.8bn (US$283m), up 19.5% YoY in rupee terms and 11.6% in constant currency, with TeleMedik adding 1.3pp. EBIT margin was 12.2%, up 30bps QoQ and 100bps YoY, marking the sixth straight quarter of sequential expansion. Management said two timing effects (a delayed UK collections deal and paused Medicare Advantage payer ramps) hit Q4, which it views as deferrals rather than structural. FY26 revenue crossed US$1bn at INR95.6bn with 13.6% CC growth and 11.7% EBIT margin. Management framed the strategy as "Intelligence that operates" and guided FY27 CC growth of 10-13%.

segments.name: Banking & Financial Services (BFS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 9% YoY and 5% QoQ in CC with six new logos. UK collections deal, delayed by regulatory approval, is now live; Q4 exit financial services pipeline described as among the strongest in recent quarters.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 16% YoY and 10% QoQ in CC with one new logo. Payer side saw short-term timing shifts as Medicare Advantage plans paused program ramps from January 2026; rates flat per management.

segments.name: Communications, Media & Technology (CMT)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3% YoY but fell 4% QoQ in Q4 due to timing of work packets and program transitions in large consumer tech engagements; management expects a return to healthier growth.

segments.name: Diverse portfolio (retail, utilities)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23% YoY but fell 8% QoQ in CC in Q4 on a seasonal retail dip after Q3 peak; four new logos added, and utilities demand described as steady.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4% QoQ and 14% YoY in CC; management expects broad-based momentum to continue across the three core verticals.

segments.name: Geography: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4% YoY and was flat QoQ in CC; two large deals won in Q4 and pipeline up about 60% over the last four quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guided at 10-13%; management said it has visibility to the lower end (10%) and expects the rest to come from pipeline and ramps.
FY27 EBIT margin guided at 12.25-12.75%, above the Q4 FY26 exit of 12.2%.
Management expects margin expansion of 50-75bps a year, with a longer-term target of 14-15% EBIT margin in the next couple of years.
Inorganic contribution to FY27 growth expected at about 2-2.5% from Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik.
Growth is expected to be spread evenly across the four quarters of FY27, not back-ended.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 20-22%.
Management said the two Q4 timing effects (UK collections and Medicare Advantage) are deferrals and should provide tailwinds in FY27.
capex_capacity: TeleMedik acquisition integrated in Q4; gives delivery presence in Puerto Rico, a US-compliant lower-cost location for healthcare and non-healthcare nearshoring.
Sales presence being set up in Canada; UK utilities and retail capabilities being replicated in the US; a North America utilities head was onboarded in the last three months.
Dedicated large-deal pursuit team set up; at least four large deals reported in each of the past five quarters.
Investment in go-to-market and technology continued through FY25 and FY26, with new roles including domain-plus-AI, forward-deployed engineers and builders.
Kairos described as the delivery platform for Intelligence that operates, designed to run in clients' own technology environments and model-agnostic across AI partners.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 added 11 new logos, including six strategic logos (potential of at least US$5m annual revenue each); FY26 added 47 new clients including 24 strategic.
FY26 had 150 clients above US$1m run-rate (up 34 over Q4 FY25); US$5m+ clients up 12 and US$10m+ clients up 2 in the year.
Top five and top 10 clients' revenue share fell 8% and 12% respectively over eight quarters.
Management said about 50% of strategic wins from the past eight quarters have converted into relationships above US$5m annual revenue.
Seven of the FY26 large deals came from new logos versus five in FY25.
Pricing for a US collections deal uses a platform fee plus per-interaction pricing with outcome accountability.
Management said AI is a structural TAM expander through scaffolding work, though clients' data quality and regulated processes slow full automation.
Offshore and nearshore delivery shift is accelerating in Europe; management said it may continue near term.
Management said FY26 organic growth was about 9.8-9.9% CC excluding Ascensos, Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik, versus about 12.1% ex-Pastdue and TeleMedik only.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Firstsource growing strongly when the market narrative says AI is cannibalising BPO revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani cited three drivers: TAM expansion as clients need AI scaffolding; share gains from challenger brands playing offense; and clients willing to move work away from in-house delivery with compelling commercial constructs.

qa_highlights.question: How should the rising debt (near INR1,600 crore) be viewed, and is there room for more acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Jain said 40-50% of cash flow goes to shareholders and the rest to acquisitions or growth; FY26 debt rose only about INR200m versus about INR700m in FY25, so the balance sheet leaves buffer for more acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 softer than expected, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani said Q4 was broadly in line barring two timing items: a UK collections deal delayed by regulatory approval into Q1 FY27 (now live), and Medicare Advantage payers pausing program ramps from January 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic contribution in FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik contributed about 1.5% to FY26 growth (organic about 12.1%). Inorganic contribution to FY27 is expected at about 2-2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the right to win against diversified IT services firms in the full-stack intelligent operations strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani argued that clients buy one continuous motion across implement, run and transform rather than pillars; Firstsource's size and domain depth in regulated workflows let it assemble teams around the customer problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much will investment in the Intelligence that operates strategy affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said efficiency saves from automation and offshoring fund new capabilities, and it remains confident of the FY27 margin guidance; FY26 margin expansion was about 74bps.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 growth phase across H1 and H2, and why does organic growth appear to slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is expected to be spread evenly across the four quarters, not back-ended. Management said about 2% of FY27 growth is inorganic, and the lower end of guidance is backed by visibility plus pipeline and ramps.

532809|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the FY27 10-13% CC growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin guidance, and on pipeline (above US$1bn, highest ever). rows.why: 17 large deals in FY26 (vs 14 in FY25), 4 in Q4, six strategic logos added in Q4 and deal pipeline above US$1bn (highest ever); about 50% of strategic wins from the past eight quarters have converted into US$5m+ relationships.

532809|2026-06.headline: Firstsource Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.9% YoY to INR27.2bn (+2.2% QoQ cc) with EBIT margin 12.4%, but INR717m exceptional charges and a healthcare BPaaS wind-down weigh on outlook.
532809|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.9% YoY and 5.5% QoQ to INR27.2bn (US$288m), or 12.3% YoY and 2.2% QoQ in constant currency, the ninth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth. EBIT margin was 12.4%, up 110bps YoY and 20bps QoQ, the seventh straight quarter of margin expansion. Reported PAT was INR1.7bn after INR563m net exceptional charges, against adjusted PAT of INR2.2bn. Management said a healthcare payer BPaaS program is being wound down by a client after a leadership change, costing roughly 1-1.5% of quarterly revenue, and reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10-13% cc growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.

financial_highlights.change: +22.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ reported; +12.3% YoY, +2.2% QoQ constant currency
three items: INR357m healthcare program termination, INR284m regulatory penalty indemnity, INR76m contingent consideration fair value (Ascensos)

financial_highlights.value: around 23% in Q1; guided 22-24% for FY27

segments.name: BFS
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 14% YoY and 5% QoQ in constant currency; five new logos added. Management cited a strong exit deal pipeline and collections demand from record US consumer debt.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY but fell 2% QoQ in constant currency; four new logos added. Payer-side Medicare Advantage programs were paced by CMS rate changes, and one BPaaS payer program is being wound down.

segments.name: CMT
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency; two new logos added. Management cited volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions in Silicon Valley consumer tech.

segments.name: Diverse portfolio (incl. utilities, Pastdue Credit, retail)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency; one new logo added. Management said utilities demand is steady with a healthy pipeline.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency. Management is setting up sales presence in Canada.

segments.name: Geography: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18% YoY and 6% QoQ in constant currency; two large deals won in Europe. South Africa is the fastest-growing geography, and a Glasgow office was opened.

segments.name: Geography: Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY, driven by both existing clients and new logos.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth reaffirmed at 10% to 13%.
FY27 EBIT margin reaffirmed at 12.25% to 12.75%.
Original guidance had included about 1% to 1.5% of growth from the healthcare BPaaS program now being wound down; management says guidance holds after absorbing this.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be strong as new wins ramp over roughly the next three months.
Long-term aim of a 14% to 15% EBIT margin over the next two to three years, with 50-75bps annual expansion thesis reiterated.
Management expects the exceptional-item amounts (INR357m and INR284m) to be recovered from the client and insurer, though they were expensed on a prudence basis.
capex_capacity: No capex plan, capacity figure or utilisation metric was disclosed on the call.
Headcount 36,875 at Q1 FY27 end, +670 QoQ; offshore and nearshore hiring close to 80% of gross additions.
New delivery footprint: new Glasgow office for UK financial services regulatory work; South Africa cited as fastest-growing geography; Canada sales presence being set up.
Healthcare BPaaS program (payer) wound down; client had been at advanced implementation stage on a new technology platform, now reverting to status quo platform.

Five new growth engines (Middle East, South Africa, Canada and others) and three new capability frontiers (US Retail and CPG practice, marketing services, security and resiliency services) stood up in Q1.
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5m) won in Q1, the sixth straight quarter of four or more; ACV intake was the highest in the last four quarters.
12 new logos added, including three strategic logos; 145 clients above US$1m run-rate; US$5m+ clients up 80% and US$1m+ clients up 45% over two years.
Healthcare deal wins were more than a third of Q1 wins, in line with the roughly one-third revenue share from healthcare.

Hedge book at 30 June 2026: GBP61.6m at an average of 118-120 for the next 12 months; US$119m at about INR92.7/US$. Around 25-30% of the portfolio is in options at roughly 125-130 for GBP; blended GBP rate about 123-124 and USD about 94.
Management said the BPaaS client is wound down by client decision after leadership change, and the client has added more work elsewhere in the account.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue impact of the healthcare BPaaS termination in Q1, and what does the INR271m charge include?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Q1 revenue impact of about 1-1.5%. The charge relates to partner-ecosystem deliverables; Firstsource is the single point of contact and is recovering amounts from the client and repaying partners.

qa_highlights.question: How is guidance maintained despite this hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was the best quarter for new deal wins in the last four quarters and that several wins ramp quickly, offsetting the 1-1.5% loss, so the 10-13% range is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the healthcare payer churn a sector-wide issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an isolated, one-off event caused by a new client leader pausing programs, not a secular trend. The same client continues to expand its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How does the wound-down program compare with the USD50m steady-state run-rate expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 1-1.5% contribution was its estimate at the start of the year, reflecting slower ramp and schedule risk; the program will not reach the implied trajectory this fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: How are segment margins evolving versus FY24 (BFS above 20% now, healthcare low double-digit)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly segment movements are aberrations from ramp costs and that company margin is up from 11% eight quarters ago to 12.4%, with no systemic issue seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedge liability and forward book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the GBP book is typically 50-75% of committed year-one value and USD about 25%; GBP 61.6m and USD 119m are hedged for the next 12 months at blended rates of about 123-124 (GBP) and 94 (USD).

risks_watch: Healthcare payer exposure: Medicare Advantage program pacing under CMS rate changes, with healthcare Q1 revenue down 2% QoQ cc; management attributed this to pacing, not demand.

Recovery of INR357m (healthcare program termination) and INR284m (regulatory penalty indemnity, insurance claim) exceptional charges; both expensed on a prudence basis, with recovery timing not committed.
Ramp of new wins: management expects H2 FY27 to be strong, but wins are phased transformational deals, so revenue conversion timing is uncertain.

Europe and CMT volatility: Europe shift to offshore and nearshore, and CMT timing of work packets and Silicon Valley consumer tech program transitions; voluntary attrition at 27.5%.

532809|2026-09.headline: Firstsource Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR 28.3bn (12.3% constant currency), EBIT margin 12.5%; FY27 CC revenue guidance floor raised to 10.5%.
532809|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 3.7% QoQ in INR and 2% QoQ in constant currency, the 12th straight quarter of sequential growth, with EBIT margin at 12.5% (up 100 bps YoY, 10 bps QoQ) for an eighth straight quarter of expansion. Management signed four large deals (two from new logos) and added 17 new logos, including six strategic logos. Headcount rose by 3,062 to 39,937, largely from a major banking client transition and offshore/nearshore ramps. FY27 constant currency revenue guidance was narrowed upward to 10.5%-13% from 10%-13%, with the EBIT margin guidance of 12.25%-12.75% reaffirmed. Healthcare declined 2% QoQ, and the company is still pursuing recovery on the exceptional charge tied to two clients from last quarter.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY but declined 2% QoQ in constant currency (Q1 was +11% YoY), with four new logos. Management attributed the softness to Medicare Advantage scope recalibration after CMS rate changes and the wind-down of a transformative payer BPaaS engagement.

segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, with two new logos; management flagged quarter-to-quarter volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions.

segments.commentary: Grew 25% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, with two new logos; retail seasonal ramps expected in Q3 and part of Q4.

segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and 1% QoQ in constant currency; BFS led growth while healthcare reflected program ramp timing.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY and 7% QoQ in constant currency, led by BFS with CMT momentum; two large wins in the quarter.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 50% YoY, supported by existing relationships and an improving pipeline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guidance raised at the lower end to 10.5%-13% (earlier 10%-13%); upper end of 13% kept 'very much in play', dependent on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance reaffirmed at 12.25%-12.75%.
Management expects a 50-75 bps annual margin improvement to continue over the next couple of years, targeting a 14%-15% EBIT margin band within two to three years.
FY27 effective tax rate guided at 22%-24%.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1, citing large-deal ramps, the banking client transition, 17 new logos, and a healthy pipeline described as the best ever.

Wage increments: frontline and mid-level staff received hikes in Q2, senior staff in Q3; management said forecasts already reflect this and remain within guidance. Quantification was deferred to an offline follow-up.
capex_capacity: Headcount closed Q2 at 39,937, net addition of 3,062 QoQ; India and Philippines accounted for more than 85% of the increase, with South Africa also contributing.

Kairos platform capitalisation is work in progress; some directly attributable costs are capitalised. Intangible asset under development was INR 232 million; the capitalised Kairos cost figure was to be provided offline.

M&A philosophy: plug capability gaps (healthcare, retail, distribution access). Past deals cited: QBSS (~3 years ago, RCM mid-office), Ascensos (retail, ~2 years ago), TeleMedik (earlier in FY27, Puerto Rico footprint and clinical operations).
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5 million) signed in Q2, the seventh straight quarter of four or more; two from new logos. Management said the large-deal run rate has moved from about 2-3 per quarter historically to 4 and wants to reach 5-6.
51 clients above US$5 million run rate, six more QoQ, the largest sequential addition on an organic basis in five quarters; 23 clients in the US$10 million-plus cohort after adding three.
Top 5 and top 10 client revenue share fell by 6 and 10 percentage points respectively over eight quarters; management says top clients are growing at industry rate.
More than 50% of revenues are non-linear; management is working to increase that share through productised services.
Management said renewals with some scope deflation have been held revenue-neutral by adding new work in adjacent processes.
Hedge book as of 30 September 2026: GBP 69.2 million at an average INR 116.6 per pound and USD 68.5 million at an average INR 95.7 per dollar over the next 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be affected by furloughs or holidays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business runs continuous mission-critical operations, so it does not expect the furloughs typical of IT services.

qa_highlights.question: Is attrition structurally higher than peers, and is it by design?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said attrition is not comparable to IT services; BPO-type operations are in line with industry averages. Voluntary attrition for associates with more than 180 days of tenure was 28.4% on a trailing 12-month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be stronger than H1 given the Q1 contract termination?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management cited large-deal ramps, the banking client transition, 17 new logos and a healthy pipeline; this is why the lower end of guidance was raised to 10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Has the healthcare vertical bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some timing issues, including the payer BPaaS wind-down and Medicare Advantage scope changes, are behind it. It cited HR1 provider-side tailwinds and voice AI and Denials AI now in production at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is needed to lift large-deal wins above four per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs more pipeline, proactive deal shaping and creative commercial constructs; it is pushing the sales organisation to reach five or six.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin trajectory expected to evolve beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 50-75 bps annual expansion toward 14%-15%, with levers including right-shoring, automation, pricing, exit of loss-making accounts, talent cost and facility optimisation; some gains are reinvested in capabilities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the lower guidance band 2% QoQ, and what drives the upper end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the floor reflects line of sight from H1 visibility, while the 13% upper end depends on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next two to three months.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI affecting deal sizes and decision cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-driven share-of-wallet expansion can lead to larger ACVs; Kairos intelligent context framework is attached to about 50% of the top 50 clients and has shortened some cycles, with one case going live in 8 weeks.

risks_watch: Healthcare sequential decline (-2% QoQ) continues after the payer BPaaS wind-down and Medicare Advantage scope changes; recovery depends on HR1 provider-side ramps from January 2027.

H2 acceleration depends on phased transformation programmes hitting milestones and on pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months; the upper end of guidance is conditional.
Wage increments for senior staff in Q3 and continued onboarding ahead of revenue could pressure margins; quantified impact was not given.
AI-driven deal deflation and elongated decision cycles, which management says are offset by share-of-wallet gains.
Capitalisation of Kairos costs and the carrying value (INR 232 million under development) were not fully disclosed on the call.

We are actively engaged with them on recovery and we remain optimistic about the outcome.

532810|2026-03.headline: PFC FY26 standalone PAT hit a record INR 20,051 crore (+16% YoY), but FY27 spread guided lower at 2.40-2.50% and loan growth at ~10%.
532810|2026-03.overview: PFC reported its highest-ever standalone net profit of INR 20,051 crore for FY26, up 16% YoY, helped by 13% NII growth and about INR 1,800 crore of provision reversals. Net NPA fell to 0.13% and net credit-impaired ratio to a new low of 0.15%, after resolution of Sinnar Thermal and TRN Energy. Disbursements were INR 1,65,414 crore and loan book grew about 7% to ~INR 5.8 lakh crore, with management blaming elevated prepayments in a falling-rate cycle. Management guided FY27 spread to 2.40-2.50% and loan growth to around 10%, and outlined the proposed PFC-REC merger targeted for 1 April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: of which ~INR 800 crore from Sinnar/TRN resolution, ~INR 1,000 crore from DISCOM ECL reversal

financial_highlights.metric: Yield / cost of funds / spread / NIM FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 18.55 per share total; final INR 3.95

segments.name: Renewables
segments.commentary: Group renewable book INR 1.65 lakh crore; PFC standalone renewables about 16% of lending. Major FY26 disbursements were hybrid solar-wind; ~INR 16,000 crore sanctioned for battery and pumped storage.

segments.name: Conventional generation
segments.commentary: About 50% of PFC lending now generation, of which 16% renewable and balance conventional (down from ~75% historically). Thermal and nuclear expansion cited as emerging opportunities.

segments.name: Distribution (DISCOMs)
segments.commentary: Lending focused on short- and medium-term DISCOM needs; RBPF short-tenor revolving loans fell as DISCOMs shifted to 3-7 year loans. DISCOM ECL provision reversal of ~INR 1,000 crore on improved ratings; AT&C losses 15.04%; DISCOMs posted first all-India PAT of ~INR 2,700 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 spread guided to 2.40%-2.50% (FY26 actual 2.46%), reflecting yield pressure from competitive pricing and forex-driven funding cost.
FY27 loan growth target around 10%; management says without FY26 prepayments growth would have been within the 10-11% guided range.
Management does not expect further RBI rate cuts in FY27 (repo held at 5.25%); expects prepayment pressure to moderate.
PFC-REC merger targeted to take effect 1 April 2027, subject to MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet and presidential approvals; government to retain government-company status.
Dividend to follow DIPAM policy of 30% of profit, subject to RBI NBFC dividend rules.
No specific FY27 disbursement guidance; FY26 sanctions INR 2.85 lakh crore with only ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed, so spillover expected.
capex_capacity: India installed capacity crossed 530 GW; about 55 GW non-fossil capacity added in FY26, a record (per management).
Peak power demand hit an all-time high of 256 GW in April 2026.
PFC sanctioned ~INR 16,000 crore cumulatively for battery and pumped storage projects.
Sanctioned-but-undisbursed pool estimated at INR 2.5-3 lakh crore (approximate, per management).
Infrastructure disbursements slow in construction phase; pick-up expected as projects approach commissioning.
demand_pricing: PFC consciously priced new lending competitively in FY26 amid banks' aggressive refinancing of commissioned renewable assets, which drove prepayments.
Banks most willing to refinance renewable portfolios given low gestation, early commissioning, certain cash flows and small ticket sizes.

Forex volatility (rupee depreciation vs USD and EUR, Middle East conflict, trade tariffs) raised FY26 funding costs; hedging covers 97% of USD 10.3 billion foreign currency borrowing, with management saying most mark-to-market losses are notional until maturity.
Borrowing mix: 80:20 domestic-foreign; 65% fixed-rate; 60% bonds, 20% bank term loans, 20% foreign currency (per management).
Repayments from borrowers in FY26 were about INR 1,28,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did disbursements and loan growth weaken despite stable disbursement volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said disbursements were broadly flat (INR 1,65,414 crore vs ~INR 1,68,000 crore) but DISCOMs shifted from short-tenor RBPF revolving loans (~6-month average) to 3-7 year loans, reducing rollover-driven disbursement counts; competition from banks also present.

qa_highlights.question: Why is only a fraction of sanctions disbursed and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sanctions were ~INR 2.85 lakh crore with ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed; infrastructure disbursements are slow due to pre-commitment conditions, environmental and land approvals, and pick up near commissioning. Management said the balance is spilling over, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How will the merger affect the government shareholding and borrowing limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Government shareholding would fall to about 41-42% post share swap; management said the government has committed to keep the merged entity a government company, with modalities yet to be decided. Single-borrower exposure limit to banks would fall from 25% to 20% for the merged entity, which management does not see as a challenge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend and ROE outlook post-merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 30% of PFC's standalone profit, of which PFC receives REC dividend as income; post-merger dividend will be declared on combined profit under DIPAM's 30% policy, subject to RBI rules. No ROE guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does PFC view the impact of a potential future rate hike?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% of borrowings are fixed-rate and bond liabilities average 5-6 years, so repricing is gradual; lending rates are linked to the weighted cost of borrowing, so a rate rise would transmit slowly as older debt matures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 spread decline and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 2.40-2.50% versus 2.46% in FY26, citing competitive lending rates, prepayment pressure and forex-driven funding costs; the spread is calculated on weighted average cost including foreign borrowings.

risks_watch: Continued prepayments and bank refinancing of commissioned renewable assets could keep loan growth below the ~10% target.
Rupee volatility and Middle East conflict could raise hedging and translation costs on USD 10.3 billion foreign borrowing; ~97% hedged.
Shiga Energy (INR 522 crore) co-lender approval pending within the INR 854 crore of Stage-3 assets resolved outside NCLT.
Stage-3 book of INR 6,323 crore across 19 projects; FY26 provision write-backs (~INR 1,800 crore) will not recur at the same level, so credit cost may rise.
Merger execution: government stake falling below 50%, creditor exposure limits, and workforce integration (about 520 PFC and about 1,000 combined employees per management).
New ECL norms from April 2027 under RBI; management says current policy broadly in sync with RBI IRAC norms.

532811|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover rose 8.76% to INR1,322.30 crores but PAT fell 3.63% to INR80.14 crores; FY27 growth guided at 15-20%.
532811|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 turnover grew 8.76% YoY to INR1,322.30 crores, while PAT declined 3.63% to INR80.14 crores and EBITDA margin compressed to 9.35% from 10.17%. For FY26, turnover rose 11.38% to INR4,565.20 crores and PAT rose 31.17% to INR264.32 crores, with EBITDA margin at 9.52% versus 8.34%. Management blamed Q4 on labour flight from NCR and Bengal/Assam elections, NGT construction bans, a cash crunch in Assam, and war-driven LPG, fuel and supply-chain disruption. The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, with an order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, but gave no formal PAT guidance.

segments.name: Central Vista (EPC, design-build, INR2,600-3,000 crores)
segments.commentary: Awarded 14 January 2026; Nirman Bhawan demolished and excavation/concrete started. Management targets about INR1,000 crores of FY27 execution, with a turnover run-rate of INR100-150 crores per month.

segments.name: CSMT Mumbai (order value INR2,076 crores ex-GST)
segments.commentary: Designs now approved and execution has picked up after a slow 1.5 years. FY27 execution target is about INR600 crores.

segments.name: Dahlias (private)
segments.commentary: FY27 execution target about INR400 crores.

segments.name: IJPM - India Jewellery Park (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Design changes ongoing; ground work expected to start in the last month of Q1 FY27 after the Mumbai monsoon. FY27 target kept modest at about INR100 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%, up from the 10-15% guidance given in prior years.
EBITDA margin expected to reach double digits in FY27 (currently 9.5% in FY26); management said margins will rise over the next two years as mechanisation takes effect.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, including two L1 positions worth INR1,620.95 crores (RML Hospital Delhi and an Odisha government university project in Bhubaneswar).
FY27 capex about INR300 crores, down from an earlier guidance of about INR500 crores; FY26 capex was about INR274 crores.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very slow due to elections, labour exodus and Eid; ramp-up from Q2 and H2 significantly above H1.
Management said no guidance is prudent beyond FY27 given headwinds; a FY28 number was not given. Share buyback 'not in the offing'.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR274 crores; FY27 capex planned at about INR300 crores, with depreciation rising in line.

Mechanisation (tower cranes, passenger hoists costing INR50-70 lakh each, batching plants, concrete pumps) is the stated response to labour shortage. Management estimated the IRR uplift at 7-10% and payback at 4-5 years on equipment with a 4-year life; other assets have a 7-8 year life.
Q4 depreciation was about INR29 crores; management expects a similar run-rate going forward.
Management is evaluating precast and pre-engineered building technologies, but said these would take 2-3 years to be used on projects.
demand_pricing: Government vs private mix is targeted at roughly half and half. Private clients were over 60% of the order book, per an analyst's read.
Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book; 89% of orders have built-in escalation clauses.
Government contracts use WPI-linked escalation with about a one-quarter lag; private contracts pass through volatile materials (cement, steel, grit, sand) roughly month-on-month.
Management is walking away from some projects, including with existing clients, and is raising bid margins by a couple of percentage points or more.
Pipeline has been slowed by the war, with developers delaying launches. The company is bidding selectively with existing or well-funded clients.
Competitors named: L&T, B&F, Nagarjuna, Shapoorji Pallonji, Kalpataru and Tata Projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will execution ramp up in FY27-28, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth guided at 15-20% and order inflow target about INR8,000 crores. FY28 was not guided; management said FY28 is 'similar' and gave no firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and depreciation rising while margins lag, and is this a new normal?

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and fuel-price increases being protected against?

532811|2026-06.headline: Ahluwalia Q1 FY27 PAT fell 77.65% to INR11.42 crore on 4.29% EBITDA margin, as AIIMS Jammu bill cut and NCR labour cost spike hit margins; FY27 double-digit margin ruled out.

Net order book stands at INR20,663.52 crore, with only INR512.81 crore of inflow in FY27 to date. Management guided to 12-15% top-line growth but ruled out double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, and did not give a firm date for margin recovery.

532814|2026-03.headline: Indian Bank Q4 FY26: Q4 net profit Rs 3,103 crore (+1.3% QoQ), FY26 profit Rs 12,156 crore (+11.33%), gross NPA cut to 1.98%.
532814|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a decent year, beating guidance on most parameters except cost-to-income, with advances up 13.43% led by RAM (+15.18%) and corporate growth reviving to 9.19%. Gross NPA fell 111 bps to 1.98% and annualised Q4 slippage eased to 0.85%, while NIM for the year declined 17 bps to 3.24%. Management guided FY27 to tighter NIM (3.10%-3.25%), ROA (1.20%-1.30%) and growth (advances 11%-13%), citing rising cost of deposits and lower treasury income. ECL impact was not quantified; management said it would be absorbed over one to three quarters and that the final guidelines were received only the day before the call.

IND Optima cash management launched with 150-plus corporate customers onboarded.
Digital pipeline: corporate CRM, corporate ecosystem engine, RFP creator, invoice processing, intelligent document reader, IND UPI app upgrade, and automated suspicious transaction reporting.
Digital and IT budget to be roughly equivalent to employee cost, per Ashutosh Choudhury.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the bank for the final ECL guidelines, and how large is the hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final guidelines came the day before and impact will be a little higher than draft estimates, adding the HTM book is now included. It declined to give a number yet, saying it would give concrete figures later, and expects the impact to be absorbed over one to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia war and tariffs raise slippages? What about SMA trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 slippage rose on about Rs 400-500 crore of March MOC, which recurs each March. SMA fell mainly because two government accounts left SMA-2; management also said some stress has been present since tariffs in August but is not visible in SMA.

qa_highlights.question: How will treasury income trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said treasury will be lower but not as severe as last year, since securities have not been sold at low yields. It expects Rs 1,000-1,200 crore of treasury profit for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank measuring the revenue benefit of digital investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits are real but not quantified; cited 94% digital transactions (branch visits cost at least 5x more), and said it will try to quantify going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What levers exist on the asset side if cost of deposits rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said few levers remain since about 50% of loans are external-benchmark linked; MCLR-linked loans may reprice up. It is focusing on mid-sized corporates of Rs 50-500 crore for better pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and why is it so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Average LCR was 127% (currently 123%-124%). Management said 115%-120% is a fair operating level and that excess SLR holdings support the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AFS reserve movement?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS reserve moved from about Rs 400 crore in December to minus Rs 200 crore in March, per management.

532822|2026-06.headline: Vodafone Idea posted its first positive net subscriber addition since merger in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 6.0% YoY to Rs 11,689 Crore and Cash EBITDA up 13.5% to Rs 2,475 Crore.

segments.commentary: Net additions reportedly doubled over the last year; a dominant position in connected car IoT was cited. Management gave no subscriber breakup, but said M2M was a major driver of Q1 net adds.

532827|2026-03.headline: Page Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.1% to INR12,526 million on 10.8% volume growth; FY26 EBITDA margin 22%, guided to 19-21% for FY27.
532827|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 14.1% YoY to INR12,526 million, with volume up 10.8% to 54.5 million pieces and PAT up 9% to INR1,787 million. Management attributed the pickup to better consumer sentiment, a correction in distributor inventory that aligned secondary and primary sales, and product upgrades, with March the strongest month. EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the quarter and 22% for FY26, but management guided to a 19-21% range for FY27 citing marketing normalising to 5% of sales, input cost inflation and technology investments. Price increases were small: a 2% weighted average taken in January on product enhancements, with a further price increase planned in Q1 FY27 to cover input costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp volume acceleration to double digits, and what initiatives contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better consumer demand in Q4 and recovery in athleisure after distributor inventory correction. Primary and secondary sales are now closely aligned, and March was strong. Management said upstocking was not encouraged and festive timing played little role.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 19-21% EBITDA margin range still hold after input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated 19-21% for FY27, citing marketing at 5%, gross margin levels and salary costs as the basis. FY26 margin was higher because marketing was below 5% and gross margin held up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 margin 22% and why should it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 benefited from marketing below 5% of sales and sustained gross margin. Normal marketing at 5% plus input inflation will pressure EBITDA, though not to the 22% level.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2% price increase cover raw material inflation, and will there be more price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2% increase was for product enhancements, not inflation. A Q1 FY27 price increase is planned to cover input costs, with the pass-through share still undecided. Management said it would absorb costs if volumes were at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes hurt volume elasticity in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to price only to the extent volumes are unaffected and would rather absorb cost temporarily in margin than cut volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of market share in economic segment and the new product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product upgrades launched in Q3 and Q4 were well received. Groove 3 is being extended to about 500 EBOs, select MBOs and e-commerce, and the men's Bonded collection outdoor campaign launched around 20 May.

qa_highlights.question: Are digital-first brands taking share, and is distribution friction behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce has grown for 3-4 years and Jockey ranks number one on major platforms in core categories. Auto replenishment has settled in for about 2.5 years, and a new distribution management system is being rolled out over the next year.

532832|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 presales hit record INR2,632 crores (+89% QoQ), but FY26 reported PAT was a loss of INR872 crores on revenue-recognition timing and merger accounting.
532832|2026-03.overview: Embassy Developments posted record Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores and FY26 presales of INR4,631 crores (+128% YoY), with 93% of the INR5,000 crore guidance achieved. FY26 collections were INR1,673 crores, slightly below FY25's INR1,852 crores, which management attributed to the lag from H2-weighted presales. Reported FY26 revenue fell to INR1,732 crores and PAT swung to a loss of INR872 crores, which management framed as structural (completion-based revenue recognition and reverse-merger fair value step-up). FY27 guidance is INR6,000 crores own presales (plus INR2,000 crores from DM projects), INR3,000 crores collections and about INR19,400 crores of new launch GDV. Two legal overhangs (CIRP petition and KIADB resumption order) were resolved, and the ASM framework exit took effect 6 May 2026.

532832|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 presales rose 338% YoY to INR868 crore and collections 54% to INR496 crore, but revenue fell to INR217 crore and net loss widened to INR234 crore.
532832|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR868 crore (up 338% YoY) and collections of INR496 crore (up 54% YoY) led the quarter, while no new projects were launched in Q1 by design. Reported revenue from operations fell to INR217 crore from INR681 crore, EBITDA was negative INR106 crore, and net loss widened to INR234 crore from INR166 crore, as revenue is recognised only on completion and handover. Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore; management expects collections to pick up from Q2 as launches from H2 FY26 hit milestones. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore owned presales, INR2,000 crore DM presales and about INR3,000 crore collections, and a promoter warrant issue at INR111.51 to repay Embassy Group's INR363 crore shareholder debt.

segments.name: Residential (owned development)
segments.commentary: Presales INR868 crore in Q1; ongoing portfolio of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; OC-received inventory about 98% cumulatively sold. Construction spend INR276 crore, about 56% of collections.

segments.name: Development management (DM)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza (Juhu) received RERA approval just before the call and is slated for Q2 launch; FY27 DM presales guidance INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Embassy East Business Park is under excavation and may be held as an annuity asset or sold near completion. Embassy Knowledge Park commercial product is in early planning, with timelines targeted by end-FY27; not included in GDV.

FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crore reiterated; management says it could be bettered, with more clarity by Q3.

FY27 launch pipeline: 11 projects, GDV about INR19,400 crore (9 owned, INR13,300 crore; 2 DM, INR6,000-plus crore). Four to launch in Q2 (Embassy One North tower, Embassy Knowledge Park villas and apartments, Juhu DM project); the rest targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.
Management expects a cash-flow inflection around mid-calendar 2027 (April-May) as slab cycles start on Greenshore, Verde and Citadel.

Some Gurgaon landlords have asked about the Indiabulls association; management says the entities are separate and that this is a slow-to-resolve perception issue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Bangalore launch delays (as at Prestige) also affecting Embassy, and can the other 5 Bangalore projects launch within FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 non-launch to choice, not approvals; Embassy One North was pushed to Q2 after the Four Seasons branding was dropped. Knowledge Park villas and apartments are targeted for Q2, and Bangalore projects are targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given EBITDA of negative INR106 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore because no launches occurred in Q1; collections from Q3-Q4 FY26 launches should accelerate from Q2. Cash balance started FY27 at about INR1,165 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR19,400 crore GDV split between H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: The four Q2 launches (North tower, Knowledge Park, Juhu DM, plus Embassy One already launched) are in H1; the remaining projects are targeted for Q3, possibly Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average cost of debt and the cost of the Blackstone debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is about 14%. Blackstone debt accrues at 18%, added to the gross debt rather than paid out; management is in talks to convert the Blackstone portion to equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why the promoter warrant issue if the promoter debt is accruing rather than paid in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it brings no new liquidity; it is a confidence signal, priced at INR111.51 (the earlier pre-merger price), and the Embassy Group debt (growing at over 15%) will be cleared. Warrants will convert within 6 months, versus the 18-month maximum.

qa_highlights.question: Can collections of INR3,000 crore be achieved without new launches, and what is the collection schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Most collections are expected from already-launched projects (Greenshore, Verde, Eden). Launches in Q2 and Q3 are expected to yield 10-20% collected in the quarter; management is confident of the INR3,000 crore.

532832|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales hit a record Rs 3,225 crore, but revenue fell to Rs 292 crore and EBITDA was negative Rs 131 crore.
532832|2026-09.overview: Embassy Developments reported record Q2 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 3,225 crore, lifting H1 pre-sales to Rs 4,093 crore, and collections rose 10% QoQ to about Rs 546 crore. Reported financials remained weak: revenue from operations was Rs 292 crore (vs Rs 494 crore a year ago), EBITDA was negative Rs 131 crore and loss after tax was Rs 271 crore, which management attributed to legacy projects and the project completion method. Three launches in the quarter carried a combined GDV of Rs 8,397 crore against a pre-launch estimate of Rs 7,500 crore. CEO Sachin Shah announced he will step down on December 31, 2026, with Aditya Virwani becoming MD and CEO from January 1, 2027.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Embassy Riverine (GDV Rs 3,155 crore) and South Reserve (GDV Rs 1,957 crore) at Embassy Origins; combined sales exceeded Rs 1,800 crore within two weeks, with Riverine at Rs 933 crore and South Reserve at Rs 880 crore. Management cited a 93% EOI-to-booking conversion over those two weeks.

segments.name: Mumbai (MMR)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza, Juhu (GDV about Rs 3,285 crore) sold Rs 758 crore shortly after launch, including a single Rs 711 crore residence. Embassy Citadel, Worli, crossed Rs 1,350 crore of sales in under nine months; approvals secured for all 81 floors.

segments.name: Projects nearing completion
segments.commentary: Golf City Savroli received OC for remaining towers in Q2 FY27; OC-received portfolio is over 95% sold by area. Embassy Paradiso is fully sold, with OC slated in FY27. Embassy Edge and East Avenue are about 90% sold, targeting FY28 completion.

segments.name: Park Panvel (legacy Indiabulls)
segments.commentary: 17 towers, about 8 million sq ft, with about Rs 500 crore invested so far and Rs 40 crore monthly burn. First two towers expected to get OC around June 2027. Sold receivables plus inventory about Rs 1,800 crore; management estimates a surplus of Rs 300-400 crore after construction and interest.
