FY27 pre-sales target of Rs 8,000 crore: Rs 6,000 crore from owned projects and Rs 2,000 crore from DM projects.
FY27 collections target of about Rs 3,000 crore; management expects to reach it over the next two quarters (H2 FY27), with about Rs 2,000 crore needed.
Management expects positive operating cash flow by end-March 2027.
Debt expected to start declining around end-Q2 or Q3 FY28 (about this time next year), once collections exceed capex and overheads.
Revenue guidance for next year to be given in Q3 or Q4 FY27 once completion dates are firm; RERA dates have been replaced with completion dates, to be updated every six months.
Launch mix for Q3 and Q4 FY27 to be spread evenly, with Q4 likely to carry a larger share; some launches timed to avoid the mid-December to mid-January market slowdown.
capex_capacity: Owned portfolio: 13 projects with total GDV above Rs 27,422 crore, 55% of area sold (excluding DM projects).
Cumulative sold receivables plus unsold inventory of about Rs 25,536 crore: sold receivables Rs 8,290 crore and unsold inventory Rs 17,246 crore.

Development pipeline beyond FY27 of 20.3 million sq ft with estimated GDV of about Rs 23,470 crore; fully paid land bank of 3,251 acres, including 1,400 acres at Nashik under MIDC resolution and debonding.
Sky Terraces (DM project) targeted for launch in Q4 FY27, delayed by the pending GBA meeting; Sky Terraces sits under the Rs 2,000 crore DM target.
Embassy Citadel, Worli: approvals for all 81 floors; completion in FY33.
Panvel: about 2,000 laborers on site; OC for the first towers from around June 2027, with phased completion after that.
demand_pricing: Pricing: management says Panvel market rate is about Rs 15,000 per sq ft versus its current 12,000-13,000, and it is deliberately pacing sales at Embassy Origins to keep taking prices up.
Eight recent launches (Riverine, South Reserve, Terazza, Verde Phase 2, Greenshore, Eden, Paradiso, Citadel) are over 52% sold by area within six months of launch.
Launches are concentrated in Bangalore, MMR and NCR; Ketan Nanda hired as Business Head for North and Alok Sherry as Head of Business Development for Mumbai.
Management says buyers are mainly end-users in Bangalore; Worli sales were achieved without sample flats or a sales office on site.
Competition and market pricing were not discussed in detail beyond the Panvel and Mumbai commentary.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections reach Rs 3,000 crore in H2, and when will debt fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is picking up and it is confident of hitting the Rs 3,000 crore collections guidance over the next two quarters. Debt is expected to decline around this time next year, once collections exceed capex and overheads.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the Rs 11,900 crore of launches planned for Q3 and Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Launches will be spread quite evenly, with Q4 likely to have a larger share. Some projects with RERA approval may be formally launched only after mid-January, as the market softens in December.

qa_highlights.question: What has been invested in the Indiabulls revival projects, and what is the Panvel timeline and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 500 crore has gone into Panvel, which consumes about Rs 40 crore a month. Panvel has 17 towers and about 8 million sq ft, with OC starting around June 2027. Realisation is about Rs 1,800 crore with upside, and surplus is estimated at Rs 300-400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kaimal said operating cash flow is expected to turn positive by end-March 2027, as slab-cycle collections from Q3 and Q4 FY26 launches come through.

qa_highlights.question: Why are losses increasing, and when will the balance sheet improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current P&L reflects legacy projects started before the merger. Reverse-merger goodwill is tested for impairment every six months. Cash surplus is about Rs 30,000 crore over the next 3-4 years. Net debt to equity should start improving from next year.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Blackstone Rs 700 crore debt be converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still in discussion with Blackstone but will not convert at current prices, calling it extremely dilutive given the stock trades well below book value.

qa_highlights.question: Can a delay in Sky Terraces hit the Rs 8,000 crore pre-sales target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not, citing Juhu over-performance (about Rs 800 crore already) and Rs 25,000-26,000 crore of stock available to sell.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nashik land monetisation status?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage: the MIDC issues and land debonding must be resolved first. Data-centre use is being explored because a neighbouring 1,350 MW power plant could supply up to 950 MW.

532834|2026-03.headline: Camlin Q4 FY26 revenue about INR424 crores and EBITDA INR21 crores (5% margin), hit by a roughly 20% quarterly sales shortfall from shipping and war-related disruption.
532834|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was weak: management said sales were hit by about 20% from shipment delays, freight shortages and longer transit times linked to the Middle East conflict. Revenue was about INR424 crores in the quarter, with total revenue of INR1,723 crores after moving discontinued operations out. EBITDA was INR21 crores (5%), with vanillin sales largely from channel stock and Blends growth of 17%, short of the 20% target. Management said FY27 guidance is unchanged: revenue INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin 12-14%. The CFS Europe liquidation produced a gain of about INR100 crores and removes ongoing cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year.

financial_highlights.change: about INR53 crores lower after discontinued-business reclassification

financial_highlights.metric: Gain from discontinued operations (CFS Europe derecognition)
financial_highlights.value: about INR85 crores in PBT, about INR100 crores gain on loss of control as stated

financial_highlights.change: 18% including discontinued Blends business in Europe; target was about 20%

financial_highlights.change: up about INR50 crores YoY; Italian loans of about INR85 crores knocked out

segments.name: Straights (TBHQ, BHA and others)
segments.commentary: Management said market share was held, but revenue fell on local competition and pricing pressure. Some Straights volume is being shifted into Blends. TBHQ prices have corrected upward and BHA is slightly above pre-war levels.

segments.name: Blends (incl. Vinpai and Vitafor)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth was 17% against a 20% target. Vinpai ran at about INR17 crores over three months against an expected INR10 crores a month. Management guides Blends to upwards of INR1,400 crores in FY27, with Vinpai and Vitafor each at roughly 14-16 million (USD) and above EBITDA breakeven in FY27.

segments.name: Vanillin (methyl and ethyl)
segments.commentary: Methyl production stopped from 15 January for conversion to ethyl vanillin; Q4 sales came mainly from internal US channel stock. Ethyl orders of about 300 tonnes are on hand for Q1, with a 600-tonne ethyl campaign planned. FY27 US volume is guided at 2,200-2,400 tonnes, and Europe at 1,500-1,600 tonnes.

segments.name: Diphenol (hydroquinone and catechol)
segments.commentary: Diphenol production was discontinued on 22 May. Phenol rose from about INR85 to above INR150/kg, and about 3,000 tonnes of catechol stock covers 8-9 months of vanillin output. Hydroquinone will be imported from China.

segments.name: CFS Europe and China
segments.commentary: CFS Europe was liquidated, and its cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year ends from next quarter. China is still in liquidation, with costs expected at INR7-8 crores next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin at 12-14%; management said guidance is not changing.
FY27 blended vanillin realisation expected at about $13.5-14/kg after tariffs, with US tariff at 15.5% (5.5% base plus 10%).
Q1 FY27 vanillin realisation expected to rise over Q4; gross margin guided to hold at about 48%, give or take 1%.
Q1 FY27 combined US and Europe vanillin sales expected to grow over Q4 FY26; Q1 EBITDA said to be hard to call, with the full diphenol-discontinuation impact in Q2.
Vinpai and Vitafor expected above EBITDA breakeven in FY27; Blends guided to upwards of INR1,400 crores.
Management said a stable 10-15% growth over the next two quarters would be great, citing elevated freight and feedstock costs.
Anticipated US tariff refund of about INR9-10 crores (about 50% cash, 50% duty adjustment, per management) on duties paid until February.
Repayment of about INR60-70 crores in FY27; equity raise described as a last resort, with structured or bank debt being pursued.
capex_capacity: A fire on Saturday (about 23 May) at the Dahej plant was contained, with no spread to the whole plant; insurance cover is adequate, but there will be some loss.
Diphenol plant shut on 22 May; management is evaluating repurposing it into a multipurpose facility to cut raw material costs.
Methyl-to-ethyl vanillin conversion took about 2 months, and ethyl vanillin production has started. Methyl production resumed in April.
FY27 vanillin volume at 70% utilisation implies about 4,000-4,200 tonnes, with the gap of about 1,000 tonnes to be sourced as catechol or guaiacol from China.
Management said the company has increased its authorised capital in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Vanillin: Syensqo is pricing DDP US at about $17-18/kg; Camlin's net realisation is about $13 after holding, tariff and financing costs. Management expects Syensqo to raise prices to $19-20 once its capacity reaches 100%.

Raw materials: phenol rose from about INR85 to above INR150/kg. Total raw material cost was about $7.5/kg before the war and is now about $9/kg; caustic has about doubled and freight to the Americas is about three times the pre-war cost.
Logistics: shipments that were expected in 20 days now take 40-50 days, and management expects it to take about a quarter for normalisation.
Management said demand for 4,000 tonnes of vanillin is achievable; the bigger constraints are working capital, logistics and cash flow.
Management did not expect the EBITDA impact of the conflict to be resolved quickly; it estimated sales were hit by about INR50 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vanillin volumes reach only about 320 tonnes in Q4 when about 650 tonnes was held in the channel?

Ratings revenue reached INR 336 crore in FY26 (12.4% CAGR since FY21) with operating margin of 37.6%. Risk & Analytics (non-Ratings) revenue rose to INR 313 crore in FY26 from INR 114.9 crore five years earlier, but its quarterly run-rate has been flat at about INR 80 crore for the last few quarters, and margin is compressing as BankTech and CapTech gain mix. 532843|2026-03.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
532843|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

Doctor poaching described as ongoing but not a major concern; ESOP scheme is broad-based across zones, covering roughly 55-60% doctors and administrative staff.
Diagnostics market described as competitive; management acknowledged muted or stagnant growth in prior periods due to rebranding, and the Agilus CEO (recently joined) is reworking plans.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP charge for FY27 and the next two years, and can consolidated margin improve by 100 bps in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% margin target pre- or post-ESOP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 25% target now aspires to be achieved after ESOP cost, expected in about two years, with levers including ramp-up of new units (from -0.4% drag to +1%), new doctor teams, lower legal costs and recovery of doubtful debt provisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Manesar and Greater Noida margins below 10%, and when will they reach 20%?

qa_highlights.question: Diagnostics growth lags industry; what are the challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: The Agilus CEO, in role about 10 days, said the company is reworking plans; B2C mix target rises to 55% and then 58%, and the company cited a rebrand and lab-network rationalisation affecting growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oncology slowdown and is it chemo-driven?

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance and are acquisitions expected?

qa_highlights.question: What are diagnostics margin and growth expectations for the rest of the year?

532843|2026-09.headline: Fortis Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR 2,735 crore, with operating EBITDA pre-ESOP up 19.2% to INR 663 crore.
532843|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 2,735 crore in Q2 FY27, up 17.3% YoY, driven by the hospital business (up 18.6% to INR 2,340 crore). Operating EBITDA pre-ESOP was INR 663 crore at a 24.2% margin, up from 23.9%. Diagnostics (Agilus) grew more slowly at 12.2% on gross revenue, and management said it expects 12-13% growth for FY27. Management declined to guide FY28 margins, citing drug price capping on 137 oncology drugs, and guided FY27 post-ESOP margin to be flat at around 22%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)

qa_highlights.question: Why are Punjab and Mumbai growing slower, and is Fortis lagging listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Punjab is capacity-constrained, with about 500+ beds coming from Amritsar and Mohali expansions; other clusters are growing fast. He declined to compare with competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangalore occupancy low and why buy a small 110-bed hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small community hospitals complement larger flagships in a cluster. Bannerghatta Road is about 58% occupied, and TMI Yeshwanthpur is still ramping up. Suguna was bought via direct negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the 2,000 beds and the committed capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the 2,000 beds are completed acquisitions and brownfield expansions, excluding Gleneagles and the 400-bed Delhi greenfield. Committed capex is about INR 3,500 crore over 3-3.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What returns hurdle does Fortis apply to acquisitions, and how is capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved benchmark is IRR of at least 15% and payback within 8-10 years, though strategic factors can override. IHH may take its stake above 50%, which could bring about INR 10,000 crore at current prices; management says capital is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins and guidance be revised given drug-price capping?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said FY27 margin should be flattish at about 22% post-ESOP, with no FY28 guidance until the impact of the drug circular is clear. He reaffirmed that FY29 25% guidance holds if there is no impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for diagnostics growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vijender Singh said FY27 growth is expected at 12-13%, with mid-teens growth in a few quarters, then industry growth. Brand transition impact is largely behind them.

532851|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR2,140 crores while PAT slipped to INR139 crores on a INR9 crore deferred tax charge; Q4 grew about 19%.
532851|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of resilience, with full-year revenue up about 7% to INR2,140 crores, gross profit up about 5% to INR675 crores, and EBITDA up about 3% to INR227 crores. PAT fell slightly from INR142 crores to INR139 crores, which management attributed to a roughly INR9 crore increase in deferred tax. Q4 revenue grew about 19%, with premium products up about 24%, but May was sluggish and the company is waiting for monsoon rains. Management guided to positive top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, with the first quarter as the first visible test, while raw material inflation of nearly 10% or more supports pricing.

demand_pricing: Industry: geopolitical tension has created supply constraints; raw material prices rose by nearly 10% and more for crude-linked products, shifting the market to a supplier-driven environment.
Two price increases were taken in April; the first was well received, but the second needed discounts in May. A June price increase is under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from its approximately INR800 crore inventory as raw material prices rise, given smaller competitors may lack stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed, saying the company plans from Diwali to Holi and bought stock before the price rise; the benefit depends on converting that stock into sales as the kharif season starts in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of volume and value growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volume grew 5% and value 14%; FY26 volume grew 5% and value 2%.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle target is 120 days from 140-150 days, which management called achievable. Management internally targets a 25-30% cut in finance cost; the FY26 consolidated finance cost was INR16.87 crores against INR6.86 crores in FY25, driven by higher inventory, bank limit use and INR94 crores of new-product investment.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kaeros positioned against the Tractor/IIL brand and the partner products?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros will run a parallel distribution network with its own brand and a sales-only team. It is positioned as a follower to IIL, which gets first access to partnership products from Corteva, Nissan and OAT. Kaeros is not positioned as a cheaper brand; it will sell at a 2-3% initial discount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of premium products and can it reach 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C. Management targets 60-70% in four years, so 70% will take three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D success rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said success rates vary: about 9,000-10,000 molecules screened a year, with a dozen trial teams testing 500-600 products to yield roughly 10-15 launches. Reverse engineering has higher success rates. The first Indian patent filing is pending IUPAC name approval.

532851|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12% YoY to INR612 crore as volume dropped about 13% on a delayed monsoon; gross margin rose to 31.6%.

Gross profit fell 4% to INR193.16 crore, but gross margin widened from 29% to 31.6%, which management linked to premium mix and inventory effects amid volatile raw material prices. EBITDA margin fell from 12.2% to 11.1% and PAT margin from 8.4% to 7.2%. Management said the season was deferred rather than lost and expects stronger execution over the remaining three quarters, but declined to give revised FY27 targets until after H1.

532853|2026-03.headline: Asahi Songwon Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 30.2% YoY to Rs 23 crore, with margin at 15.6% on price pass-through in Blue pigments.
532853|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 144 crore, up 19.4% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 23 crore (15.6% margin vs 8.58% in Q3 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25) and PAT of Rs 10.82 crore. For FY26, revenue fell 4.78% to Rs 535.48 crore while PAT rose 5.48% to Rs 17.78 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to raw-material price pass-through and operational efficiencies in Blue pigments, with a small inventory gain, and said the API price decline of the prior three years has reversed. Gokul Jaykrishna handed day-to-day CEO duties to his son Arjun Jaykrishna, while remaining Managing Director.

segments.name: Blue pigment (standalone, ATC Dahej)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability improved QoQ on stronger realisation with modest volume growth. Gross margin rose to about 34% from about 29% QoQ; management cited price pass-through, operating efficiencies and a marginal inventory gain. Management said utilisation is about 80-85% and no capex is planned for capacity.

segments.name: AZO pigments (subsidiary ATC)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive and cash break-even reached. FY26 revenue Rs 78 crore with PBT loss of Rs 2.42 crore; management expects PBT break-even in FY27. Capacity is 2,400 tpa, utilisation about 65% per management, with a planned Rs 10-15 crore brownfield expansion to about 1.5x once utilisation reaches 75-85%.

segments.name: API (subsidiary Atlas, Chattral plant)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive. Volumes grew about 18% CAGR over three years, but realisations fell 40-45% since acquisition; Pregabalin prices are about 15% above the bottom. Pregabalin is 60-70% of API business. Chattral intermediates run at about 60-70% and finished APIs at about 30%. Q4 API revenue was reported as about Rs 30 crore with EBIT of about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA across all three segments to at least maintain Q4 FY26 margins, with an aim to improve.

Blue standalone: management said peak EBITDA of about Rs 50-55 crore is the goal for FY27 if prices hold, on about Rs 400 crore revenue at 13-14% margin (analyst's framing, accepted as a goal, not a formal guide).

Long-term margin targets: about 13% EBITDA for AZO and 15-16% for API; Mitesh Patel said Chattral and Atlas could reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex, at 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.
CEP certification for Pregabalin expected by end of FY27 (current financial year), seen as a driver of volume and export access.
Management aims for Rs 1,000 crore group revenue within the next few years, with priority on sustaining revenue first.
capex_capacity: AZO capacity 2,400 tpa; brownfield expansion of about Rs 10-15 crore (plant and machinery only) to lift capacity to about 1.5x, triggered at 75-85% utilisation, expected within 3-4 quarters and funded by internal accruals.
Blue: no capex planned for capacity; incremental gains expected from debottlenecking and efficiency projects.
Chattral: intermediates about 60-70% utilised; finished API utilisation about 30%, which management sees as the key lever for fixed-asset turnover.
Peak debt was Rs 220 crore after the completed four-year capex cycle; debt is falling faster than internal estimates.
demand_pricing: Blue pricing is set quarterly with MNC customers; Q4 benefit was partly locked in, so further benefit expected in Q1 and Q2. Mitesh Patel put the price increase at about 20%, and management said prices across pigments and crude rose meaningfully on raw-material tightness.
Management said China raised prices about 30-40% due to lower export incentives and VAT rebates, roughly doubled ocean freight and higher crude-linked raw material costs.

US tariffs hit AZO and Blue exports, including via India-made value-added products; US business has revived since tariffs eased but has not returned to normal. AZO export customers have restarted testing.
Management said Europe remains in a structural slowdown; India remains the main AZO growth market.
Management says the cyclical slowdown appears to be bottoming, and no new pigment capacity is expected in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA gain came from raw-material price pass-through, and does it reverse if raw material prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jaykrishna said the strategy was to pass through as much raw-material inflation as possible via long-term supplier and customer relationships. He did not quantify the split and said revenue was under pressure while the bottom line held.

qa_highlights.question: Blue gross margin rose from about 29% to 34% QoQ. Is there inventory gain, and how do margins return to 35-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said margins reflect internal strategy, some inventory addition, and operating efficiencies. Gokul Jaykrishna later put the inventory gain as marginal, since the company held finished goods bought before the war.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Blue power and fuel cost fall to under 5% of sales in Q4 because of a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said a one-time receipt of renewable-energy billing rebate, pending for two years, drove the drop. Management expects power and fuel as a percentage of sales to be lower than before but not at Q4 levels every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is AZO FY26 revenue and PBT, and will it break even in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Nupur (company) said FY26 AZO revenue was Rs 78 crore and PBT was Rs (-2.42) crore. Management said it expects PBT break-even in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone Blue utilisation and possible FY27 EBITDA of Rs 50-55 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Gokul Jaykrishna corrected the analyst's 60% figure, saying Blue runs at about 80-85%. He called Rs 50-55 crore peak potential and the goal for FY27. Mitesh Patel put Blue price increases at about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiaries: peak revenue and EBITDA potential at Atlas and Chattral?
qa_highlights.answer: Mitesh Patel said the two facilities can reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex and 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years. Arjun said API EBITDA depends on pricing, and management said the subsidiaries could reach about Rs 50 crore EBITDA at peak.

risks_watch: Q4 margin gains were partly one-off: a renewable-energy rebate lowered Blue power and fuel costs, and an inventory gain contributed. Q1 FY27 is the test.
Pricing is volatile: management says there is no stability in prices or the business environment; a reversal of raw-material inflation could compress margins.
API utilisation at Chattral finished products is about 30%, and the company has not yet hired senior business development or marketing leadership; a senior hire is expected in the next quarter.
FY26 consolidated revenue fell 4.78% and EBITDA 6.12%; FY26 net margin about 3.3%. AZO and API are still loss-making or marginal, so consolidation depends on Blue.
CEP certification for Pregabalin (targeted by end FY27) and AZO export approvals in the US and Europe remain unconfirmed timelines.
Leadership transition: Gokul Jaykrishna stepped down as CEO and Arjun Jaykrishna took over as CEO.

Management was candid that AZO and API margins are far from targets and that the environment is volatile, and it avoided quantifying the inventory gain, the price pass-through split and the Blue revenue mix. Some answers were loose or corrected on the call.
key_quotes: The strategy and implementation we have been working on is going to strongly position us in the Blue business to continue to perform at a good level in the coming quarters and year as well.

We are far from that. And we need to make serious strategic decisions as well as good business operational moves to reach this.

Capex of ₹174 crore was incurred in H1, with a planned ₹375 crore for the year partly offset by ₹134 crore of non-core asset sales. segments.name: Composite products (LPG, CNG, hydrogen, fire extinguisher)
segments.commentary: Segment grew 29% in H1 FY27 per management; guidance is 25–30% growth. Management cited a shortage-driven shift by OMCs to composite cylinders for new LPG connections.

segments.name: PVC/HDPE pipes (water, sewage, drainage, power ducts, gas lines)
segments.commentary: Guidance 20–25% growth. Management said H1 is seasonally weak (about 35–40% of pipe business), with H2 at 60–65%, and that state-level price revisions are easing contractor payment delays.

segments.name: Other products (marks film, auto components, start-up matting, lifestyle)
segments.commentary: Small share of business; guidance 10–12% growth.

segments.name: Overseas operations
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~27% with overseas capacity utilisation ~86%. Management said revenue is split across Middle East (~11%), Southeast Asia (~18%) and USA (~9%).

guidance_outlook: Minimum 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next 3 years; with 15% volume growth, EBITDA growth is expected above 20% and PAT growth above 25%.

Targeted annual ROCE improvement of 1.5–2%; EBITDA margin improvement of 1–1.5% from automation and consolidation, implying ~15.5% margin next year from ~13.3%.

Cost actions across real estate, technology and infrastructure delivered about 200 bps of margin improvement, and Q4 showed sequential recovery in revenue and margin. The Media (broadband, DTV, CelerityX) business remains loss-making at Rs 175 crore for the year, with a Rs 50 crore loss in the latest quarter. 532867|2026-03.headline: V2 Retail Q4 FY26 revenue rose 60% YoY to Rs 797 crore and PAT hit a record Rs 17.5 crore; FY27 store target is 170-200.
532867|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 60% YoY to Rs 797 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 109 crore (13.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 17.5 crore versus Rs 6.4 crore a year earlier. FY26 revenue reached Rs 3,067 crore (+63%), with PAT of Rs 162 crore (+125%) and ROE of 26%. Management said the company added 136 stores in FY26 to reach 325 stores (about 3.5 million sq ft), and it guided to 170-200 stores in FY27 and at least 50% revenue growth over the next two years. Management also flagged a softer May due to geopolitical tension, with June expected to define the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: +89% YoY vs Rs 57.5 crore; margin up from 11.6%
+77% YoY vs Rs 258 crore; margin up from 13.7%
vs 23.2% in FY25 and about 10.7% in FY24

segments.name: Old stores (pre-FY24 vintage)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales per sq ft of Rs 1,124 for old stores; company-wide PSF reached about Rs 1,125 per management, with old-store EBITDA of about 11-12%.

segments.name: New stores (opened after FY24)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales per sq ft of Rs 750, about 70% of old-store level; store-level EBITDA about 5-6%, breakeven at about Rs 500 per sq ft, and 3-4 years to mature.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Men about 41-42%, women about 27%, kids about 25%. Kurtis, men's woven pajamas and men's casual shirts were the fastest-growing categories.

guidance_outlook: FY27 store additions targeted at 170-200, conditional on performance; management indicated about 250 stores in the following year, reaching about 500 by end FY27 per the Q&A.
Gross margin to be maintained at 28-30%; raw-material price rises to be passed on, with prices up about 3-4%.
At least 50% revenue growth guided over the next two years; SSSG guided at 8-10%.
FY27 EBITDA margins expected to be similar to FY26 and company PSF similar, as new-area additions of 50-60% offset SSSG and cost gains.
Inventory to be held at 90-100 days and creditors at 45 days; safety stock to be reduced once geopolitical situation normalises.
Marketing spend about 0.3% of revenue in FY26; FY27 expected to be below 0.5%.
Long-term aim of about 2,500 stores in India and Rs 1,200 per sq ft company-level PSF; 2,000-store milestone to be followed by a year of only about 500 new stores.
capex_capacity: Store count reached 325 with about 3.5 million sq ft; 33 stores opened and 2 closed in Q4, 136 net added in FY26; company crossed 350 stores per the opening remarks.
Capex per store about Rs 2.6 crore now, rising to Rs 2.7-2.8 crore including inventory; capex component about Rs 1.2-1.3 crore.
Per-sq-ft operating cost reduced from about Rs 200 to about Rs 190, targeted at about Rs 175.
Three zonal warehouses (central plus new Kolkata zonal, southern zonal being finalised) and about 18 hubs.
Store expansion to be funded from internal accruals and balance-sheet cash for FY27; debt preferred for any further funding.
demand_pricing: Early-season buying for festivals and wedding season, plus pre-GRC of Rs 100-150 crore, lifted March inventory; total additional inventory about Rs 300 crore including new-store stock.
Management said April was very good, May slow due to the war, and June expected to be one of the biggest months.
Average selling price about Rs 300; 3-4% price increase implies about Rs 10-12 added MRP.
Full-price share 90% in FY26; volume growth 47% vs revenue growth 63% attributed to product mix, with inflationary price increase of about 4-5%.
Management argued competitors' partial pass-through strategy would not be followed by V2.

qa_highlights.question: Store additions planned this year and funding source?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 stores in FY27, dependent on performance; funded by internal accruals and balance-sheet cash for at least this year, with debt as the first preference later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SSSG look weak in Q4 versus peers, and why did PSF fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 base is about Rs 1,000-1,040 per sq ft versus peers; management says FY SSSG still leads. Company PSF fell because new stores at about 70% of old-store PSF dilute the average; old-store PSF rose 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation jump in Q4 - one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a one-time accounting change: small items such as nuts, hard tags and hangers are now expensed rather than capitalised, impact about Rs 6-7 crore in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability and pass-through of yarn/cotton costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected at 28-30%, aided by better inventory freshness, inter-store transfers and less winter discounting; raw-material increases passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin flat with 50%+ area growth?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run at 5-6% EBITDA versus 11-12% for old stores, so blended margin stays flat until expansion slows; operating leverage expected to show from FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: Lease liabilities growing slower than area; why?
qa_highlights.answer: The company changed its lease accounting policy to look at 2-3 years of new-store performance; leases are about 1-year lock-ins and vendor lock-ins about 11 years, aligning with peers and narrowing the pre-IndAS to IndAS gap.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow positive while opening 175-200 stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected to stay positive; creditor days fell about 10 days due to vendor prepayments, which can be stopped if cash is needed for stores.

risks_watch: May slowdown linked to geopolitical tension; June trading to define Q1 FY27 performance.
Working capital: creditor days down about 10 days from prepayments; inventory at about 76% under 6 months old, with safety stock to be unwound later.
New stores at about 70% PSF and 5-6% EBITDA dilute company margins while new-area additions stay at 50-60%.
Store expansion to 170-200 in FY27 and 250 the following year depends on sustaining performance; expansion into newer states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, South) still at early stage.
Commodity and yarn price pass-through of 3-4% needs to hold volume; competitors reportedly taking partial margin hit.
Q4 depreciation step-up from expensing small items (about Rs 6-7 crore one-time).
532867|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and long-term oriented on growth and store expansion, with repeated conditionality on performance. More cautious on the near term, acknowledging a slower May due to the war and declining company PSF from new-store dilution.

So, we are guiding for the similar margins and the similar PSF.
So, about 76% of our inventory is less than 6 months old and out of that also about 50% of the inventory is less than 3 months old.

rows.why: Capex per store about Rs 2.6 crore rising to Rs 2.7-2.8 crore with inventory, and a southern zonal warehouse is being finalised, but no new plant or board-level capex package was announced in the brief.

rows.why: Management guides at least 50% revenue growth over FY27-FY28 and SSSG of 8-10%, and flagged a softer May due to geopolitical tension with June expected to define the quarter, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.why: Inventory rose about Rs 300 crore in March and creditor days fell about 10 days from vendor prepayments; safety stock to be unwound once geopolitics normalises, which could release cash but also reverse the prepayment cushion.

rows.label: Expansion into Gujarat, Maharashtra and South
rows.why: Newer states are still at early stage per the risks section, and the 170-200 store plan depends on performance in these regions, with no quantified store split in the brief.

rows.why: Raw-material prices up about 3-4% to be passed on, implying about Rs 10-12 added MRP on an average selling price of about Rs 300, with management rejecting competitors' partial pass-through approach.

532867|2026-06.headline: V2 Retail Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore, with PAT up 70% to INR41.9 crore and store count at 381.
532867|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR997 crore (+58% YoY), with reported EBITDA of INR139.5 crore (+60%, 14.0% margin) and PAT of INR41.9 crore (+70%). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was about INR79 crore (~8% margin, +51%) and PAT INR50 crore (+64%). Gross margin eased to 28.6% from 29.5%, which management attributed to Adhik Maas reducing full-price sell-through to 90% from 92%. Store count reached 381 at June 30, 2026 (56 net adds), and management says it has since crossed 400 stores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 170-200 new stores and 29-30% gross margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 92% in prior-year Q1 per Q&A

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 381 stores at June 30, 2026 covering ~40.7 lakh sq ft; 57 opened and 1 closed in Q1, net +56. Crossed 400 stores after quarter-end. Stores are mostly standalone, 10,000-12,000 sq ft, in 26 states.

segments.name: New vs mature stores
segments.commentary: New stores run ~34% lower sales per sq ft than mature stores (>2 years old at ~INR1,070-1,100/sq ft); new stores at ~INR730-740/sq ft. New-store SSSG is ~2.3 pts above old stores in Q1. Cohort SPSF cited at 886 vs 925 earlier.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance at least 50% for FY27, unchanged.
SSSG guidance 8-10% for the full year, retained despite Q1 at ~7.5%.
Gross margin guided at 29-30% (earlier 28-30% range), dependent on sell-through.
170-200 store openings planned for FY27; no change in plan despite capex inflation.
Targeting ~50% CAGR growth for the next 2-3 years, per CEO.
Price increase of 4-5% in garment MRPs from Q3 FY27 to offset raw material inflation.
EBITDA margin to be maintained despite the new-store expansion; new stores pay back in 2.5-3 years and break even from their first month.
Funding via internal accruals, release of ~INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases; no QIP planned.
capex_capacity: New store capex has risen ~10% to INR1.22 crore from INR1.1 crore, due to input inflation.
Inventory held ~100 days (earlier 90-100 days target) and creditors ~45-50 days; safety stock raised due to geopolitical tension and to be reduced later.
Inventory for new stores is staged ~2 months ahead, with ~INR100-150 crore tied up per quarter of 50-55 openings.
MOU signed for the next 100 stores; ~15-20 store locations finalised each month based on regional data.
Store-level replenishment cut to 2-3 days of sales cover from 10-12 days, with store back-room space converted into selling area.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is inelastic; kids' wear is ~25% of sales. July-August trends described as in line with plan, but too early to judge given festive shift into Q3.
Adhik Maas (30 days in Q1) and fewer wedding dates weakened Tier 2/3 demand and cut full-price sales to 90%.
Price increase of 4-5% on garment cost from Q3; management says past increases reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.
Repeat customers within first year rose from ~40% to ~55% over three years, per management.
80% of stores face 3-4 other value fashion retailers in the same catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be passed on, and what is the volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation to hit from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier; a 4-5% rise in garment cost will be passed to consumers. Past price hikes reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the store addition pace slow or need new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 openings remain on track with no capex slowdown. Internal accruals, INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases will fund it; no QIP planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhik Maas cut full-price sales to 90% from 92%. Guidance remains 29-30% gross margin, dependent on season sell-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new-store productivity gap closing?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run ~34% below mature stores on SPSF; 10-12 stores are below INR600/sq ft, which management says is too early to judge. Management expects maturity in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are stores appearing in Tier 1 cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said V2 has long operated in Tier 1 (about 11 stores in Delhi NCR) and that Tier 1 is part of the target market.

qa_highlights.question: Customer experience: are NPS or other KPIs tracked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not focus on Google reviews; an NPS link is sent after billing to ~40% of customers as a pilot, with store incentives linked to NPS. AI on CCTV flags long checkout queues.

risks_watch: Gross margin at 28.6% is below the 29-30% guided range; the recovery depends on full-price sell-through in the festive season (Q2-Q3).
New-store productivity is ~34% below mature stores, with 10-12 stores below INR600/sq ft; RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2.
Working capital is inflated by vendor prepayments; cash release depends on creditor days normalising to 45-50 days.
Capex inflation (~10%) and rising rent escalation (12-15% every 3 years) could pressure store economics.
Geopolitical risk is driving higher safety stock and raw-material inflation; the timing of 4-5% price pass-through is a watch item.
Customer experience issues (store-level reviews and checkout queues) could weigh on repeat rates and SSSG.
532867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and store expansion; cautious and deflective on near-term demand, saying it is too early to call July-August trends ahead of the festive quarters. Management gave few numbers on the post-quarter trend and deferred several questions to the next call.
key_quotes: We delivered an amazing 58% year -on-year revenue growth in the first quarter while maintaining healthy returns.
So we need to have that inventory at least 2 months prior to the opening of the store.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided to 29-30% from 28.6% in Q1, helped by the 4-5% garment price increase from Q3, but dependent on sell-through and offset by new stores running ~34% below mature sales per sq ft and rising capex (~10%) and rent escalations.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 57 stores opened and 1 closed in Q1 (381 at June 30, 2026), crossed 400 after quarter-end, with 170-200 openings guided for FY27 and 15-20 sites finalised monthly; MOU signed for next 100 stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided to grow at least 50% in FY27 with 170-200 openings on top of 381 stores; Q1 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore and SSSG was ~7.5%, though management said past price hikes reduced volume slightly.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric was disclosed and no new plant or capex programme is discussed; growth is store-led and funded from internal accruals, creditor-day release of INR150-200 crore and bank limits, with no QIP planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all FY27 guidance (at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 29-30% gross margin) despite Q1 SSSG at ~7.5% and gross margin below range, and July-August trends were called too early to judge.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 SSSG was ~7.5% against an 8-10% full-year target, gross margin of 28.6% sits below the 29-30% guided range, and full-price sales fell to ~90% from 92%, with the recovery depending on festive sell-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or category launch was discussed; kids' wear is ~25% of sales but no new line was flagged.

rows.label: 4-5% garment MRP increase from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Raw material inflation hits from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier, and management plans to pass a 4-5% rise in garment cost to consumers, saying past hikes cut volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

rows.label: Creditor-day normalisation releases INR150-200 crore
rows.why: Creditor days are ~45-50 against a 45-50 target after vendor prepayments inflated working capital, and inventory of ~100 days is to be cut later; cash release depends on this normalising.

rows.label: RK Retail acquisition consolidates from Q2 FY27
rows.why: The brief says RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2, which adds to revenue, but no size or contribution figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion, the 50% growth guide and funding without a QIP, but cautious and deflective on July-August demand, gross margin recovery and new-store productivity; analysts pushed on gross margin and the new-store productivity gap.

532867|2026-09.headline: V2 Retail Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% to INR905.6 crores on volume growth, but SSSG was -14.9% reported and mgmt cut FY27 SSSG view to 5-7%.
532867|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 28% YoY to INR905.6 crores, driven by 31% volume growth, with gross margin up 310 bps to 31.1% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 20% to INR53.4 crores. Reported SSSG was -14.9%, which management attributes mainly to the Durga Puja and wedding season shifting from Q2 to Q3; underlying SSSG was stated as +0.5%, and H1 calendar SSSG was -3.7%. Management opened 49 stores in Q2 (106 in H1, a record), and sales per square foot fell to INR700 per month from INR933. Management said it will open only 60-70 stores in H2, will open a total of 170-190 stores in FY27 (with some H2 sites slipping to April), and flagged that FY28 openings could fall to around 100 if Q3 trends stay weak.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR37 crores; mainly right-of-use assets for 106 new stores

segments.name: Category mix
segments.commentary: Men's wear about 40%, ladies 29%, kids 22%, lifestyle 9%; mix described as unchanged. Full-price sales 91% in Q2 and H1 vs 92% last year.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 427 stores across 27 states and 340+ cities as of 30 Sep 2026, about 4.6 million sq ft; 49 opened and 3 closed in Q2, 106 opened and 4 closed in H1. About 60% of new stores are in core states (UP, Bihar, MP, Odisha, Assam).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 50%+ maintained; management said H2 revenue growth would need to be around 60%, with 7-9% SSSG from old stores and the rest from new stores.
FY27 SSSG guidance cut to 5-7% (from 8-10% for the rest of the year after H1 SSSG of -3.7%); Q3 SSSG target 5-7% on a period-to-period basis.

Full-year FY27 gross margin guided at 29-30%; post-Ind AS EBITDA margin 13.5-14.5% (management says it guides on pre-Ind AS); pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin guided at more than 7.5% for the full year, with H2 at least 8%.

Store openings: 60-70 in H2 FY27, taking FY27 total to 170-190; FY28 current guidance 120-150 stores, but could drop to about 100 if Q3 weak, with FY28 revenue growth then 35-40% vs about 50%. Decision point is end of Q3.
Net working capital expected to normalise to 75-80 days by March 2027; creditor days expected at 45-65 vs 65-70 average.
Q3 FY27 described as the company's best quarter ever in revenue and profitability.
capex_capacity: Opened 106 stores in H1 FY27, which management called its highest-ever H1 addition; plans 60-70 more in H2 and says back end (design, sourcing, warehousing, talent) can support 150+ stores per year.
About 18 of the H2 pipeline already opened; remainder to shift to April 2027 due to site project delays.
Closing retail space up about 1 million sq ft since March 2026; inventory rose to INR1,447.8 crores from INR1,141 crores at March 2026.
Long-term vision of 2,500 stores.
V2Kart e-commerce piloted in 2 states; operational issues with fulfilling single-piece orders from about 35,000 pieces of stock per store; expansion to more states pending.
demand_pricing: Reported SSSG -14.9% in Q2; underlying +0.5% after festive shift; H1 calendar SSSG -3.7%. Sales per sq ft per month INR700 in Q2 (vs INR933) and INR785 in H1 (vs INR948).
Mature stores (over 2 years) at INR1,000+ PSF; new stores at about INR720-730 on a last-12-month basis, 35-40% below mature stores. Management said Q2 PSF is typically 40-45% below year average.
October: calendar basis double-digit SSSG growth; period-to-period (Dussehra-to-Dussehra) flat. Winter fill rate about 20% better than last year.

Average bill value INR917 in H1 (vs INR900); ABV down about 1% and footfall down about 3% in Q2 per management. ASP about INR307 vs INR309; ASP down 3% in H1 as product mix shifted to value and economy.
Price increases: input costs up 3-7%; MRP raised 5-10% to protect gross margin. Shift to blended fabrics. Management said it will take further hikes only if raw material prices rise again.

Competitors named: unorganised mom-and-pop stores and organised players such as V-Mart, Style Baazar, Citykart, Baazar Kolkata and M Baazar. Management said its PSF is at least 30% above its closest competitor in most locations.

Repeat customers in mature stores rose from 55% to about 70%; repeat frequency fell from 5-5.5 months to 4.4-4.5 months; marketing cost under 0.5% of revenue; loyal customer spend INR2,200-2,500 a year.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of Q2 negative LFL by festival-dependent states vs other states, and October/November trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the state split; about 260 stores are Puja-impacted. October calendar growth was more than double-digit but flat period-to-period; management will update around mid-December.

qa_highlights.question: Is the store addition slowing to H2 and does the 50% growth guidance still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18 of the H2 pipeline is already open, with 60-70 more planned and the rest shifting to April on project delays. Management said it has not changed the 50%+ revenue growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an underlying demand problem beyond the festive shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no single factor stands out: ABV, ASP, state-wise and cohort-wise SSSG all showed the same slowdown, and competitor benchmarking showed similar results. Demand softened in the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut store additions if SSSG stays weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, if the trend continues through Q3, FY28 openings would be about 100 instead of 150-200, with revenue growth falling to 35-40%. The decision will be taken at end-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did new-store PSF fall to about INR700 from the INR938 level last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: PSF is a last-12-month average; new stores are about INR720-730 on that basis, and Q2 is seasonally 40-45% lower. Management said the 12-month average for new stores is still above INR730-740.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin up 300 bps despite lower full-price share; what drove it, and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Average discount depth fell to about 30% from 50%, a bill-buster promotion moved from Q2 last year to Q3 this year, and Q1 margin was 1% lower due to earlier discounting for Adhik Maas. Full-year gross margin guided at 29-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt has risen to about INR500 crores; what level is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings were INR528 crores (INR483 crores current). Management said debt-to-equity below 0.5 is healthy if EBITDA covers interest, and expects borrowings to ease as store additions slow.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be the best quarter ever and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed Q3 will be the best quarter ever in revenue and profitability. Full-year pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin should be above 7.5%, with H2 at least 8% versus about 7% in H1.

risks_watch: Reported SSSG of -14.9% in Q2 and H1 calendar SSSG of -3.7%; demand slowed in the last three months per management, with no single cause identified.
Working capital: inventory of INR1,447.8 crores, net working capital 88 days vs 81 days, and borrowings up to INR528 crores; normalisation targeted for March 2027 (75-80 days).
Store productivity: new stores at about 35-40% lower PSF than mature stores; management has stretched the maturity period for FY25 cohorts to 2.5-3.5 years.
Q3 festive and winter season is the test: October flat period-to-period; management will reassess store openings at end-Q3.
Depreciation rising sharply (INR68 crores vs INR37 crores) and expected to keep rising in Q3 and Q4 as store base grows.
Creditor days to fall to 45-65 days from 65-70 as cash is used for early vendor payments.
Input cost inflation of 3-7%; further price increases possible if raw material costs rise; V2Kart e-commerce still at pilot stage in 2 states.
Governance/disclosure: an analyst raised repeatedly the non-disclosure of the core senior team (6-7 people) and mature-store SSSG for H1; management committed to share in a future presentation.
key_quotes: So we checke d the data and nothing stands out in particular.
But in the last 3 months, definitely we saw some sort of a demand slowdown.
Yes, correct. So if this trend continues to the third quarter, then next year we'll only open 100 stores, which initially the target was 150 to 200.
Yes, I think we are not changing our guidance in terms of revenue growth.
Yes, Q3 will be V2 Retail's best quarter ever. In terms of revenue, in terms of profitability, correct.

rows.why: Gross margin up 310 bps to 31.1% in Q2 with discount depth down to about 30% from 50%, and FY27 gross margin guided at 29-30% while pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is guided above 7.5% with H2 at least 8% vs about 7% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.why: Piloted in 2 states with fulfilment issues on single-piece orders from about 35,000 pieces of stock per store, and expansion to more states is pending.

532868|2026-03.headline: DLF posted a record FY26 collection of over INR 13,500 crore (+15% YoY) and zero gross debt in development, with FY26 sales bookings of INR 20,143 crore in line with guidance.
532868|2026-03.overview: Management reported a strong close to FY26, citing record collections of over INR 13,500 crore (+15%) and cash surplus of over INR 7,700 crore (+25%). FY26 sales bookings were INR 20,143 crore, in line with guidance despite deferral of a couple of launches, with Q4 sales of about INR 3,967 crore led by Dahlias. Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR 2,452 crore with reported net profit of INR 1,256 crore; FY26 net profit was INR 4,256 crore (+16%). The rental business shows a 95% occupancy portfolio of 50 million sq ft and a 4-5 year NOI growth guidance of mid-teens, with 20-25% CAGR on a longer basis. Management steered the Q&A away from presales volume toward margins and cash flows.

financial_highlights.value: INR 14,155 crore, of which ~INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts

financial_highlights.metric: DCCDL FY26 revenue / EBITDA / PBT before exceptional
financial_highlights.value: ~INR 7,400 crore / over INR 5,700 crore / INR 2,726 crore

segments.name: Rental (annuity) business
segments.commentary: Rental portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 95% occupancy; FY26 NOI growth of about 34-35% driven by assets completed late FY25 reaching full lease. Non-SEZ office occupancy 98-99%, SEZ 88-89%, and income loss from vacancy down to ~3.5%.

segments.name: Development (DevCo)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales of INR 20,143 crore; Dahlias sales about INR 5,000 crore in FY26, guided to INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27. Management targets ~INR 9,000-10,000 crore of margin creation and INR 7,000-8,000 crore of DevCo FCF annually.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Existing mall income expected to grow 10-11% in FY27, plus three new malls. Midtown Plaza 95% leased and operational; Summit Plaza 95-97% leased, opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa 50% leasing line of sight, completion around August.

segments.name: Office (Atrium Place, Downtown)
segments.commentary: Atrium Place (JV with Hines, 3.2 million sq ft) fully leased; three towers have OC and fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27, generating ~INR 700 crore rent. Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft ~500,000 sq ft leased, completion expected Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales guidance of ~INR 20,000 crore maintained; management said upside possible if demand stays strong.
Annual margin creation of ~INR 9,000 crore guided to continue.
Rental NOI guidance: mid-teens growth in NOI and 20-25% CAGR over the next 4-5 years, though management cautioned FY26's 34-35% growth should not be extrapolated.
FY27 exit rental of ~INR 8,200 crore across DCCDL and the rest of DLF assets combined.
Launch pipeline of almost INR 20,000 crore for FY27, including a large DLF City launch (INR 8,000-9,000 crore or higher), Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa.
Dividend: no formal guidance given; ~two-thirds of dividend is funded by Cyber City's dividend to DLF.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 (Towers 5-8) completion late FY28/early FY29; Taramani completion Q2 FY28.
capex_capacity: Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27; Summit Plaza opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa mall completion around August with opening 2-3 months later.
Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft: completion expected Q2 FY28; central atrium design change made.

Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2: 7.5 million sq ft integrated development (2 million sq ft mall, 5.5 million sq ft offices); Tower 7 (2.2 million sq ft) nearly fully leased; Towers 5 and 6 being leased; finishing late FY28/early FY29; iconic tower construction to start in ~2.5 years.
Westpark Mumbai pipeline above 5 million sq ft; ~900,000 sq ft launched so far, next phase of ~800,000 sq ft in FY27, then 500,000-600,000 sq ft.
SEZ portfolio of 16-17 million sq ft; ~4 million sq ft converted to non-processing areas. Chennai operating portfolio above 10 million sq ft, rising to 14-15 million sq ft.
demand_pricing: Dahlias (super luxury, Gurugram): 32 apartments sold in Q4 plus 2 Camellias; per-unit prices now ~INR 90-110 crore for the first phase units vs ~INR 60-75 crore at launch. Dahlias per sq ft pricing is about INR 1 lakh on super area vs Camellias ~INR 1.2 lakh (INR 80-150 crore per unit).
Office SEZ rentals: gap to Cyber City rentals narrowed to 10-12% for new take-up; Cyber City vacancy lowest in SEZ portfolio; Hyderabad SEZ vacancy 17-20%.
Chennai Taramani top-floor leases at INR 145-150 per sq ft; average realisation expected INR 125-130 per sq ft.

Management flagged that large tenants are reviewing internal processes, which could defer leasing decisions, though no portfolio impact so far; cited AI and Iran-US war as factors but said there was no impact yet.
Management declined to chase presales volume, saying margins and cash flows are the priority; said presales of INR 50,000 crore a year are possible given land bank.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the medium-term launch pipeline shown as ~INR 60,000 crore versus INR 67,000 crore earlier, and is the company less confident about the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is a status update on a INR 1,14,000 crore 5-year launch pipeline announced ~2 years ago; launches are paced to market absorption and execution capacity, with further phases identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch and presales plan given the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pipeline is ~INR 20,000 crore, including a DLF City launch of INR 8,000-9,000 crore or more, Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa (approvals in place but a PIL pending).

qa_highlights.question: Why is presales growth limited to ~INR 20,000 crore versus peers at INR 30,000-35,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said presales is not the right metric and the company is chasing margins and cash flows; it could do INR 50,000 crore a year if chosen, with delivery capability the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 presales is expected from Dahlias and how much from the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahlias sales were about INR 5,000 crore in FY26 and are expected at INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27; management expects INR 13,000-14,000 crore to come from the ~INR 20,000 crore launch pipeline, as not all launches will sell out at launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts and the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Badal Bagri said the RERA cash unlocks from FY27-28; uses are shareholder returns, DLF rental capex (committed), and opportunistic margin-accretive land deals. Revenue recognition is on completed-contract method, with large projects like Arbour delivering from FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend sustainable and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said about two-thirds of the dividend comes from Cyber City's dividend to DLF, and no dividend guidance is being offered, though the trajectory has been of continuing growth.

risks_watch: Rental NOI growth of 34-35% in FY26 was driven by one-time lease-up of assets completed late FY25; management cautioned against extrapolation.
Large tenants reviewing decision-making (AI, Iran-US war), possibly deferring leasing; SEZ vacancy ~10% overall and 17-20% in Hyderabad.
Launch pipeline timing: Goa approvals subject to a PIL; Moti Nagar Phase 2 unlikely in FY27 and possibly FY28.
Dahlias sell-out and per-sq ft price trajectory is a key driver of FY27 presales; management admitted Dahlias pricing has moved fast.
Rising brokerage and overhead costs in Q4 linked to collections and year-end provisioning; management said full-year overheads should stay around current levels.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Taramani completion timelines, plus Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27.

532868|2026-06.headline: DLF Q1 FY27 net profit rose to INR 794 crore (from INR 766 crore) while pre-sales were muted at INR 657 crore amid Aureva launch deferment.
532868|2026-06.overview: DLF reported a resilient Q1 FY27 with collections of INR 2,406 crore, operating cash flow above INR 1,300 crore and net cash of INR 15,200 crore, of which close to INR 11,000 crore sits in RERA escrow accounts. Pre-sales were INR 657 crore, held back by the deferred Aureva senior living launch awaiting approvals and a deliberate pacing of Dahlias sales. Rental revenue was INR 1,605 crore with EBITDA of INR 476 crore, and occupancy stayed above 95% by space and 97% by value. DCCDL posted revenue up 10% YoY to INR 1,917 crore and PAT of INR 717 crore, up over 20%, though this included one-time tax entries. Management said FY28 would be the reporting inflection as large projects begin contributing under completed-contract accounting.

segments.name: Office rentals
segments.commentary: Vacancy is very low; newer assets Cyber Park, Atrium Place, Downtown Gurgaon and Downtown Chennai are nearly 100% leased. Rentals in the portfolio grew about 8.5%-9% from Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Midtown Plaza is fully operational, about 85% open and 96%-97% leased; Summit Plaza had a soft launch and is about 90% leased; Goa mall has OC, is 64% leased as of 31 July, and is targeted to open late 2026 or early 2027. Retail spend grew about 13.5%-14%.

segments.name: Residential (Dahlias, Golf Links)
segments.commentary: Dahlias is about 65% sold with 34 units sold in the quarter; price realisation is above INR 1 lakh per sq ft, reaching INR 1.20-1.25 lakh on higher floors, with entry ticket above INR 100 crore.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: DLF will act only as real estate developer and builder for data centres, not own technology or operate them; Data Center 3 in Noida expected to add rental around March-April 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY28 expected to be the reporting inflection point as large projects starting with Arbour contribute to P&L under completed-contract accounting.
Management hopes to stick to broad FY27 sales guidance; Goa residential shortfall would be about 10% of the INR 20,000 crore guidance and is expected to be covered.
Group exit rentals for FY27 guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.
Midtown Plaza and Summit Plaza expected to reach steady-state rentals by Q4 FY27; Goa to stabilise around May-June 2027; Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected in September 2026.
Q2 and Q3 expected to be good quarters for office leasing as global companies and GCCs return to decision-making.
capex_capacity: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 construction at full speed; Gurgaon leasing about 40%, Taramani pre-leasing about 17%-18%.
Downtown Chennai Towers 4 and 5 (3.5 million sq ft) to complete by beginning of 2028; Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 by end 2029.
Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected September 2026; all three new malls (Midtown, Summit, Goa) now operational in FY27 per management.
Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres consolidated) still on drawing board; sizing and launch decision expected within next year.
Land spend of about INR 545 crore over the last two quarters, including an INR 80 crore EMD for an NCR auction not yet concluded.
Mumbai project with potential above 5 million sq ft; launch targeted within FY27 or calendar 2026.
demand_pricing: Office demand slowed by AI-related hiring uncertainty and the Iran-US conflict since February; management sees GCC and large multinational enquiries returning in the last 4-5 weeks.

Gurgaon rentals: Atrium Place about INR 175 per sq ft weighted average, Downtown 4 about INR 150-155, Phase 2 leasing averaging INR 200; Cyber City existing rentals INR 140-150 versus INR 210-220 for newer buildings.
Dahlias: 25%-30% of demand now from rest of India and NRIs; secondary sales in Privana at INR 2,500-4,000 per sq ft.
CAM costs rose about 2%-2.5% due to minimum wage revisions; no tenant pushback reported because CAM is audited annually and passed through.
Pre-sales pacing for Dahlias to be held until Experience Centre opens after Diwali; next Privana phase expected early 2027 as a high-rise scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown in Dahlias sustenance sales (34 units vs typical 12-15 units per quarter) deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pace was consciously managed around the Experience Centre opening after Diwali; Dahlias is about 65% sold and entry ticket is now above INR 100 crore, with some additional sales held back pending paperwork.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Goa residential launch slip without hurting the INR 20,000 crore sales guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said Goa accounted for only a couple of thousand crore, about 10% of guidance, and that the gap should be covered comfortably; all Goa approvals are in hand but the PIL is being addressed before taking customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stabilised run-rate of group rental income and what ramp-up remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Midtown and Summit Plaza reach steady state by Q4 FY27, Goa by May-June 2027, and Atrium Place Tower 1 adds a full tower after its September OC; exit FY27 group rentals guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will Cyber City 2 and the next commercial pipeline start?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres) sizing and launch remain undecided with a decision expected within the next year; construction in Hyderabad or Cyber City is planned for sometime next year.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Dahlias sales velocity versus price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said about 3.5 years of sales were achieved in 15-16 months, with roughly 3 years remaining; Ashok Tyagi said there is no direct binary between velocity and price, and the next phase depends on physical and commercial progress, implying a 3-year cycle.

Goa residential launch is subject to a PIL; customer payments will not be accepted until the path is clear.
Office leasing recovery depends on GCC and large multinational decisions in Q2 and Q3 after the Iran-US conflict and AI-hiring uncertainty.

Land acquisition spend of about INR 545 crore over two quarters; GAV addition depends on parcels fructifying in 1-2 quarters.

532868|2026-09.headline: DLF Q2 FY27 booked INR 3,800 crore sales and reported INR 2,298 crore revenue, aided by a one-time INR 738 crore fair-value gain in other income.
532868|2026-09.overview: DLF reported new sales bookings of about INR 3,800 crore and collections of INR 2,780 crore, with operating cash flow of about INR 1,858 crore and net cash of about INR 15,100 crore after roughly INR 1,980 crore of dividend payout. Consolidated revenue of INR 2,298 crore included a one-time INR 738 crore valuation gain on a JV investment booked as other income, with EBITDA of INR 1,060 crore and net profit above INR 1,300 crore. Rental portfolio reached 50 million sq ft at 96% occupancy by area and 97% by value. Management said accounting revenue remains back-ended under completed-contract accounting until the pre-Arbour projects complete in FY28. Management flagged likely Q3 construction outflow slowdown from labour migration and Delhi GRAP restrictions.

financial_highlights.change: includes one-time INR 738 crore gain booked as other income

segments.name: Development (DLF)
segments.commentary: Aureva luxury retirement housing sold out; Dahlias super-luxury sales at about 276 units sold so far with prices up about 10% this quarter. Gross margin potential of development business about INR 40,000 crore, cash generation potential over INR 42,500 crore.

segments.name: Rental (DLF portfolio)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 96% occupancy by area and 97% by value; quarterly rental about INR 120 crore, with full-potential exit run-rate of INR 175-180 crore per quarter (about INR 750 crore annualised), excluding Atrium.

segments.name: DCCDL (commercial annuity)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,014 crore, EBITDA INR 1,537 crore, net profit over INR 750 crore (+17% YoY). Exit rental guidance about INR 6,800 crore.

guidance_outlook: Accounting revenue inflection expected in FY27-28 as launched projects (about INR 75,000 crore launched so far) complete and are recognised under completed-contract method, continuing over next two to five years.
Arbour commissioning targeted FY27-28, followed by a series of project completions; completion timelines seen as broadly within a quarter of plan.
Experience Centre for Dahlias targeted by December; Mumbai launch in Q3 and Gurugram launch plus a new luxury-plus project in Phase 4 (Hamilton, unnamed) targeted in Q4.
Forward other expenses to be in line with average of last two quarters; other income expected at about INR 150-200 crore per quarter excluding one-offs.
DLF dividend guidance remains annual; DCCDL to provide more predictable dividend flow to DLF.

capex_capacity: Rental portfolio 50 mn sq ft; Atrium fully rent-generating this year; Summit Plaza and Midtown Plaza commissioned this quarter.
Chennai Blocks 1-3 operational; Chennai Blocks 4-5 (3.6 mn sq ft) to become operational by calendar 2027.
Downtown Gurugram Blocks 5-8 and Mall of India Gurugram: completion targeted end-FY28 to FY29, most blocks operational FY29-FY30.

Land: acquired remaining 7.06-acre encumbered parcel from IREO bonds transaction and a fresh 7.48-acre contiguous parcel in Sector 61, creating a 36-acre contiguous land parcel; land deal expected to conclude by Q4.
Construction outflows expected to be slightly weaker in Q2-Q3 due to labour migration for Chhath and GRAP restrictions (30-40 days typical in Gurgaon).

Dahlias South sale reached about INR 100 crore per apartment, described as a new landmark.

Aureva booking amount INR 50 lakh; about INR 1,900 crore of INR 1,985 crore potential reported in the quarter, with about six units spilling over into October on NRI payment confirmations.
Q1 described as relatively quiet for pre-sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Aureva sales extend into October and are Dahlias price hikes already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales closed before 30 September; only money-received and KYC-complete units are booked, so about INR 1,900 crore of INR 1,985 crore was booked in Q2 and the rest was recorded in October. Dahlias prices already rose about 10% this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exit rental run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-potential quarterly rent of about INR 175-180 crore (about INR 750 crore annualised) for DLF portfolio excluding Atrium; DCCDL exit rental about INR 6,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will construction outflows slow and will completion timelines hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a slight blip in Q2-Q3 construction outflows due to labour migration and GRAP; completion timelines seen as broadly within a quarter, with no major challenges foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: Could dividends move to quarterly or half-yearly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit; DLF dividend remains annual, though DCCDL dividend flow to DLF is being made more predictable.

qa_highlights.question: Why are accounting revenues below expectations and what drives other expenses and other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Completed-contract accounting defers recognition to OC; inflection in FY27-28. Cyber City (about INR 2,000 crore quarterly revenue) and Atrium Place (INR 150-175 crore) are not consolidated despite 67% control due to minority AVM rights. Other expenses are overheads in line with prior average; other income guidance INR 150-200 crore per quarter excluding one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hamilton project and when will it launch?
qa_highlights.answer: Unnamed luxury-plus project in DLF Phase 4 near the same vicinity, targeted for launch in Q4.

risks_watch: Accounting revenue remains depressed until pre-Arbour projects complete; FY27-28 inflection is key.

532884|2026-06.headline: Refex Q1 FY27 standalone continuing revenue rose 76% YoY to INR619 crore, with EBITDA of INR105 crore (17% margin) and PAT of INR73.6 crore (+123%).
532884|2026-06.overview: Standalone continuing-operations revenue grew 76% YoY to INR619 crore and EBITDA rose to INR105 crore at a 17% margin, while PAT reached INR73.6 crore (11.9% margin). Ash and coal handling remained the largest contributor despite acute diesel shortages and logistics disruptions linked to geopolitical developments. Wind turbine execution started contributing INR295 crore in the quarter at near-zero margin, and the mobility demerger is progressing toward a shareholder meeting next month.

Q2 expected to be slower, Q3-Q4 to scale up. Management guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%.

segments.commentary: Asset-light premium corporate mobility; being demerged into a separate listed company. NCLT has approved convening shareholder and creditor meetings, with equity shareholder meeting scheduled for next month. Expected to exit discontinued operations by end of Q3 FY27.

Blades currently imported; localisation under way, with in-house blade manufacturing planned.

Railway Rail-cum-Road (RCR) initiative started, with freight discounts opening Northeast routes.

Ash handling order book INR1,635 crore; management says digital tender wins in the past four months should improve the Q4 order book.

Management welcomes new entrants in ash handling, arguing they expand awareness and market; says Refex is the only organised player.
Wind market tailwinds cited from hybrid renewables (wind, solar, storage) and the 100 GW by 2030 government ambition. Exports ruled out; focus is domestic only.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it always guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%; Q1 EBITDA margin was 17%.

qa_highlights.answer: INR1,860 crore in hand, of which INR525 crore executed; INR1,300 crore to be executed in FY27. New orders would spill into FY28; growth expected to be very good, with no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pledge reduction trajectory for promoter shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledge was reduced last month, another disclosure due within 15 days, with further releases expected within two weeks.

qa_highlights.answer: Refex holds about 76-77%, the JV partner 23%; technology was transferred directly for payment, and the partner runs operations. Management did not disclose the partner's equity infusion on the call.

532884|2026-09.headline: Refex Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 36% YoY to INR560 crore and PAT 13% to INR60 crore, despite monsoon-hit ash volumes.
532884|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from continuing operations was INR560 crore (up 36% YoY) with EBITDA of INR91 crore (16% margin, up 22%) and PAT of INR60 crore (up 13%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,179 crore (up 55%) and PAT INR133 crore (up 55%). Management attributed the weak Q2 volumes to monsoon disruption in ash handling, and said wind execution and the new RMC and green mobility businesses are at early stages. The demerger of green mobility awaits NCLT final approval, with the next hearing on 11 November 2026.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (new)

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited UltraTech and RDC Concrete earning about 10% profit on RMC; expects better margins through zero-capex, tech-driven operations. RMC is expected to contribute meaningfully from FY28; FY27 is set-up year.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and receivables: why is receivable at INR1,251 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is 120-130 days, driven by retention money and billing/certification delays of up to 70 days; target is to hold about 130 days. Management said zero amount is overdue or at risk of bad debt.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost rise versus cash balance and other income decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said vendors are now paid through TReDS, which raises finance cost (INR13 crore to INR17 crore QoQ) but lowers direct cost; the bank balance rose at quarter-end and fluctuates intra-quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR400-450 crore is secondary pledge for an acquisition, expected to be released in 3-5 months; about INR100 crore is borrowing-linked and to be cleared in 12-24 months. Management denied any forced-selling risk.

532885|2026-03.headline: Central Bank of India Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR724 crore on a one-time INR632 crore DTA charge; FY26 net profit rose 15.43% to INR4,369 crore.

532885|2026-06.headline: Central Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, with advances up 28.58% YoY and gross NPA at 2.60%.
