Net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, NIM was 3.06%, and ROE improved to 14.92% from 14.17%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.60% (down 53 bps YoY), net NPA at 0.49%, and slippage ratio at 0.29%. Management said the quarter's advances growth was driven partly by a low base in corporate loans, and quarter-on-quarter advances growth was only about 2.85%. Liquidity coverage ratio fell sharply from 235% to 156%, as the bank deployed liquidity into loans.

segments.name: Agriculture

segments.commentary: An analyst cited wholesale segment at minus ₹139 crore (vs ₹284 crore) and unallocated at minus ₹75 crore (vs ₹322 crore). Management said provisioning had not risen and did not clearly explain the change.

segments.commentary: Bank holds about 26% in Generali Central Life and Generali Central Non-Life, with ₹627 crore invested in total. Management expects higher income from both this year after the establishment phase.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.
532891|2026-06.overview: Presales grew 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores on 9% higher volume (1.36 million sq ft) and 18% higher realisation (INR10,589/sq ft). Collections rose 40% to INR1,199 crores and 745 homes (0.94 million sq ft) were handed over. Total income rose 63% YoY to INR877 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 25% from 15%, and PAT was INR25 crores versus a loss of INR69 crores a year earlier. Management kept FY27 presales guidance and the INR700 crores debt-reduction target, while adding four Bengaluru land opportunities (GDV ~INR5,200 crores) and signing a sale of Purva Zentech to ICICI Prudential AMC at ~INR625 crores EV.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the amount paid for the four Bengaluru acquisitions from cash on hand; no land cost is unpaid, but future development spend will be booked as construction cost, and new land purchases would add land payments.

qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crores of debt on that asset will be repaid from proceeds; the rest will be evaluated for debt reduction, business development or working capital, with closing expected this month.

qa_highlights.answer: Both held; launches slipping from Q1 moved to Q2 for one or two projects, and management said opportunity spend versus debt reduction will be reviewed from time to time.

qa_highlights.question: What margin is targeted over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin guidance of 25-30% at portfolio level held, with product mix (plotted, JDA, outright, redevelopment) causing project-level variation.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Purva Estrella contribute to Q1 sales and how does it compare with the top projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Estrella contributed about INR200 crores in Q1 and about INR800 crores since launch; management could not confirm a separate top-three ranking, citing South's Northern Light and Provident Equinox and West's Estrella.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no zero-debt target; free cash flow will be split between new opportunities and debt, and debt is an important part of the business as the portfolio (about INR58,500 crores) grows.

532892|2026-03.headline: MOFSL FY26 operating PAT rose 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores; Q4 operating PAT up 25% with a ₹661 crore exit run rate.
532892|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating PAT of ₹2,360 crores (+16% YoY), with Q4 operating PAT up 25% and the strongest of the four quarters. Asset and Private Wealth businesses grew profit 33% and now contribute about 50% of operating PAT, with Asset Management at 33% of group operating PAT versus 26% in FY25. Reported PAT including OCI was hit by notional MTM losses of about ₹1,000 crores on a ~₹9,000 crore investment book, which management said were largely recouped in April 2026. Long-term credit rating was upgraded to AA+ (stable). Q&A focused on SIP and MF flow share, yield compression from product mix, MTF and broking trajectory, digital broker competition, and treasury MTM.

Digital brokers are gaining share in cash and F&O and as MF distributors (analyst cited 60-70% of new SIPs via fintech platforms); management says wealth model is research and advisory led and focusing on high-value traders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP market share dip in the quarter and what is being done to regain it?
qa_highlights.answer: SIP run rate is ₹1,400+ crores per month; passive decline due to international funds closed to new money and a locked microcap fund, with a small active drop. SIP books are at last-year levels and should climb as performance recovers.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving revenue yield compression and the lending growth in Private Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: TER changes had no fee impact. Compression is mix-driven, as passives (lower retention) grew fastest. Private Wealth lending is a strategy to offer solutions to UHNIs and family offices, combining loans against securities and investment assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF book guidance for FY27 and the QoQ decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline (₹6,500 crores at 9M to ₹5,700 crores at Mar'26) is market-driven and industry-wide. Management is confident of strong growth, citing ~7% cash and MTF share and a strong balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹1,000 crore treasury loss unrealised and has it been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is a notional MTM loss under Ind AS, with most recouped in April 2026. The investment book's 10-year-plus IRR is ~18%, and including buybacks and dividends it has compounded at ~40% p.a.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned against digital brokers and fintech SIP platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth model is research and advisory led across franchisee, direct and branch channels; cash market revenue share held. Wealth distribution AUM grew 40% to ~₹44,000 crores. Working on high-value trader positioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Private Wealth client quality and AUM per RM trend?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM per RM rose from ~₹300 crores a couple of years ago to ₹450 crores at Mar'26 despite a larger RM base. Among ~9,000 families, almost 50% have UHNI potential. Segments are HNI (₹50-100 crores), UHNI (₹100 crores+) and family offices.

Leadership vacancy on the MF investment side pending decision.

532893|2026-03.headline: VTM Ltd FY26 PAT fell about 75% to Rs 11 crore on US tariff discounts (~Rs 20 crore), with FY27 turnover guided up 12-14% and EBITDA margin targeted at 10-11%.
532893|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 8% (base ~Rs 372 crore) but PAT of about Rs 11 crore, down roughly 75% YoY. The drop was attributed to an ~18% US tariff-related discount (~Rs 20 crore), chargeback discounts (~Rs 8 crore), a Rs 2.3 crore forex MTM loss on PCFC borrowings, a gratuity provision under the new Labour Code, and ~15% higher raw material costs. FY26 EBITDA margin was 7.43%, and management said the 18% discount to the US customer Quince is still in place, with negotiations ongoing and the current price point at about 10%. Management guided to 12-14% FY27 top-line growth, a 10-11% EBITDA margin, and a 6.5 million-unit order backlog as of 31 May.

532898|2026-03.headline: POWERGRID delivered ₹28,206 crore capitalisation and ~₹40,000 crore capex in FY26, guiding FY27 capex to ₹37,000 crore and capitalisation to ₹30,000 crore.
532898|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 capex (close to ₹40,000 crore against an initial ₹28,000 crore guide) and capitalisation (₹28,206 crore against a ₹25,000 crore commitment) both beat guidance. Standalone PAT rose 4% to about ₹15,921 crore and consolidated PAT rose 3% to about ₹15,928 crore, with total income of ₹47,684 crore versus ₹47,459 crore. Management flagged a natural RTM revenue decline as assets reach 12 years, offset by FY26 capitalisation that it expects to flow into FY27 revenue. The pipeline was described as ₹1.7 lakh crore of works in hand and ₹1.1 lakh crore under bidding, with new avenues in BESS, integrated storage under Section 62, and the first international PPP in Kenya.

segments.commentary: Accounts for about 81% of the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand (₹1.37 lakh crore). Management said FY26 saw 9 TBCB wins out of 28 projects floated, at a total tariff of about 44% share.

segments.commentary: Works in hand of about ₹28,000 crore. Revenue is on a natural downward trajectory after assets complete 12 years, offset in FY26 by ~₹1,700 crore of depreciation-related gaps covered by other income items.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,195 crore; first 400G interface in India, first international long-distance link to Bhutan, and a 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible in the next quarter.

FY27 expected to show full revenue benefit of FY26 capitalisation, which came mainly in the later part of FY26.

Pang-Kaithal HVDC project excluded from the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand pending Government of India review.

Pilot 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible within the next quarter; 220 kV mobile GIS in place, with 132 kV and 400 kV mobile GIS expected within this calendar year.
demand_pricing: Works in hand ₹1.7 lakh crore (TBCB ₹1.37 lakh crore, RTM ₹28,000 crore, others ₹4,200 crore), excluding Pang-Kaithal HVDC.

Under-bidding pipeline of ₹1.1 lakh crore, including ₹5,270 crore of intra-State; major projects include Barmer Phase 4, Vizag Green Hydrogen, Jam Khambhaliya, Krishnagiri, Lakadia, ERWR and Nawada-Durgapur.
Management cited a ₹7.9 lakh crore opportunity under the 900+ GW by 2036 anchor programme and ₹6.4 lakh crore from Brahmaputra basin hydro; 22 HVDC schemes (127 GW) are in planning or bidding.
Intra-State TBCB thresholds are ₹150-250 crore by state; the smallest project POWERGRID has bid was about ₹60 crore.
Management said electricity share in the energy basket is about 22% and is expected to rise, supporting transmission demand.

On competition, management said it bids on risk-return framework and declined to quantify changes in TBCB tariff or IRR; equity IRR guidance of 11-13% was described as possibly better, with change-in-law as a cost pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the Q4 FY26 EBITDA decline and whether new TBCB projects use service concession accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the natural RTM tariff dip after 12 years of asset life; new BOOT-method TBCB projects are accounted for using the financial lease model.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and commissioning expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 expected beyond ₹40,000 crore, in a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range. Capitalisation guided at ₹30,000 crore for FY27 and about ₹35,000 crore for FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has bid TBCB for about 14 years and selects projects by risk-return framework rather than volume; it did not indicate a change in intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Equity IRR on TBCB projects given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns could be better than the 11-13% range, as cost-plus RTM rewards cost but TBCB rewards efficiency, and change-in-law provisions protect against surprises.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing of capex and capitalisation in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing depends on individual project completions, expects an even spread across quarters, and noted that the Q4-heavy FY26 was incidental.

qa_highlights.question: Regulated equity on standalone and consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulated equity exists only in standalone; TBCB projects have no regulated equity.

532898|2026-06.headline: POWERGRID Q1 FY27 PAT flat at Rs 3,598 crore (vs Rs 3,631 crore QoQ) as regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore offset Rs 790 crore transmission-charge growth.

532899|2026-06.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
532899|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

Maize was the largest drag: revenue fell about 36.3% in the first half, partly due to a monsoon-related sowing shortfall and delayed onset, while non-cotton products grew with new hybrids in vegetables and rice. Management said cotton volume pressure is tied to illegal Bt cotton seed sales and that the company is shifting toward new hybrid cotton products, with 85-90% of the cotton portfolio expected to come from new hybrids over 3-4 years. Management flagged elevated maize and rice inventory (Rs 150 crore plus higher than last year) and higher cash-to-payables timing effects, and said export expansion into Bangladesh, Philippines, Indonesia, Tanzania and others is aimed at building its own brand.

532900|2026-03.headline: Paisalo posted record Q4 FY26 PAT of Rs.722 million, up 56% YoY, with AUM up 17% to Rs.61,009 million.
532900|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 35% YoY to Rs.2,609 million and net interest income rose 61% YoY to Rs.1,733 million, driving a record quarterly PAT. FY26 PAT was Rs.2,372 million, with total income up 22% and NII up 29%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 0.76% and NNPA at 0.61%, and cost of borrowing eased to 10.22%. Management reaffirmed a three-year guidance to double AUM, income and net profit, and said co-lending is excluded from that base.

qa_highlights.question: What trends are seen in SME and overall book in April and May amid the war situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress is concentrated in large SMEs and mid-corporates with export exposure, hit by insurance, freight and Strait of Hormuz flow issues (about 5% capacity). Paisalo has no large concentrated exposure; LCC segment may see difficulty this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Update on co-lending expansion with State Bank of India?
qa_highlights.answer: Paisalo has completed its RBI-circular compliance on both methods; one is expected live within Q1 FY27 and the other awaits the bank's compliance confirmation, expected by end of Q1 or early Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How are NPAs recognised and what is recovery on collateral?
qa_highlights.answer: NPAs are recognised under RBI IRAC norms on both secured and unsecured books. Secured lending uses 50-60% LTV, with recovery typically covering principal plus cost of funds; only NIM is lost, not principal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the three-year doubling guidance still intact given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management reaffirmed doubling AUM income and net profit over the next three fiscal years.

qa_highlights.answer: Promoters raised stake by about 4.7% last fiscal year after warrants of Rs.180 crore and 5% creeping acquisition earlier; management declined to comment on FY27 plans.

qa_highlights.question: How is collection efficiency at 98.5% achieved despite industry MFI stress, and is inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited a 'lend right, collect tight' philosophy with credit processes designed for elimination rather than servicing. It confirmed active scouting for inorganic opportunities and partners.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products will drive FY27 revenue, and why was QoQ disbursement growth low?
qa_highlights.answer: Six new segments have about 18-20 partnerships, to be scaled in FY27 with roughly three sub-products per category over time. Reported QoQ disbursement growth was 3%, with Q3 to Q4 growth of about 27% and FY26 growth about 15%.

532900|2026-06.headline: Paisalo Q1 FY27: record disbursement of Rs.17,309 million (+128% YoY), PAT up 30% to Rs.613 million, gross NPA 0.70%.
532900|2026-06.overview: Management, represented solely by Deputy MD Santanu Agarwal (CFO unavailable), reported AUM of Rs.67,074 million (+28% YoY) and a record quarterly disbursement of Rs.17,309 million. Management set a three-year ambition to roughly double AUM, income and profitability, and launched a Rs.300 crore NCD tranche under a Rs.900 crore shelf. 532906|2026-06.headline: Maan Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR232 crore and EBITDA to INR7 crore, with margin near 3%.

532926|2026-06.headline: Jyothy Labs Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 8.4% (down ~820 bps YoY) as gross margin dropped to 38.5% on crude-linked input inflation.

532926|2026-09.headline: Jyothy Labs Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA margin fell to 2.5% from 16.1% as gross margin dropped to 34.8%, despite 3.3% revenue growth to INR760 crore.
532926|2026-09.overview: Reported revenue rose 3.3% YoY to INR760 crore, but the Pril and Fa exit (brand licence expired May 2026) depressed reported volumes; excluding these brands, value grew 12.4% and volume 8.1%. Crude-linked raw material and packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 34.8% (48.1% last year, 38.5% in Q1), pushing operating EBITDA to INR19 crore and PAT to INR10.6 crore. Management took about 4% price increases, said pricing alone cannot close a 13-14% inflation gap, and called FY27 an aberration year. The Board approved a INR147 crore tender-offer buyback at INR215 per share, with promoters not participating.

segments.name: Fabric Care
segments.commentary: Led growth with 10.4% value growth; liquid detergents grew over 50% YoY (Henko, Ujala, MoreLight, Mr. White), and Ujala Young & Fresh fabric conditioner is performing well. Management said liquids carry lower margins than powder while the category scales.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Excluding Pril, segment grew 15.3%, mainly on volume. Exo dishwash grew 23% on new variants, liquids, wider distribution and brand investment.

segments.name: Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Coil share of HI portfolio fell to 30-35% from 43-45% a year ago as liquid vaporisers, aerosols and other formats scale; Maxo Agarbatti launched with a government-approved formulation. Profitability improvement is the priority.

segments.name: Personal Care (Margo)
segments.commentary: Grew a little over 11% in value on Margo pricing and a favourable GST base. Price increases of about 10-12% in Margo could not fully absorb palm oil and neem oil inflation; Margo Gentle glycerin soap (argan and moringa variants) launched in select markets.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said natural space still has loyal and young consumers, Margo will grow through extensions such as Margo Gentle, and other personal care opportunities will be addressed through other brands.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no one-off; other expenses were about INR66 crores vs INR69.74 crores last year, so there is no major reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16% EBITDA margin guidance standalone or consolidated, and does it include other income?
qa_highlights.answer: 16% is standalone at transformer level and includes other income; consolidated margin (19% in Q1) is higher, and the CFO guided consolidated FY27 margin to around 20-21%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $1 billion revenue target still valid, and how does it reconcile with 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Target re-based to about INR8,000 crores by FY29 (from INR9,600 crores at old rupee rate), from INR5,000-6,000 crores capacity plus INR800-1,000 crores third-party backward integration sales.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build-up and debt: how will working capital and capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is high as a hedge until backward integration is running; inventory reduction starts from Q4 FY28. Management says no increase in debt planned, with capex funded by cash, QIP balance of about INR145 crores, leasing (about INR500 crores) and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HVDC timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 9 months are needed to complete repair work on HVDC, after which PGCIL would empanel the company for a first trial order; full HVDC manufacturing is 15-16 months away.

qa_highlights.question: Will Changodar utilisation normalise, and what about Moraiya at 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Changodar is expected at 60-65% in FY27 and 80-85% in FY28; Moraiya at 60-65% (57% per chart) is expected to reach 80-85% after Q3, with raw material protection through December.

risks_watch: Changodar ramp-up: utilisation at 60-65% through FY27; the August 2026 start and Q3 FY27 stabilisation are key checkpoints.

CRGO steel anti-dumping investigation by DGTR may raise raw material costs; management has not quantified impact.
Geopolitical risk to raw material supply and execution beyond December 2026.
Margin sustainability in FY27 at 16% standalone if mix shifts toward lower-rated transformers as Changodar recovers, per analyst question; management said no risk.

532928|2026-09.headline: TARIL Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 66% YoY to INR709 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 16.1%, with order book at INR7,237 crore (+32% YoY).
532928|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR709 crore (+66% YoY, +27% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR114 crore (+203% YoY), with margin at 16.1% versus 8.8% a year earlier, which management attributed to higher utilisation and operating leverage. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,268 crore (+35% YoY) and EBITDA INR185 crore (14.6% margin). Order inflow in Q2 was INR1,169 crore (+97% YoY off a low base), and the unexecuted order book stood at INR7,237 crore, executable over 18-24 months. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 25% growth and 9-10% PAT margin, while working-capital days (about 154) remain the key drag on cash flow.

+47% YoY; margin 14.6% vs 13.4% in H1 FY26

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 8% of Q2 revenue and about 15% of the order book. Export inquiries are about 20% of the INR21,000 crore inquiry pipeline.

segments.commentary: CTC plant to be commissioned around Diwali, with commercial manufacturing by Q4 FY27; about 60% of its 3,000 MTPA capacity is captive. Management expects 200-300 bps margin expansion once integration is complete.

Realisation is about INR7 lakh per MVA on average. Price variation clauses are billed every quarter. Management attributed about 7-8% of revenue growth to price variation, with no list price increase in Q2.

Raw materials (transoil, CRGO, copper) remain high-priced; Middle East disruption has not hit imports materially, but timely availability of some critical raw materials is an issue. Inventory is sufficient until Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Details of Kaiga and Megha orders; is Kaiga repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaiga was competed against Crompton and others for generator transformers at 400 kV+; management expects repeat NPCIL orders. Greenfield nuclear transformer content is about 15-18% of the transformer cost.

qa_highlights.question: Mix of order book by voltage class?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55-60% of the order book is 400 kV and above; about 56% of Q2 power transformer execution was in this class.

qa_highlights.question: When will free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to cut working-capital days from end-FY27, targeting below 120 days and 110-120 days this year, which should lead to positive cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation per MVA and capex on Changodar?
qa_highlights.answer: Average realisation about INR7 lakh per MVA; Changodar capex about INR150 crore for about 35,000 MVA capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance looks conservative given H2 run rate; can FY27 revenue reach INR3,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it maintains the INR3,200 crore FY27 revenue target and the 9-10% PAT margin. It needs to execute about INR900 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a path to USD1 billion revenue and does it need more capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects USD1 billion by late FY29 or early FY30 from transformers plus bushings, pressboard, CRGO, CTC, and tank sales. It said no additional capex is needed.

risks_watch: Working-capital intensity: inventory about INR654 crore and receivables about INR1,053 crore against INR1,268 crore H1 revenue. Operating cash flow conversion is weak relative to PAT.
Commissioning timelines for Changodar (around Diwali) and CTC (Q3 FY27, commercial from Q4) could slip; the CTC timeline was questioned against earlier guidance of Q2 FY27.
Raw material price volatility and supply of critical inputs amid Middle East disruption; part of the order book has price variation clauses, but the rest does not.
Retention money of about INR200 crore (5-10% of order value) is tied up on the balance sheet.
HVDC and converter transformer qualification is roughly 1.5 years away; BESS orders are not yet in hand.
Pricing: about 7-8% of revenue growth came from price variation; underlying realisation trends need to be tracked.

532929|2026-03.headline: Brigade FY26 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 7,424 crore on approval delays; FY27 pre-sales guided to at least 20% growth, aiming for INR 9,000 crore.
532929|2026-03.overview: FY26 pre-sales were INR 7,424 crore, down 5% YoY, as launches slipped: 8.3 million sq ft launched against a 12 million sq ft plan, with about 3.3 million sq ft pushed into FY27 (mostly Chennai). Q4 pre-sales were INR 2,521 crore (up 44% QoQ by value) from 4 million sq ft of launches. Consolidated FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 5,909 crore with EBITDA of INR 1,638 crore (28% margin), and PAT after minority interest was INR 644 crore. Operating cash flow weakened because of higher construction spend, and management expects it to rise in line with sales growth. Management says the approval issues are largely behind it, and it has guided FY27 launches of about 11.5-12 million sq ft.

segments.commentary: Turnover INR 1,303 crore (+12% YoY) with EBITDA INR 906 crore (+18%). Q4 turnover INR 337 crore with EBITDA INR 228 crore. segments.name: Hospitality (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 604 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA INR 207 crore. Q4 turnover INR 160 crore with EBITDA INR 60 crore. Q4 occupancy 78%, ADR up 8% QoQ, RevPAR up 13% QoQ; FY26 RevPAR +6% on ADR +7%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales: at least 20% growth over FY26, aiming for about INR 9,000 crore, conditional on current sentiment and market conditions holding.

Commercial pipeline of about 10 million sq ft over FY27-FY28 with capex of about INR 6,000 crore over 4 years (INR 1,200-1,700 crore a year). Debt-equity expected to stay well below 1x even as commercial debt rises; residential capex is self-funded, and commercial capex is a mix of debt and cash flow.

FY26 launches: 8.3 million sq ft (GDV about INR 10,000 crore) vs plan of 12 million sq ft. Q4 launches: 4 million sq ft (GDV about INR 4,500 crore).

Launch timing: Hyderabad 2 million sq ft Kokapet plot in Q3 and 1 million sq ft Northern Hyderabad project in Q4; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3 (including East Bengaluru OMR in Q3); Chennai Morgan Heights relaunch in Q1 FY27 plus two projects in Q3 and Q4. North Bengaluru project is delayed by bylaw changes requiring redesign.

Office: Whitefield JV with Bain (50:50, pure equity partners) on 10.8 acres opposite ITPL, with about 2 million sq ft of office and a 250-key 5-star hotel, targeted for completion in about 40 months after approval. Leasing: about 3 million sq ft of new completions expected in FY27. WTC Bengaluru: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft, with about 100,000 sq ft already leased.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales mix FY26: sustenance 57%, launches 43%. Q4 launch share of pre-sales about 55%. Geographic split (Q4 and FY26 approx. same): Bengaluru 65%, Hyderabad 20%, Chennai 15%.
Conversion of site visits steady at 10-12% across cities; NRI buyers around 10% of pre-sales value; some markets showing longer conversion cycles.

Upcoming launch APR around INR 10,000 per sq ft vs inventory above INR 12,000 per sq ft; overall APR increase of 13% was partly mix-driven.

Ticket-size mix: ultra-luxury about 30% of portfolio, expected to decline. Most FY27 launch tickets below INR 3 crore; affordable up to INR 75 lakh, mid-segment up to INR 1.5 crore, premium up to INR 3 crore.
Unsold inventory about 7.5 million sq ft. Residential buyer base: GCC and IT are the largest; IT services about 26% of leasing portfolio.

Leasing: about 1.1 million sq ft leased in FY26; GCCs 58% of the lease book; top anchor tenants (above 1 lakh sq ft) are 65% of the portfolio. Lease rent escalation expected at 10-15% for Amazon's vacated space at WTC Bengaluru. Rental collections 99%.
Commercial monetisation (strata sales) annual run-rate about INR 550 crore; Twin Towers to be exited in FY27, keeping about 100,000 sq ft of common amenities.
Hospitality demand anchored in domestic travel; foreign arrivals and MICE were hit by Middle East tensions.

qa_highlights.question: Plan to fill WTC Bengaluru after Amazon exit, and expected rental uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft; about 100,000 sq ft already leased on a couple of floors. Leasing is expected floor-wise or 2-3 floors at a time over the next couple of quarters, with 10-15% rent mark-to-market (up to 20% for half-floors).

qa_highlights.name: Cumulative GDV available for launch over two years and land replenishment?
qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative GDV available for launch over the next two years, and what is the land replenishment strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolling four-quarter pipeline of 11.5 million sq ft and INR 11,900-12,000 crore GDV. Land bank of 57 million sq ft, of which about 75% is residential. Replenishment focused on Bengaluru and Hyderabad, moderately Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 9,000 crore pre-sales guidance conservative given unsold inventory and launch conversion history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted it is somewhat conservative. It cited Chennai launches selling more evenly across construction, and launch slippage into H2 leaving less time to sell in-year. Management aims to push inventory sales and pull launches forward.

qa_highlights.question: Quarter-wise launch phasing and approval status for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad about 1 million sq ft in Q3 and another 1 million in Q4; Morgan Heights 1 million sq ft relaunch in Q1; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3. The primary approval issues are considered resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow trajectory and collections trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections were flat as launches were deferred early in FY26; that cash is now converting. Operating cash flow is expected to grow in percentage terms close to sales growth, a few hundred bps lower.

qa_highlights.question: Reported margin weakness in resi and leasing, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Resi reported margins reflect completion-based recognition of older, earlier-sold projects that did not capture recent price increases; POCM operating margin is around 30%. Leasing is above 80% on a normalised basis; reported margins are diluted by about INR 200 crore of facility management revenue at about 15% and about INR 35 crore of fit-out recoveries, plus a Q4 accounting gross-up.

532937|2026-03.headline: Kuantum Papers Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 22% QoQ to INR48 crore (15.90% margin) on NSR of INR3,700/MT, despite input cost pressure.
532937|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operational income was INR301 crore, up 4% QoQ, driven by NSR improvement to INR3,700/MT, while input costs rose about INR2,000/MT amid the West Asia conflict. EBITDA reached INR48 crore (margin 15.90%, up 234 bps QoQ) and PAT INR14 crore (margin 4.75%, up 137 bps QoQ). For FY26, revenue fell 1% YoY to INR1,093 crore and EBITDA was INR162 crore (14.80% margin), with NSR down about INR2,000/MT and costs up about INR3,200/MT. Management guided to volume growth to about 2,30,000 MT and EBITDA margin of 18-20% over the next few years, with PM3 upgrade and pulp (DDS) commissioning slated for mid-June to July 2026.

segments.name: Notebook paper
segments.commentary: Share fell from about 22% of sales before the September GST change to about 7-8% now; management intends to exit the segment after machine upgrades, citing reversal of input tax credit at nil GST.

segments.name: Copier, high-end printing, specialty paper
segments.commentary: Copier share is growing steadily; Maplitho and size grades target high-end printing; specialty grades targeted at 20-30% of production volume.

segments.commentary: Management noted MIP for paperboard continues with a one-year extension; paperboard was not discussed in detail.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected at INR1,400-1,500 crore, rising gradually to INR1,600 crore; FY28 INR1,600-1,700 crore (management's medium-term view: INR1,600-1,700 crore).
Volumes to rise from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT, a 40-50% increase, at utilisation above 90-95%.
EBITDA margin target of 18-20% over the medium term.
Operating cost reduction of 5-8% of total manufacturing cost once AI/digital projects are fully implemented, expected across machines by FY27-FY28.
Peak long-term debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027, reducing INR100-200 crore a year thereafter; annual repayments of INR170-180 crore over the next 2-3 years.
Remaining capex of about INR125 crore to be spent in FY27; no new capex planned beyond current projects, though another expansion may be considered in about two years.
Tissue paper project deferred, not shelved, until debt is under control.
Wheat straw prices expected to ease after rice sowing starts in early June; Q1 season expected to be lean with pricing pressure.
capex_capacity: PM2 rebuild completed March 2026, capacity raised to 75 TPD; PM1 rebuild in December 2025 added about 20 TPD on average in Q4.
PM3 upgrade delayed due to German imported parts; now planned by mid-June/July 2026 (previously around May).
Displacement Digester System (DDS) for wood pulping under extensive testing, commissioning targeted by mid-June; pulp capacity to come on stream by PM3 commissioning (July).
Two-stage recausticizing plant and 80 TPD synchro sheeter commissioned; overall utilisation above 92% on PM1, PM2 and PM4 (OE levels).
Cost of PM3 upgrade not expected to escalate versus the earlier INR140-150 crore estimate.
demand_pricing: Pricing firmed in Q4 on higher demand, but May price hikes partly reversed; management says it holds prices at about INR69,000-70,000/ton.
Low-priced imports persisted through FY26, lowering domestic prices; West Asia freight disruption reduced import volumes in Q4, with risk of China/Indonesia trade diversion.

Anti-subsidy application expected to be processed by FY-end (March 2027); anti-dumping application on writing and printing paper typically takes 1.5-2 years; MIP for writing/printing paper still under review.
Global pulp prices at about USD600-700/ton, expected to stay in that range given new capacity additions.
Wheat straw prices up about 50-60% YoY, with the fuel-use competition now unwound; wood chip prices broadly stable.
Chemical input costs up about 3-5% for some chemicals; the company is absorbing rather than passing these through.
Dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers; Gulf and North African export markets being developed.

qa_highlights.question: Are import pressures visible now, and will they hurt pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes from China and Indonesia did not arrive in Q4 due to West Asia freight disruption; the impact may return later, and the industry is pursuing Gulf export opportunities. Comment restricted to white paper, not paperboard.

qa_highlights.question: Current debt and capex plans for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026; peak debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027. Remaining capex of about INR125 crore in FY27 and no new capex planned beyond existing projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PM3 and pulp capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: PM3 delayed due to German parts, now targeted by mid-June; pulp upgrade to come on stream alongside PM3 in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new capacity be absorbed, given the demand environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 95%+ utilisation; cited the dealer network, Gulf and Northern Africa markets, and a 25-30% specialty grade mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: How much opex can be cut from AI and capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction once AI systems are deployed across machines, progressing machine by machine and mill-wide, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company refinance or reduce cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Average long-term cost of funds is about 8.5%; management is exploring FCNRB and cheaper funding options. Buybacks are not being considered for now.

532937|2026-09.headline: Kuantum Papers Q2 FY27 revenue fell 8% QoQ to INR279 crores and PAT was INR2 crores, as PM 3 shutdown and input costs hit a lean quarter.
532937|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operational income was INR279 crores, down 8% QoQ, as the PM 3 rebuild (28 June to 21 August 2026) cut volumes by about 6,000 tons. EBITDA was INR35 crores at a 12.4% margin, down 84 bps, on lower realisations and higher raw material and fuel costs linked to the West Asia conflict. PAT was INR2 crores (0.8% margin). H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR533 crores, but H1 PAT was only INR9 crores because depreciation and finance costs rose. Management guided to a 7% to 11% price increase over Q3 and Q4, of which about 4% was taken in late September.

financial_highlights.change: lower due to higher depreciation and finance costs

segments.name: Writing and printing paper (core, four PMs)
segments.commentary: Q2 production was 40,600 tons, with the remaining machines running at 100% utilisation. Management said orders were booked in advance and all output was sold. Specialty paper is about 17% to 18% of the mix, against a target of 25% to 30% in 12 to 15 months.

segments.name: Paperboard / kraft
segments.commentary: Management said a minimum import price (MIP) is already notified for kraft and paperboard varieties. No segment financials were given.

guidance_outlook: Price increases of 7% to 11% targeted by end of year, across Q3 and Q4. About 4% was taken in late September and is being sustained. The next hike is expected after Diwali.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 14%. Management also said industry margins should recover to 18% to 20% in FY28. Analysts' 17% to 18% H2 figure was not confirmed.
Revenue target of over INR1,300 crores for FY27 reiterated. Management said Q3 should be far better than Q2, with lost volume of about 6,000 tons to be regained.
Cost savings of about 1.5% to 2% on total chemical consumption expected from the single-vendor TCM chemical solution.
Depreciation of about INR80 crores per year. Debt repayment of INR180 crores in FY27 is on track, with a similar amount in FY28. Management said deleveraging will begin after the next two years.
Target of about 1 crore clonal saplings a year in the next two to three years. Current production is 17.93 lakh saplings in the quarter.
capex_capacity: PM 3 commissioned 28 August 2026, rebuilt in 59 days against a 65-day plan. All four paper machines are now upgraded, adding a film press, I-table, table vision, web break monitoring, calendaring and automatic starch cooking.

Marketable output is about 600 tons per day at the optimised product mix, against a design capacity of 675 tons per day on an anchor GSM of 64. Orders are shifting to 52 to 58 GSM, which lowers tonnage.
Double Displacement Digester system improved wood pulp yield by 1% and cut steam use from 1.8 to 0.8 metric tons per tonne of pulp.
Environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG gas handling) are in progress, with about INR139 crores of CWIP, to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said there is no further major capex planned.
Environmental clearance has been applied for and is at an advanced stage. The 20 MW turbine generator and a 30 TPH boiler were overhauled during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 was seasonally lean and the industry faced cost inflation. Management said Q2 had almost no price increase, with the first hike taken in the last week of September.

Imports have fallen because of higher ocean freight from the Gulf conflict, and exports have also fallen, so domestic supply is more balanced. Anti-dumping duty applications on writing and printing paper are with the government, with 3 to 6 months expected for completion.

Wood (about INR12,000/tonne) is expected to stay flat or fall as availability improves. Wheat straw prices are temporarily elevated after unseasonal rain and a labour shortage, and are expected to normalise after Diwali.

Starch is about 2% to 2.5% of paper cost. Sulphuric acid from West Asia added about 2% to sales cost. Fuel costs rose about 3% to 3.5%. Input coal costs rose about 2.5% to 3%. Coal mix is about 85% coal and 15% agro.
Chinese capacity is being cut (Chenming and Nine Dragons closures), and Indonesian exports are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the West Asia war impact on costs, and what was the wood-cost offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphuric acid and chemicals added about 2% to sales cost, and fuel about 3% to 3.5%. Raw material cost and consumption fell 15% to 17% versus Q1, but no absolute figure was given.

qa_highlights.answer: About 6,300 tons lost, mainly from PM 3. Management put the EBITDA impact at about INR40 crores, though the transcript does not say whether this is per tonne or total.

qa_highlights.answer: The balance is for auxiliary efficiency items and environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG), to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said no further major capex is planned.

qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt is about INR700 crores. Depreciation is about INR80 crores a year. Debt repayment is INR180 crores in FY27, with a similar amount in FY28. Deleveraging is expected after the next two years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is on cash flow for debt repayment, and there are no plans for changes to the equity capital structure.

Coal supply is constrained because allocated coal is being diverted to the power sector. Open-market coal is available but more expensive.
Mix shift to 52 to 58 GSM is cutting tonnage below the 675 TPD design capacity, and output is now about 600 TPD. Management said it is targeting revenue over tonnage.
Debt of about INR700 crores and higher depreciation and interest will weigh on PAT for the next two years. H1 PAT was INR9 crores.

Wheat straw and fuel costs are expected to normalise after Diwali, but management also said input costs are rising structurally.

532940|2026-03.headline: J. Kumar FY26 revenue rose 1% to INR5,723 crore with EBITDA flat at INR823 crore; management guides 15% top-line growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue been flat for FY26 despite a strong order book, and what is different now?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% FY27 revenue growth achievable given Q1 was 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be more visible, Q2 growth will still be positive, and 15%+ is achievable by year-end, with FY27 and FY28 both expected at about 15% growth.

532953|2026-03.headline: V-Guard Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and PAT 23% to INR112 crore, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.8%.
532953|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was strong, with revenue up 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and EBITDA excluding other income up 19.3% to INR171 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 7% and EBITDA rose 2.6% to INR527 crore. Growth came almost entirely in the second half after a weak summer in the first half. Management is pursuing price hikes of roughly 13% to offset input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, with about 75% landed so far. Net cash rose to INR231 crore and the board recommended a final dividend of INR1.5 per share.

segments.name: Electronics (Stabilizers, UPS, Inverters, Batteries)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 22.3% YoY with all categories growing; about 3% of growth was price and the balance volume, per management. Solar inverters are a newer line, not yet at INR500 crore.

segments.name: Electrical (Wires, Pumps, Switchgears, Modular Switches)
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; Q4 revenue grew 15.9% YoY. Wires face rising competition from new entrants, though management sees the category as low-margin and scale-dependent.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, Air Coolers)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 4.1% YoY; fans and air coolers declined while water heaters and kitchen grew strongly. TPW fans are short of supply due to a plastic raw material shortage.

segments.name: Sunflame (Kitchen Appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.6% YoY; the CSD business is still slowing, but non-CSD grew about 16%. GT integration is complete and sales integration is still underway.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 10-12% volume growth and 1-2% price growth (about 15% total) over time, with higher price growth likely in FY27 due to cost inflation.
EBITDA margin: management says at least 10% is the target for the next year if summer is good, but declined to commit to 11-12%; cited prolonged high cost as a reason for caution.
Expects a good growth year for Consumer Durables on a low base, and a strong start to FY27 given Q4 momentum and a supportive summer forecast.
Cost discipline: no major manpower increases planned; variable pay will fall if top and bottom line targets are missed.
Price increases: about 75% of the required ~13% price hike landed so far; the remaining ~25% is expected as high-cost inventory flows in during May-June.
Raw material supply secured through June for most items; sulfuric acid and certain TPW fan plastics remain tight.
capex_capacity: Management said bulk of new capacity investment is done and ramp-up is under way; capex will still absorb some cash in FY27.
Company spent close to INR300-400 crore over the last 8 years on plants and manufacturing integration.
BLDC is about 40% of ceiling fan sales; BLDC chimneys launched; BLDC mixer grinders not yet launched.
Lighting entry is still work in progress, with launch targeted around early next quarter (Q1 FY27).
No acquisitions planned; any opportunity would be assessed case by case.
demand_pricing: Input costs up 8-13% across representative categories; management says the West Asia conflict has caused commodity inflation and supply shocks, worse than the Ukraine-war period.
Price hikes of about 10-12% (some up to 15-20% industry-wide) face retailer pushback; the company gave case-by-case support in regions where summer has not started.
South India summer demand is strong (sales started early March/April); non-South is mixed due to rain, with East a key market for summer products.
Channel financing covers about 35% of the debtor book (customer-linked, not category-linked); collections were strong in the March quarter.
Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue; no impact seen so far, with summer in Kerala supportive. Non-South contributed 48% of FY26 revenue; South grew 16.2% and non-South 11.8% in Q4.
Competition: wire entrants and lighting peers are entering; management expects consolidation to be slow and sees the top 4-5 brands per category as the survivors.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken across segments, and is another round needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs up 8-13%; about 75% of the required price increase has landed, with the remaining 25% expected as high-cost inventory arrives in May-June.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Kitchen Appliances segment come out of its slump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes demand is improving, with traction for both V-Guard and Sunflame; Sunflame now uses V-Guard's sales network.

qa_highlights.answer: No impact seen so far; Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue and summer there has been supportive. Q1 is primarily a summer quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY26 EBITDA was about 9.5%; management is confident of at least 10% once raw material prices normalise, but declined to guide 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar business size and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar is below INR500 crore, about 36 months old; management expects it to be among the larger categories in 3-4 years, focused on residential B2C.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material availability a risk to production?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfuric acid and polymers are tight; supply is locked up for about a month or more, and management sees no supply challenge through Q1.

532955|2026-09.headline: REC H1 FY27: disbursements of INR56,457 crore (+67% vs Q1) and net NPA at 0.11%, but management concedes NIM pressure from 3.22% level.
532955|2026-09.overview: REC reported H1 FY27 with loan book at an all-time high of INR6.17 lakh crore (up 6% YoY) and PAT of INR7,541 crore for the half. Management cited disbursements of about INR90,000 crore in H1 (power sector ~INR80,000 crore), with net credit-impaired assets down to 0.11% from 0.24% a year earlier. Management guided FY27 loan book growth of 10-12% and NIM of about 3.2%, while acknowledging NIM pressure from competition, derisking and rising borrowing costs. The call also covered the pending PFC merger, with the draft scheme awaiting Cabinet approval.

qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said ~24% of borrowings are floating (INR term loans and some ECBs) versus ~25% of the loan book floating, so rate rises are offset; a zero-coupon bond last year gave ~10 bps benefit and the company is seeking withholding-tax exemption on ECBs and a green bond basket mandate.

qa_highlights.answer: T.S.C. Bosh cited ~80 GW minimum additional capacity under NEP, implying INR1.8-2.2 lakh crore REC financing needs by 2031-32, with a 30:70 equity-debt assumption.

qa_highlights.answer: Chairman declined to give numbers for the merged entity, citing synergies in borrowing, lending and capital base, and restricted guidance to FY27 for REC.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident of 10-12% growth given competition from unlisted players and banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said prepayments had peaked (INR19,000 crore in H1 FY27 vs ~INR1 lakh crore in FY26), banks face sectoral limits, and power, transmission and biogas (INR23,000 crore scheme) are growth drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields fall further on competitive pricing to state utilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said rebate/concession proposals to state sector are largely settled and yield curve is rising, so limited yield downside is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 disbursement momentum seasonal or sustainable, and how does the pipeline look?
qa_highlights.answer: Bosh said Q1 weakness reflected documentation delays and peer competition; ~40% of disbursement pipeline is under documentation, and the Chairman cited ~INR70,000 crore of documented projects yet to start disbursement.

qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said ~1% ECL is being provided on incremental loans (~INR300 crore in Q2 on ~INR26,000 crore growth), with ~80% of ECL being reserve-type given state-sector exposure; straight 1% provisioning expected going forward.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.
532967|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 63% YoY to INR 295 crore on realisation-led growth in dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals, with standalone material margin at 31.9% versus 23.5% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. Consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR 312 crore with EBITDA of INR 37 crore (7.84%), and the group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings. The copper and fertiliser project moved into structured construction, with financial closure still incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received).

Management cited a JV result of about INR 71 crore EBITDA and INR 51 crore PAT on INR 368 crore revenue, as referenced by an analyst; Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, with 60-70% of JV raw materials sourced from Kiri.

qa_highlights.question: Will the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore still hold given staggered tube and rod commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 figure does not hold; projections are moving with vendor delivery timelines. It added that sales are not a constraint since the output would substitute imports.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper revenue start and when will it be fully ramped?
qa_highlights.answer: First copper revenue expected around May-June 2027 (Q1 FY28), with commercial operations from Q2 FY28; majority of operating revenue expected in FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Kiri's standalone profitability low when Lonsen Kiri earns strong margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, which captures finished-product margins; the JV also makes products Kiri does not, so the combined value chain should be assessed. Lonsen Kiri is operated by Kiri management with no plan to replicate its products in Kiri.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to raise equity to reduce debt?

532967|2026-09.headline: Kiri Industries Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 48% YoY to INR 288 crore, with EBITDA turning positive at INR 7 crore on H-Acid price spike.
532967|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR 288 crore (up 48% YoY), with material margin at 29.1% versus 26.4% a year earlier and EBITDA of about INR 7 crore (2.4% margin) against a loss of INR 14 crore. Consolidated Q2 revenue was INR 299 crore (up 40%), EBITDA about INR 2 crore, and loss after tax INR 39 crore before associates, which included a non-cash treasury fair-value loss of INR 57 crore. Management said H-Acid price gains were only partly reflected because of earlier fixed-price orders, with the benefit expected to flow into Q3 and Q4. Copper and fertilizer project phase one remains on track for 1H FY28, and the company took a 40% stake in Makilala Mining in the Philippines.

segments.name: Dyes and dye intermediates (standalone and JV)
segments.commentary: Q2 standalone material margin improved to 29.1%, but sequential material margin was hit by a narrower price-cost spread in dye intermediates. Intermediate capacity utilisation is below 60%, and about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively.

segments.name: Copper and fertilizer project
segments.commentary: Equipment deliveries have started at site, with civil, foundation and structural works progressing. Phase one is on track for 1H FY28, and downstream facilities are due to be operational next fiscal year.

segments.name: Makilala Mining (Philippines, 40%)
segments.commentary: Expected to produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, of which about 100,000 t would come to India, covering roughly 6-7% of the company's 1.6 million t requirement from 2028-29.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY27 to show significantly higher performance than Q1 and Q2 as H-Acid price gains flow into dye realisations with a one-to-two-quarter lag.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of at least 8-10% on consolidated dye revenue of INR 1,300-1,500 crore at peak; Q2 margin was about 3-4%.
H-Acid prices are expected to stabilise by calendar 2027 at levels above earlier prices; no visibility of China stabilisation before March 2027.
Demand for dyes and intermediates is expected to stay stable through 2H FY27.

Downstream copper facilities of about 2.6 lakh t are targeted for operation next fiscal year; smelter and fertiliser units are targeted for 2028-29. Post-start production guidance is 5 lakh t copper and 11 lakh t fertiliser.
Around 80% of copper concentrate and semi-finished requirements are said to be secured through LME-week supplier discussions.
capex_capacity: Makilala MCB project capex is about USD 280 million; Kiri's equity share is expected to be a little above USD 40 million, with the balance to come from strategic partner equity, domestic partner equity and debt (still under evaluation).
Intermediate capacity is operating below 60% because of raw material shortages, and management is working to raise utilisation for merchant sales.
India H-Acid capacity is about 60,000 t a year against domestic consumption of about 30,000-40,000 t a year.
Phase one of the integrated copper and fertiliser project is on track to start in 1H FY28; equipment deliveries have begun.
Acquired 40% in Makilala Mining Company Inc (Philippines) and incorporated Andamina SPA in Chile during the quarter.
demand_pricing: H-Acid prices have moved from about INR 400-500/kg to INR 1,600-1,800 over the last three to four weeks, per management, with China output below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t requirement due to continuous-nitration regulation.
Vinyl sulphone is above INR 450, but input costs (sulphur, aniline) have risen sharply, so spreads have not expanded proportionately.
Reactive dye prices are around INR 1,500-1,600, and dye prices follow intermediate prices with a two-to-three-month lag.
Over 50% of dye sales are exported; the company has a two-to-three-month running order book.
Dystar remains a major customer, and Lonsen Kiri is its single largest global supplier.
Copper cathodes: duty-free Japanese imports of about 200,000 t a year are insufficient, so other origins with duty are needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated EBITDA still weak despite the H-Acid price rise, and are Philippine legal costs a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal expenses in Q2 were under INR 3 crore and not the main reason. The lag comes from earlier fixed-price dye orders, with the price effect expected to show in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri appoint a CEO or CFO at Makilala to get operational control?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiri is a minority holder but sits on the board. A new management team was jointly appointed with the partner, including a CEO, Yulo Parese, formerly of Carmen Copper, and a new CFO, and Kiri has deputed staff through Carabao Corporation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H-Acid disruption in China last, and what is the cost structure of continuous nitration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China output is below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t need. Visibility is absent before March 2027, and prices may stabilise by calendar 2027 at levels above earlier prices. Continuous nitration adds capex, not operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri shift its strategy toward selling intermediates?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Dyes are the core business and about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively. Spot sales of intermediates are opportunistic and only occur after dye orders are met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and equity requirement for Makilala, and what is its production profile?
qa_highlights.answer: The MCB project capex is about USD 280 million, with Kiri's equity a little above USD 40 million. Makilala would produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, with about 100,000 t coming to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will copper price moves affect the project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the LME-minus-to-LME-plus spread is constant, and purchases and sales are hedged through a dedicated desk, so the exposure is operational rather than price-driven.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on H-Acid prices holding, and a China capacity restart could reverse the spread gains.
Standalone PAT is heavily affected by mark-to-market treasury losses (INR 57 crore in Q2).
Litigation: Celsius has appealed the arbitration awards linked to the Makilala stake.
Funding for the USD 280 million Makilala project is still being evaluated (equity versus debt split).
Preferential allotment at INR 475 per share is still in progress; a shareholder asked for a rights issue instead.
Dye prices are passed through with a two-to-three-month lag, so Q3 is only partially expected to reflect the H-Acid increase.
